title: Happy New Year (of the Snake!)
description:
Happy New Year, Here's where you can try the Year of the Snake, themed on 2025, by Adrian: https://sudokupad.app/qss44f03sx 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in ordinary killer cages sum to the given total and cannot repeat in a cage. Digits in golden cages multiply to the given total and can repeat in a cage. Digits on one of the main diagonals sum to 20. Digits on the other main diagonal sum to 25.
To celebrate the year of the snake, a snake is hiding in the puzzle. This snake can move horizontally, vertically and diagonally from digit to digit, but cannot cross itself or visit digits in any cages. The snake is 12 digits long and has both modular and entropic properties, ie. each set of 3 consecutive digits has one from {123}, one from {456} and one from {789}, also one from {147}, one from {258} and one from {369}.

title: Happy New Year Sudoku: It's a bit WROGN!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very HAPPY NEW YEAR to all our viewers! Thank you so much for enjoying these puzzles with us.

We have a very rare beast today in the form of a 2/5 difficulty WROGN sudoku. It's called Yin Yagn and it's by Timotab (and it's been recommended to us about 20 times!!).  Don't worry about the long rules - everything is pretty standard.  Just make sure you understand exactly what qualifies as a clue being wrong!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/de2dt3ohoq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply: Place the digits 1-9 in every row, column, and box, without repetition.
Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. 
A clue that is in cells that are all shaded or all unshaded is RIGHT. A clue that has at least one cell shaded and at least one cell unshaded is very, very WROGN. See below for exact definitions of WROGN clues. 
RIGHT Cages: Digits in cages must sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage.
RIGHT Kropki: Where digits are separated by a black dot, one must be double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.
RIGHT Renban: Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. 
RIGHT Nabner: No two digits on a gold line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits may not repeat on lines.
RIGHT Quadruples: Digits in a Quadruple circle must be placed at least once in the four cells touching that circle.
WROGN Cages: Digits in cages must not sum to the value in the top left corner of the cage.
WROGN Kropki: Where digits are separated by a black dot, neither is allowed to be double the other. 
WROGN Renban: No two digits on a purple line can be consecutive, regardless of their position on the line. Digits may not repeat on lines.(ie, WROGN renban lines are RIGHT nabner lines).
WROGN Nabner: Digits on a gold line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. (ie, WROGN nabner lines are RIGHT renban lines)
WROGN Quadruples: Digits in a Quadruple circle must not be placed at all in the four cells touching that circle.

The musical intro today is, of course, Happy New Year by Abba.

title: Like Shooting Fish in the Fog!
description:
Here's where you can try Drunken Fish by Russian Singer: https://sudokupad.app/rMGD6f9q8n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total in the leftmost cell in the top row. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. Cells that are a chess king's move apart cannot contain the same number. Adjacent digits along a green German whisper line differ by at least 5. Digits along thermometers strictly increase from the bulb end. The cell marked with a grey square contains an even digit. Cells with a circle contain an odd digit. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Red markings can be ignored. The grid is partially covered with fog. Placing correct digits will remove the surrounding fog.

title: The Sudoku Secret - Squared!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It is a testament to how good tonight's puzzle is that it ranks as one of our favourites of the whole year!  It's called The Secret Squared and it's by BenTen and, from start to finish, it's quite wonderful :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/hxxmopig9c

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each 3x3 box contains a circled digit which is equal to the multiplier of that box. The multiplier applies to all cells of the box it lies within. The value of each cell is equal to the digit placed in the cell multiplied by the multiplier of its box. The given cage total shows the sum of the values of all cells within the cage. Box borders divide the blue lines into segments whose values have the same sum. Different lines may have different sums.

title: Field Research Into Fog Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ChinStrap's puzzle, Field Research, combines dynamic fog-of-war sudoku with index lines (beloved, apparently, of computer programmers).  This puzzle deserves a LOT more plaudits - it's inventive and brilliant.  Don't miss this one!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/7n6wneuch2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. On an “index line”, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. For example: 3214 would be a valid line with the 3 on the diamond; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd digit is a 1, and so on. Inequality signs point to the smaller of the two digits. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by an X sum to 10. Not all such symbols are necessarily given.

A brand new type of puzzle this evening in the form of Grundriss by Myxo.  Apparently it's called Latin Square Jam and the idea is to fill the grid with square-shaped regions.  What we can say is that this is a fabulous idea that is a blast to solve.  Enjoy!

https://sudokupad.app/3dr1ufz01v

Divide the grid into square-shaped regions. Fill each region of size NxN with the numbers 1-N, such that no number repeats in any row or column of the region. title: The maths is easy - but the Vampires make this Hard!
description:
Here is where you can have a go at Nos482 by Starwarigami: https://sudokupad.app/zph1u3t3zq 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Within a cage, digits may not repeat, and the sum of their values is equal to the expression in the top left corner.
There are nine vampire cells and nine prey cells in the grid, one of each in every row, column and box. Every digit from 1-9 appears exactly once in a vampire cell, and exactly once in a prey cell. A vampire cell steals the value of the digit in the prey cell in the same box and adds it to its own digit to create its value. The value of the digit in a prey cell is 0.

title: The Cliffhanger Finale To Season 2: Sudoku Rat Run In The Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears shows us that, in sudoku, there's no such thing as the difficult second album by blowing our socks off again with the finale to Season 2 of his Rat Run series.  Finkz learnt English in the last episode and today, without revealing any spoilers, more incredible things happen to her in the fog.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/mpi5qhto7n?setting-foganim=1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT:
Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick walls. (The walls have been decorated with red tinsel.)
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so.
DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct digits may clear fog somewhere in the maze.
CHRISTMAS LIGHTS: An orange Christmas light indicates that any digits visited by Finkz in its row or column are odd. A blue Christmas light indicates that any digits visited in its row or column are even.
TELEPORTS: Every teleport is part of a matching pair. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits.
BLACKCURRANTS: Blackcurrants sit between two digits with a 1:2 ratio.
BAUBLES: The number on a gold bauble gives the total of any cells it touches.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, any two cells that are adjacent along the path contain consecutive digits (except when separated by teleportation, where the digits are identical.)

title: A New Twist On Fog Sudoku For Boxing Day
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
If you'd like a late Christmas present then here it is!  A new rule for fog sudoku from Nurator in a sudoku called Hit, Reveal, Solve!  This has some lovely ideas in it and is only 2/5 on the difficulty scale - well worth some post-mince-pie puzzle time :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/99c09jh573

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells. Guessing is not required. A cell with an arrow contains the sum of all cells where the digit in a cell (in the direction of the arrow) equals the distance from that arrow clue. If multiple arrows are in one cell, the sum total of all such digits in those directions is used. E.g. if the digit in Row1, Column7 is a 2, it would contribute to the sum in Row3, Column7 while every other digit in that cell would not.

description:
Here's where you can attempt Music Sudoku: Joy To The World by BoaConstructor: https://sudokupad.app/grtlxdmkas 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the attached circle. The green boxes (box 1 and 6) are magic squares. title: The Sudoku Rat Learns Words In The Fog!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears has outdone himself this time by taking the sudoku rat, Finkz, into the fog and requiring her to learn words!! (?)  What an astonishing puzzle for Simon to attempt after his short holiday last week - an absolute joy from start to finish.  (And it's the season 2 finale next week!!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/oj8y6yrx16?setting-foganim=1&setting-toolletter=1

Please be aware that you will need to play this puzzle on your computer as, on mobile devices, entering letters after I in the alphabet is not possible as yet in the software.

Rules:
In this experiment, nine letters of the alphabet (to be determined) must be used to fill the grid so that no letter repeats in any row, column or 3x3 box.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
DYNAMIC FOG: Entering correct letters may clear fog somewhere in the maze. No guessing is necessary.
CUE CARDS: Each pink cue card sits between two letters that both appear on that cue card.
BRAINWAVE MONITORS: The faint light of 11 blue monitors are visible through the fog; Finkz must visit all of these before reaching the cupcake. With any luck, they will provide an insight into her thoughts.
TEST CONSTRAINT: 3x3 box borders divide Finkz' path into segments. If a segment contains more than one cell, then the cells must be visited in alphabetical order.

title: Peas Be With You ...
description:
Erbsenzähler by Sujoyku and SamuPiano: https://sudokupad.app/z14kvlwqlh 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3. 
A circled digit indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Note: This also includes all circles which are bounding the split pea lines. If, for example, a 3 appears in a circle, then there must be exactly 3 circles that contain a 3.

title: The Balancing Act: Sudoku Genius From 2 Big Brains!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had so many recommendations to try this collaboration between AnalyticalNinja and palpot called Balancing Act. It's got an innovative ruleset which makes for a fascinating solve!!  [Simon should be back "live" tomorrow - he has been on a short holiday, which is why the videos have been pre-recorded (other than yesterday's crossword video).  He appreciates your patience (especially those who have had to wait for their birthday announcements!).]

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/atfgvx1pgc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Along a line, any changes in shading divide that line into segments of fully shaded or fully unshaded cells. On each line, each such segment (shaded or unshaded) must have the same sum as all other segments. Within the shaded areas, adjacent digits along the lines must differ by at least 5. Within unshaded areas, any string of 3 or fewer digits along the lines must be from a different set of (147), (258) and (369).

title: This Sudoku Must Be An April Fools???
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The sheer panache evident in the setting of this puzzle is clear the moment you see it.  Every clue is a zero!!!  It's called double negative and it's the work of arctan and, although it's only a 6x6, it takes some thinking to crack this one.  Absolutely bonkers.  And absolutely BRILLIANT! 

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/k6k9bgnqht

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and must sum up to zero. Digits on the indicated diagonals also sum up to zero, but may repeat if allowed by other rules. Divide the grid into two orthogonally connected regions, such that no 2x2 area is entirely one region or the other. In one region, every digit counts as twice its value for the purposes of cages and diagonals. In the other region, every digit counts as the negative of its value for the purposes of cages and diagonals. [For example, a two-cell cage that adds up to zero could be fulfilled by a doubled 1 (which counts as 2) and a negated 2 (which counts as -2).]

A really outstandingly good sudoku tonight from Chris Napolitano called ± Information.  It's one of the best uses of the "negative constraint" we ever seen and makes for a simply fascinating solve.

title: The Sudoku With The Perfect Rating
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tacosian is a new name to us but this puzzle should put Tacosian on every sudoku lover's radar, it's that good. It's called Galactic Union and it's earned the "perfect" rating of 100% and 5* on Logic Masters Germany.  

(We will hopefully return to the Saturday Pencil Puzzle Series next weekend.)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/wxkk82qye4

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. One region border is given between R4C7 and R5C7. The dots in the grid are the centres of 180 degrees rotationally symmetric "galaxies" (non-overlapping sets of orthogonally connected cells). Each half of a galaxy forms a killer cage, summing to the number given on its side of the dot. All cells within a cage must belong to the same region. The two cages formed by a single galaxy must belong to different regions.

title: The Most Popular Sudoku Series Ever Returns!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The exciting mounts as we move towards the end of Season 2 of the most popular sudoku series of all time: Marty Sears' Rat Run - which has reached episode 18.  The great thing is that, just like the first 17, it's another genius puzzle - this one themed around "mirror digits"... what are those I hear you ask?  :) 

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/hypzc2xwbi

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits.
MIRROR CELLS: Each row, column and box contains exactly one mirror cell. Mirror cells may not contain teleports. The value of a mirror cell equals the digit in that cell subtracted from 10. Eg: a 2 in a mirror cell is 'mirrored' on the 1-9 scale, and has a value of 8. Every mirror cell contains a different digit. 
ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the values of any two physically adjacent cells along the path (ie; not separated by teleportation) must have a difference of at least 5.

description:
Here's where you can play Squeeze Play by Darth Paradox: https://sudokupad.app/sn2nojv4os?setting-nogrid=1

title: A Phistomefel-ian Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir is a maths professor by day but a sudoku wizard at night.  He's managed to construct a quite ridiculous miracle sudoku using some ideas from recent Phistomefel puzzles.  It is hard to overstate how beautifully this solves nor how other-worldly Dorlir's mind must be to come up with this stuff!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ksn2ld67um

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. A border square is a 2x2 square that crosses at least one 3x3 box border. For all border squares exactly 2 digits are the same. The middle 3x3 box in the grid is a magic square i.e. the sum of digits in each row, column and main 3-cell diagonal in that box is N (where N must be determined by the solver). There are exactly N ‘friendly’ cells in the grid. A cell is friendly if its digit is equal to at least one of its row number, column number or box number. (Rows are numbered top to bottom; columns are numbered left-to-right; boxes are numbered in normal reading order.) Digits separated by a black dot must be in ratio 1:2 (ie one digit is double the other). Not all dots are necessarily given.

title: This Fog Sudoku Is Utterly MAD
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This sudoku is called We're All Mad Here and it is certainly an apt description of the neurons in gdc's brain!  The basic idea here is that the grid can be folded such that the middle 5 columns disappear and yet the existing clues still need to work within the leftover 4x9 grid. This dynamic Fog puzzle will make you doubt your own sanity when solving but the revelations are so magnificent that the payoff is absolutely worthwhile!!  Please do watch the video introduction if you are unsure about the rules.  

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/oaeuopmvrt

Explanatory example:
https://sudokupad.app/a5fksb2o7y

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells. The vertical dashed lines are folded onto each other so that columns 1, 2, 8 and 9 form a secondary grid (as if the other columns disappear). In this grid all clues are still valid. Digits in a cage don't repeat and sum to the total given in the top-left corner. Cages don't overlap. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Clues outside the grid give the sum of all cells that contain a digit equal to the distance of that cell from that clue in the row or column. For example, a 4 in Row 2, Column 4 would count towards the 10 clue in row 2, and any other number would not. Horizontal distances in the folded 4x9 grid are limited to 1-4.
If you are unsure about the rules please watch the video introduction and, in particular, check out this link which explains the idea very well:
https://sudokupad.app/a5fksb2o7y

title: The Ring Of Logic: Kyklos
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One comment on Logic Masters Germany says "Incredibly beautiful puzzle! I do not understand the 88% rating, for me it is 110%". The rating at the time of recording has gone up to 93% but, for Simon, this is a 100% puzzle.  It's called Kyklos, it's by Shintaro Fushida-Hardy and it's absolutely brilliant.

(And another comment on LMG says it is "fun and easy"... we'd agree with the first adjective but the second is a bit of a push!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/yvxj355qfi

Rules:
The grid consists of three types of cells: 'clue cells' (brown), 'shaded cells' (dark grey), and 'loop cells'. You will use the clue cells to determine shaded cells (which can touch each other), and draw a loop through all remaining cells. The loop travels orthogonally through the centres of cells and may not branch or cross itself. Two shaded cells are given. Place the digits 0 to 8 in the nine brown clue cells with no repeats ie the brown cells must contain one of each of the digits 0,1,2…7,8. Each digit counts two things: first, it is the number of shaded cells in the eight neighbouring cells. Second, it is the total number of shaded cells in all indicated directions. (This count is not obstructed by any other cell-types.) For clarity, clue cells are not considered shaded, and cannot be shaded.

For answer-check, place a 0 in all shaded cells and a 9 in all loop cells.

This page gives an example puzzle:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000KCF

title: The Unexpected Crossover: Sudoku & Word Search
description:
Word Search by Itai Cohen: https://sudokupad.app/PHBrnqT7QJ 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers are alpha numeric (1=a, 2=b, 3=c…. FOR ANSWER CHECK TO WORK, YOU MUST USE NUMBERS IN THE GRID, unlike Mark). 
Any vowel cannot be a chess knight’s move away from an identical letter. The green 3-cell lines form a 3-letter word from the list: ACE, AGE, AID, BAG, BEG, DIE, DIG, FED, FIG, HAD, ICE, BID, BAD. Each word occurs exactly once along a line, though it may occur again outside of a line. The gray cell contains a larger digit than each orthogonal neighbour.

title: Rat Run 17: Sudoku Perfection Continues!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Friday's always been a great day of the week but, of late, we've been able to solve the latest Rat Run sudoku from Marty Sears on Fridays too - what could be better!  The latest (no.17) is called Trapdoors and introduces some unusual 'buttons' into the maze :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/h46kngm99n

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Each rectangular trapdoor has a different total (the sum of its two digits.) Finkz should not step on a trapdoor without first locking it shut, making it safe to cross. To make it safe to step on a trapdoor, Finkz must first press all the circular buttons that match the colour of the trapdoor. A digit on a coloured button indicates how many buttons of that colour contain that digit. In this experiment, the correct path will be entropic, ie; every group of 3 adjacent cells along the path must contain one low digit (1, 2 or 3), one medium digit (4, 5 or 6) and one high digit (7, 8 or 9).

title: Sudoku Man Shares His Secrets
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A VERY classy sudoku tonight from ChinStrap which combines two rules in a natural and rather lovely way.  The puzzle is called Assigned Seating and comes recommended by some of the most famous names in sudoku.  We loved it (and it's not TOO difficult, especially if you listen to the secrets Simon shares at the start of the solve!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/unrk3m4tg3

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Colour every cell in the grid light or dark. Cells of the same colour are orthogonally connected. Every 2x2 contains both colours. On an “index” line, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 3214 would be a valid line with 3 as the diamond; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd cell contains a 1, the 2nd cell a 2, and so on. All cells that reference their own position on a line (the digit N is in position N) should be dark. Cells that are not “self-referencing” should be light. Eg for the line 3214 with 3 as the diamond, the 2 and 4 would be dark and the 1 and 3 would be light. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive and have the same colour. Not all such dots are necessarily given.

title: Queens (on LinkedIn): How To Solve It
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Apparently 100,000 people every day are playing the new Queens game on LinkedIn!  It's a puzzle created by Cracking The Cryptic's old friend Thomas Snyder (3x World Sudoku Champion, 1x World Puzzle Champion) and very enjoyable it is too!

It's based off the logic puzzle Starbattle but where only one queen (star) needs to be placed into every row, column and region. The puzzles get harder through the week (with Monday being the easiest and Sunday the hardest).... so yesterday Simon thought he'd show you some of the strategies he uses vs the hardest puzzles.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://www.linkedin.com/games/queens

The exact puzzle Simon plays in the video is no longer available on LinkedIn but you can play it in our software at the following link:
https://sudokupad.app/tlr3i291g8
(Use 1 for a Queen and 2 for an empty cell to make the solution check function work)

Rules:
Place exactly one queen in every row, column and coloured region. Two queens  cannot touch each other. Not even diagonally.

title: This Is One Of The Best Sudoku Puzzles Of 2024
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is one of those sudokus that teaches you things you already know. We all know how to add numbers together and yet there is something so fundamental and clever about the way that logic is presented by yttrio here that it feels new.  The puzzle is called One Look Could Kill and it's absolutely one of the best we've seen this year.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/pmv1jze5n3

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits MAY repeat in cages if allowed by other rules.  The sum of digits in each cage must be a two-digit number that acts as a valid “look-and-say clue” for that cage.  Eg if the sum is 21, there must be exactly two 1s in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 21). Eg2 if the sum is 17, there must be exactly one 7 in the cage along with any combination of other digits (such that, overall, the digits in the cage sum to 17).

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
On Saturdays we've taken to trying a non-sudoku puzzle and we continue that theme tonight by looking at Skeptical Mario's A Fistful Of Circles - a gorgeous hybrid of fillomino and "circle" logic.  

Don't be fooled into thinking this is incredibly easy - we thought it was VERY clever indeed!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/51pjq2i21m

Rules:
Divide the grid into non-overlapping regions. Regions can be any size (including one cell) but the cells in a region must be orthogonally connected with one another. Every cell should contain a number equal to the number of cells in its region. Regions of the same size cannot share an edge. A number in a circle indicates how many circles contain that number. (There are 41 circles in all.)\\nNote for solution checking: for regions larger than 9 cells, enter the units digit of the region size. Leave the cells with the given 15 and 26 clues empty.

title: Schrödinger's "Rat": Sudoku Perfection (And Comedy!)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The next Rat Run sudoku (no. 16) is up on deck today:  Schrödinger's Rat by the extraordinary Marty Sears.  This is the most popular series in the history of sudoku and it hard to overstate just how wonderful this collection of puzzles is.  Every single one has been great but this might be the most jaw-dropping of all - Simon is almost crying at one point.  Unmissable.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/fi311m5b4u

Rules:
SCHRODINGER CELLS:
Fill each row, column and box with the digits 0-9 once each. To make this possible, each row, column and box contains one Schrödinger cell, which contains two digits. The value of a Schrödinger cell is equal to the sum of its two digits.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
BLACKCURRANTS: Two values separated by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio.
ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow in the direction it is pointing. A purple arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into segments that each contain at least 2 cells. The values of two adjacent cells within the same segment always have the same difference, and this difference is unique for every segment. Eg: if a segment has a sequence of values 1, 3, 5, 7, then its 'same difference' is 2, and so no other segment may have a 'same difference' of 2.

The MATH+ Advent Calendar mentioned during the introduction is available here:
https://www.mathekalender.de/wp/

title: The Sudoku That Tells You Where To Place Digits!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Thanksgiving! We're celebrating with Crusader175's sudoku, Tilted - a fascinating puzzle which actually gives you the positions of seven of the digits in the grid...  sort of ;)

Anyway, it's interesting and brilliant and allows us to give some thanks to all those of you who enjoy these wonderful puzzles with us.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/m35yptjo24

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits X, Y and Z in pill shapes (reading left to right) signify that rXcY = Z. Eg, if a pill read [825], then the cell in row 8 column 2 would have to be the digit 5. Digits along the negative diagonal (thin blue line) must not repeat. Any set of three sequential cells along the thick teal line must contain one digit from [1,4,7], one digit from [2,5,8] and one digit from [3,6,9]. Cells separated by an X sum to 10. Not all Xs are given.

title: This New Fog Sudoku Is EPIC
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Last week we showcased a new type of Fog sudoku by James Sinclair in which the fog clears "dynamically".  Unsurprisingly constructors are starting to make use of this idea and who better to showcase what it can do than gdc!  This one is called Dynamic Chaos - it is 3/5 for difficulty and wonderful from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://beta.sudokupad.app/xgn9g0d94r

Rules:
Divide the grid into nine non-overlapping regions each consisting of nine orthogonally connected cells. Place the digits 1-9 once in each row, column, and region. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit in a cell lifts fog in that cell and possibly other cells; revealing new clues. Some cells contain a grey square inside them. The digit in such a cell is equal to the sum of the (up to 8) surrounding digits that are in different regions. Digits separated by a white dot differ by 1 and belong to the same region. A digit N on an arrow counts how many cells it sees of its region in the indicated direction, including itself. Region borders block vision. Additionally, the digit N+1 must appear immediately behind the first seen region border. Each arrow MUST therefore see a region border within the grid.

title: The Sudoku You Cannot Use Sudoku To Solve!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It has not been often, if at all, that in the history of the channel we've attempted a sudoku variant with so many given digits!  The puzzle is called This One Goes To 11 by Super Mikal and it's an extremely unusual sudoku - at least partly because sudoku is positively misleading if you try to do it in the wrong way!!  Mad and brilliant would be two accurate adjectives for this one!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/jan0hcmke0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules sort of apply, except this one goes to 11: Fill in the cells with the numbers 0 through 11 (where 10 and 11 are represented by A and B respectively) such that each row, column and box contains 9 different numbers. Additionally, each valid set of numbers can only be used in at most one row, one column and one box (ie each row must be different from every other row but could repeat a column or box; and likewise for every column and every box). The classic set of the numbers 1 through 9 is not allowed due to being deemed bogus, lame, square etc. However, every row, column and box must still pay homage to The Secret of these numbers (ie they must add up to 45). The grey cells are just extra space for taking notes. Bonus task: Can you guess how many valid sets of 9 numbers there are, given these rules?

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in this puzzle is either a Renban Line or a Nabner Line. The solver must determine which is which. description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Last Saturday we took a brief hiatus from doing non-sudoku puzzles on Saturdays in order to celebrate the 80th birthday of Aad van de Wetering.  This Saturday, pencil puzzles return with a bang as Simon tackles Math Pesto's incredible Modular Fillomino!  This is a very long video but we really have to commend Math Pesto on the sheer variety of logic included in this puzzle.  It is, quite honestly, fantastic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/polbu9hw3d?setting-conflictchecker=0

Rules:
Fillomino: Divide the grid into polyominoes so that polyominoes of the same size don't share an edge. Each cell contains a number equal to its polyomino's size. Draw a loop that moves orthogonally from one cell to another through the grid. The loop must not touch itself orthogonally; however, it can touch diagonally. Along the loop, any three consecutive cells must contain numbers congruent to 0 mod 3, 1 mod 3, and 2 mod 3. (In other words, one of the numbers is from the set {3, 6, 9, 12, …}, one is from {1, 4, 7, 10, …}, and one from {2, 5, 8, 11, …}. Numbers on cells with arrows refer to the total amount of loop cells seen in the indicated direction or, if more than one arrow, in the directions combined.

title: Do Rodents Dream Of Sudoku Sleep?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's Friday so, of late, we've been able to enjoy the latest Rat Run puzzle from Marty Sears.  We're now up to episode 15, Connectedness, and it's another absolute doozy.  It's also one of the most colourful sudokus we've seen. This we approve of :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/athyahqib1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall. If digits are connected by a blackcurrant one digit will be double the other. Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. Finkz' path is formed of one or more segments. Any uses of teleports will divide Finkz' path up into physically separate segments, ie; if a teleport is used, the current path segment ends at the entry teleport, and a new separate path segment begins at the matching exit teleport. Any path segment must function as a “renban” ie it must consist entirely of a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits, which can be arranged in any order along the path segment.

title: Announcing A BREAKTHROUGH In Fog Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have never had a sudoku recommended so often and so quickly as this puzzle, Fog Of Where? by James Sinclair.  It uses a completely new fog mechanic in which placing correct digits may or may not clear fog and any fog cleared might be elsewhere in the grid!!  It will, we predict, revolutionise sudoku setting for a while as constructors go crazy!!  It is rated 1/5 for difficulty and has been solved a quite incredible number of times in the last day!  Not to be missed.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://alpha.sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/fog-of-where

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. *Some* correctly-entered digits clear fog from certain cells, but those cells may be in other parts of the grid. Other digits, even when entered correctly, do not clear fog at all. When the puzzle is fully solved, all the fog will be cleared. Digits in a cage sum to the small clue in the cage's top left corner, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle (and these digits can repeat if allowed by other rules). Arrows do not cross or overlap, and all arrow sums are single-digit. Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. If digits are separated by a black dot, one is double the other.

Thanks to Sven for creating the software allowing this innovation to work (his sudokupad software is linked below.)

You can find more of James' puzzles at artisanalsudoku.com.

Simon has also solved James' recent puzzle, Thank You Very Much, on Patreon today.  Link below.

title: Outfoxing The Sudoku Trolls!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Many constuctors have alerted us over the last year or two to some "strange" ratings being awarded to puzzles on the public forums by certain solvers.  We're fortunate that we get recommended dozens of puzzles every day and so, even if a sudoku doesn't have the highest rating, we may still be able to tell that it is a beauty.  ChinStrap's debut on the channel this evening is one such example:  it's been downgraded but, having solved it, we have zero clue why - it's lovely.  And Marty Sears recommended to us too!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/mwpu102gkm

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. On an “index line”, the digit in the Nth cell along the line (starting from the diamond) indicates the position along the line where the digit N appears. Eg: 3214 would be a valid line; the 1st digit, 3, indicates that the 3rd cell contains a 1, the 2nd cell a 2, and so on.

title: Find Harmony In Fog Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The master of all things Fog-related, gdc, returns to the channel tonight with Double Scaled Harmony - a beautiful mixture of arrows, yin yang and, of course, fog!  Be prepared for some very surprising things as you explore this grid!!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/qn9k75pdfy

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. No guessing is required. Shade some cell such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected and each 2x2 area contains shaded and unshaded cells. The value of an unshaded cell is its digit. The value of a shaded cell is double its digit. Values along an arrow sum to the value of the attached circle. Arrows don't overlap.

title: The Sudoku With Only One Given Digit (The 80th Birthday Of Aad van de Wetering)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today is the 80th birthday of Aad van de Wetering, the incredible Dutch sudoku constructor whose puzzles have featured in many of our most popular videos.  We are absolutely delighted therefore to be able to share this 80-themed sudoku with you by the great man himself. We're hoping some viewers might like to leave a comment tonight about their history with Aad's puzzles so this wonderful community can make his day even more memorable.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/4hca9hq4bd

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each separate grey line (lengths: 3, 5 or 7) the product of the digits is 80. Each cage contains a 2-digit prime number (read left-to-right). A+B = C+D = A+C = B+D = 80

description:

Brand new incredible Fog Sudoku puzzles by the likes of Phistomefel, Marty Sears, James Sinclair, Qodec, Dorlir, ThePedallingPianist, Sandra&Nala, Peter Veenis, Mr Menace, Florian Wortmann, Math Pesto & HalfBakedLunatic.

Thank God It's Finkz-Day on the channel as we attempt the new Rat Run sudoku from Marty Sears!  We're up to episode 14 in the best sudoku series of all time and it is hard to believe just how consistently high the quality of these puzzles remains. Unmissable.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/vcncpwgckm

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio. All cages have the same total, to be deduced. An electricity symbol indicates the cage's ‘shock value’. Finkz may not enter any cage with a shock value of 5 or higher. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. In this experiment, dotted 3x3 box borders divide the correct path into segments. The total of each segment must be higher than the total of the previous segment on Finkz' path.

title: The Original Sudoku Sin
description:
*** NEW FOG APP IS OUT ON STEAM & ANDROID ***
Brand new incredible Fog Sudoku puzzles by the likes of Phistomefel, Marty Sears, James Sinclair, Qodec, Dorlir, ThePedallingPianist, Sandra&Nala, Peter Veenis, Mr Menace, Florian Wortmann, Math Pesto & HalfBakedLunatic. 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3165770/Cracking_the_Cryptic__Fog_of_War_1/

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We attempt one of the most well-regarded sudokus of recent times tonight in the form of Nordy's Original Sin.  It's just a gorgeous puzzle with an interesting (but very understandable!) ruleset and some lovely logic.  Well worth your precious puzzling time.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/zaputh99gx

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Each snake-circle contains a different digit and is the end of a snake that moves orthogonally through the grid. Snakes cannot touch themselves or each other orthogonally, but they may touch themselves and each other diagonally. The digit in the snake-circle is the length of that snake. Orthogonally-connected groups of non-snake cells are called "gardens." Digits cannot repeat on a snake or in a garden. A small number clue in the top-left corner of a cell gives the sum of the digits in the snake or garden that contains that clue. (You can think of snakes and gardens as Killer Cages, where some of the sums have been given). 
Digits joined by a red apple cannot contain a 5; cannot both be low (1234); cannot both be high (6789); cannot both be even (2468); and cannot both be odd (1379)

(The musical intro today is, of course, the opening bars of Superman by John Williams.)

title: The Sudoku With Only 4 3x3 Boxes
description:
*** NEW FOG APP IS OUT ON STEAM & ANDROID ***
Brand new incredible Fog Sudoku puzzles by the likes of Phistomefel, Marty Sears, James Sinclair, Qodec, Dorlir, ThePedallingPianist, Sandra&Nala, Peter Veenis, Mr Menace, Florian Wortmann, Math Pesto & HalfBakedLunatic. 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3165770/Cracking_the_Cryptic__Fog_of_War_1/

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Someone who has given the puzzle world a great deal of pleasure is Dorlir - the maths professor.  He has made tonight's sudoku to celebrate the first birthday of his son Rubin and we can think of no better puzzle to attempt today!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/r2zxe5nquo

Rules:
Draw four 3x3 boxes in the grid that don't overlap, and fill them with the digits 1-9. Digits can't repeat in a row, column or 3x3 box. Cells that are not in any box are empty, and their value is 0. Digits can't repeat in a cage, and sum to the clue given in the top-leftmost cell of that cage. Draw four snakes, each existing completely inside one of the 3x3 boxes. Each snake is a one cell wide path that only moves orthogonally, and must pass through every cell of its box. Adjacent digits along a snake sum to 10 or 11.

description:
*** NEW FOG APP IS OUT ON STEAM & ANDROID ***
Brand new incredible Fog Sudoku puzzles by the likes of Phistomefel, Marty Sears, James Sinclair, Qodec, Dorlir, ThePedallingPianist, Sandra&Nala, Peter Veenis, Mr Menace, Florian Wortmann, Math Pesto & HalfBakedLunatic. 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3165770/Cracking_the_Cryptic__Fog_of_War_1/

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Well this has made us feel a bit silly. Simon read the rules to this one early this afternoon and was worried they might be a bit too much for newcomers to pencil puzzles (which our Saturday series is aimed at). One of our testers (thank you E.!) insisted we needed to try this one... and she was absolutely right - it's absolutely epic.  It's called Twilight Cave Fillomino and it's by Agent.  If you do find the rules complicated check out the example grid in the video introduction - it helped Simon understand what's going on.  

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/p636wzk7e0

Rules:
Fillomino: Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions such that no two regions of the same size share an edge, and enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region. 
Cave: Shade some cells in the grid such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all shaded cells are orthogonally connected by other shaded cells to an edge of the grid. 
Each region must either be entirely shaded or entirely unshaded. If a clued cell is unshaded, the clue indicates the sum of numbers seen orthogonally from that cell; region borders block vision. If a clued cell is shaded, the clue indicates the total sum of numbers in its group of orthogonally connected shaded cells (which could include more than one region).

title: The Rat Returns.  And Loves The Number 13...!!?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the great treats being afforded to us puzzlers at the moment is the time we get to spend each week in the company of Finkz The Rat as she battles through one of Marty Sears' mazes.  This is the best sudoku series of all time and Triskaidekaphilia - the 13th puzzle - is another gem (and WHAT a remarkable grid!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/zsk8n4tjvw

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
NULLIFIERS: In each row, column and 3x3 box there is one 'nullifier' cell to be located. The value of a nullifier cell is zero. Each nullifier cell contains a different digit.
MOTION SENSORS: The value on a pink motion sensor indicates how many of the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor are visited by Finkz. The sensor itself is counted, if visited.
BLACKCURRANTS: Values connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio.
GRAPES: Values connected by a green grape have a difference of at least 5.
FORBIDDEN DOORS: Values connected by a red X sum to 10. Finkz may not pass directly through a red X.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, if a row / column / box is visited by Finkz, then the values of ALL the visited cells in that row / column / box must sum to exactly 13 (even if the cells aren't all adjacent on the path.)

title: A Brilliant Way To Teach A New Sudoku Rule
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A fantastic new rule tonight from Xenonetix in a puzzle called Cradle.  The use of consecutive digit totals outside the grid leads to some fascinating interactions with the zipper lines.  This one was recommended to us by Dorlir, a maths professor, and it really makes you think about the basic principles of arithmetic!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/z7eug3yrqd

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits an equal distance from the centre of a purple line must sum to the digit in the centre of that purple line. description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
[A reminder we're streaming tonight at 10pm UK time - link below.]
Simon realised he hadn't done a zetamath puzzle in too long and decided to put that right!  Here he attempts Alarm - which turns out to be every bit as clever as we've come to expect from one of the World's leading constructors.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/nivm1qdkzj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each thick grey line can be divided into one or more non-overlapping segments. Each segment contains digits that sum to 10. Eg 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits. These digits can appear in any order. Digits along a thin grey line connecting two circles must have values between the digits in the circles. Eg if the two circles at a line’s ends contain 3 and 8 then digits on the line itself must be selected from [4567]. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one digit is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.

description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION RELEASED TODAY ***
November's sudoku hunt competition launched yesterday!  It's Duality II by the Sudoku Skunkworks.  It really is a fantastic collection of puzzles and we've decided to have a different type of prize.  The winner (drawn after the closing date of 20 November) will be invited (NOT required) to solve a sudoku with Simon...

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Shintaro Fushida-Hardy came to our attention via Reddit recommendations and every puzzle of Shintaro's we've tried since has been so exceptionally good.  Today is non-sudoku day on the channel so we attempt Habitat 67, a variant involving Dutch flatmates (!)  And it's an absolute cracker!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/581lub7qrf

Rules:
Subdivide the grid into orthogonally connected regions such that regions of the same size do not share a border. The value of each cell in the grid is equal to its region size. Each "?" represents a digit from 1 to 9 which must be deduced. Dutch flat mates: every cell with value 5 either has a value-1 cell above it, or a value-9 cell below it (or both). Mod-3 groups: all cells with values which are equal modulo 3 form a single orthogonally connected group. This means every cell in the grid belongs to one of three orthogonally connected groups. (I recommend shading cells to keep track of groups.) For answer-check, replace 2-digit numbers with "0", and check that no digits have been rendered above clues.

title: Rat Run 12: More Sudoku Magic From Marty Sears
description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT COMPETITION RELEASED TODAY ***
November's sudoku hunt competition launched this afternoon!  It's Duality II by the Sudoku Skunkworks.  It really is a fantastic collection of puzzles and we've decided to have a different type of prize.  The winner (drawn after the closing date of 20 November) will be invited (NOT required) to solve a sudoku with Simon...

Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Is there a better way to celebrate a Friday than with a new Rat Run sudoku by Marty Sears?  This is the 12th in the series (and the 2nd in Season 2) and it's every bit as magical as those puzzles that have gone before. Weird, wonderful and Finkz-tastic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/wxhrpva2lr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Digits separated by a green grape have a difference of at least 5. In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into 'index lines'; In any box, the Nth cell visited by Finkz is called 'position N'. (So, for example, in box 7, r9c2 is position 1.) The digit in position N always indicates which position along that segment contains the digit N. Eg: In a box, Finkz might visit the digits 35142 in that order. The first digit being a 3 indicates that the third digit is a 1, the second digit being a 5 indicates that the fifth digit is a 2, and so on.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy Halloween!  We thought we'd celebrate by attempting a sequel in fjam's Graveyard series.  These sudokus are not easy but they are extremely interesting - especially when the dates on the graves are always wrong ("knapp daneben").

title: Creatures In The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In the run-up to Halloween, it seems appropriate to do something scary!  So we're trying Creatures In The Fog by Br1312te (whose debut it is on the channel).  There's some very nice logic in this one and remember not to guess if you don't want to upset the monster under your bed!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/3f7o01c1ws

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply, but strange things are afoot.. Creatures of the night have invaded the land! Each row, column and box contains one creature, marked by a coloured dot. All creatures are marked. Cells containing a creature ‘index’ either the row, column or 3x3 box number (read in normal reading order) they're placed in. Each number assigned to a creature is unique and can't be repeated. Marked by a green dot, zombies have an infectious bite ie orthogonally adjacent cells are even when the zombie's number is even, or odd when the zombie's number is odd. Marked by a grey dot, poltergeists throw everything into disarray ie orthogonally adjacent cells are either all higher than the poltergeist's number, or all lower. Marked by an orange dot, horsemen have a knight's reach ie Cells a chess-knight's move away from the horseman can't contain the same digit as the horseman's number. Marked by a red dot, vampires suck the power from their victims ie Orthogonally adjacent cells sum up to the vampire's number. The land is covered in fog. Placing correct digits will lift the fog. No guessing is required. The monster under your bed will know if you cheat!


This video is the chess genius that Simon mentioned in the introduction:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XAlcDWQ6iTM

title: Opening A Sudoku Live On Camera...
description:
[Please note that, in response to questions in the video's comments, attempted to clarify the rules further.  We hope this enhances the enjoyment of a wonderful puzzle.]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ever since The Miracle Sudoku, Simon has occasionally opened puzzles live on camera and today is one of those days!  What's revealed is one of the most terrifying rulesets you'll ever see (unless you're a decent physicist)!  Lorentz factors and their role in Special Relativity play a part in Tobias Brixner's bonkers and brilliant excursion into the theoretical universe.  Mad. And. Magnificent.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/qhib25buqr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage marks a spaceship that is initially at rest in the solver's reference frame, i.e., the grid. Digits may repeat within a spaceship if allowed by other rules. Each spaceship then accelerates to a high velocity and moves in an orthogonal direction without changing its orientation. The solver must find its new position that is fully inside the grid. Spaceships initial/final positions do not overlap with either their own or other spaceships initial/final positions. Neither may spaceships pass through the initial/final positions of other spaceships. As a consequence of the special theory of relativity, each moving spaceship is contracted along its direction of motion, i.e., its shape is scaled down in the solver’s reference frame. The length of the spaceship at rest DIVIDED BY the observed length of the spaceship in motion is called Lorentz factor. The size is unchanged perpendicular to the direction of motion. The energy of a spaceship is given by the sum of its digits. The energy of a spaceship in motion is equal to its energy at rest MULTIPLIED BY the Lorentz factor. Cells connected by an X sum to 10.

description:
Here's where you can attempt German Indeuxers by Donatello_86: https://sudokupad.app/420917reil  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by an "X" sum to ten. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits do not repeat in a cage, and sum to the number given. Digits on an arrow sum to the attached circle. Neighbouring digits along a green line have a difference of at least five.

Position one of a green line starts at the attached green circle and the position increases along the line, eg. line "A", starting from position 1 has a sequence of 6, 1, 8, 2, 7, meaning line "B", starting from position 1 has a sequence of 4, 9, 2, 8, 3.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We continue our Saturday series of non-sudoku puzzles with a gem from Dumediat and Piatato called Allegory.  It's a mix of Masyu and Cave with some very surprising results.  Moreover it's achieved the rare distinction of a perfect rating despite not being too difficult.  Do have a go at this one if you can!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/x5qynmcg31

Rules:
Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of some cells that passes through every circle and moves orthogonally between cells (ie never diagonally). The loop must turn on black circles and travel straight through the cells on either side. The loop must go straight through white circles, and turn in at least one of the cells on either side. All orthogonally connected groups of non-loop cells must be connected to the edge of the grid. 
For the solution check function to work, enter a 1 into every non-loop cell and 2 into every cell in which the loop turns.

title: Desert Island Sudoku
description:
Here is the place to try Unique Islands Of Nine by Scruffamudda: https://tinyurl.com/bdctjfbj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into an ocean and islands of one or more orthogonally connected cells such that each island contains a set of digits summing to 9. Digits may repeat on an island but each island must contain a unique set of digits.
Islands must not touch each other (even diagonally) except at cells joined by a line, each line marks a bridge between two islands.
All cells not part of an island are in the ocean which must be a contiguous region of orthogonally connected cells that never completely fills a 2x2 area.
A digit in a circle counts the number of cells in its own region (island or ocean) seen in its row and column combined, including itself, where cells in other regions block vision and are not seen.

title: Season 2:  Rat Run Sudoku returns!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It would have been hard to believe a few years ago that a series of sudoku puzzles would warrant a second season and that it would be so anticipated... and yet here we are!  Marty Sears Rat Run 11 - Limited Addition sees Finkz begin a new adventure and it's every bit as mad and wonderful as anything in Season 1!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/yuarri3g7w

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits. A redcurrant always sits between an even digit and an odd digit. In this experiment, any cell on the path equals the digit at the top of its column plus the digit at the left-hand end of its row.

title: Getting Lost in a Cave of Sudoku!
description:
Here's where you can try Killer Caves by Stephen Mason: https://sudokupad.app/eaox36rsvw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the total indicated, if it is shown. Digits do not repeat within a cage. Digits that appear in a cage also act as "cave clues".
Shade some cells to leave behind a single connected group — the cave — with no enclosed, shaded cells (ie. all shaded cells must be connected by other shaded cells to an edge of the grid). All "cave clues" must be a part of the cave, with each number indicating the total count of cells connected vertically and horizontally to the numbered cell including the cell itself.

title: This 6x6 Puzzle Drives Sudoku Expert Crazy!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We are so lucky on this channel to have the opportunity of sharing with you the output of minds like ThePedallingPianist's. His latest sudoku, Moving Day?, is his usual fare: brilliant, original and totally bonkers. Oh and hardly anyone seems to have solved it!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/eh7t6u3zz8

Rules:
Select six different digits from the set 1-9.  Use these six digits only to fill every cell such that a digit does not repeat in a row, column or box. Grey lines are entropic AND modular; i.e every 3-cell sequence on a line must contain a digit from {123}, one from {456} and {789}; also these digits must include one from {147}, one from {258} and one from {369}. Both indicated diagonals have the same sum. The inequality sign ‘points’ to the lower digit. Any 5 in the grid must have a 1 directly above it or a 9 directly below it (or both).  

[This last rule is apparently sometimes called 'Dutch Flatmates'!!]

title: The Answer To The Ultimate Question
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolute masterpiece this evening from ViKingPrime.  It's got everything you could ever want to see in a puzzle: fantastic logic, theme, sparsity of clues, wit and a 100% rating on Logic Masters.  Definitely grab some popcorn and settle in, this is a BRILLIANT sudoku.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/3peflzyncd

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The value of cells along an arrow must sum to the value in its originating circle. White dots separate two cells of consecutive value. Black dots separate two cells where one is double the value of the other. Cells along a pink line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. Cells along a green line must differ in value by at least five. No two lines will occupy the same cell. Place 𝐂𝐎𝐏𝐘𝐂𝐀𝐓 cells into the grid so that there is exactly one Copycat cell in each row, column and box; each Copycat cell must contain a different digit and the value of a Copycat cell is the digit in the cell rotationally opposite itself in the grid - 180° rotation about the centre of the grid (for example, if R2C3 is a Copycat cell containing the digit 5 and R8C7 contains the digit 9, the value of R2C3 is the digit in R8C7, which is 9). The value of cells within a cage must sum to the number in the top-left corner (if given). The grid is partially covered in 𝐅𝐎𝐆; placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding area. (Digits at the bottom of the grid have been provided for tracking purposes.)

title: How can a Mushroom Create a Puzzle?
description:
Nothing about the Times Crossword Championship today - maybe tomorrow! Here's where you can try Nexus by Ren the Mushroom: https://sudokupad.app/y7x01mea2l 
Normal sudoku rules apply. One cell within the grid, to be deduced, is a “multiplier nexus” cell. The value “n” within this “nexus” cell indicates that there are: exactly “n” 1s which have a taxicab distance of 1 away from the nexus; exactly “n” 2s which have a taxicab distance of 2 away from the nexus; exactly “n” 3s which have a taxicab distance of 3 away from the nexus; and so on... up to and including 9. A taxicab distance is the shortest distance between two cells, moving only horizontally and vertically.

title: It's Hammer Time For Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A very nice debut on the channel for Elytron today and a fog sudoku called Fog! Hammer Time!  It contains a new type of line and some indexing to please the computer programmers out there.  It's only rated 2 stars (out of 5) for difficulty on Logic Masters but we'd give it 3.

We hope you can forgive our sometimes lengthy introductions - and thank you to @Wirtual for appreciating our unusual approach to YouTubing :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/n3e6mr3qwr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Multiplying the digits on two circles of the same colour equals the sum of the digits on the line connecting them. Each product band is associated with a unique colour and does not split. Digits on the endpoints of a product band index either their row, column, or 3x3 box. (Boxes are numbered in normal reading order). Arrow clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio; not all black dots are necessarily given. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.

title: If You Don't Like Brilliant Puzzles, Don't Watch This.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We continue our Saturday series of non-sudoku puzzles with KNT's Cave Stations - an absolutely ASTONISHING hybrid.  The vision and skill required to create this puzzle cannot be overstated.  Mind you there is a LOT to think about and it's takes some unravelling but every step on the journey feels rather wonderful.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/9yzwo16hpj

Rules:
Draw a closed loop through the centre of some cells that passes through the numbers 1 to 9 in order (so after the 9 the loop returns back to the 1). Each number is passed through exactly once and all other numbers are unvisited. The loop may not turn on numbers it passes through, and the loop crosses itself exactly at the given intersections. Some cells are to be shaded such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all orthogonally-connected groups of shaded cells touch the perimeter of the grid. A digit not visited by the loop is unshaded and indicates the number of unshaded cells “seen” in all four directions from the cell containing the digit, including itself (where shaded cells block vision). All digits visited by the loop as well as intersections are shaded. Along the loop, there may never be three shaded or three unshaded cells visited sequentially. For the solution check function to work, enter a ‘1’ in every cell where the loop turns and a ‘2’ in every other unfilled loop cell.

description:
*** STREAM TONIGHT AT 10PM UK TIME ***
We'd love to see you if you can make it at the following link:
https://youtube.com/live/h9HYHiVBNj4

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A joyous beginning to tonight's video with an incredible version of our theme music from Robert and Elspeth - who have become parents TODAY. Many congratulations on the birth of twins Lachlan and Charlotte!!

On the sudoku side we try a new puzzle Eureka! from Michael Lefkowitz and get to say things like "Eureka" and "rinky dink" a lot during the solve!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/jx80un5ofh

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some additional cells grey ("walls") and leave some unshaded ("cave"). The cave is one orthogonally-connected group, and walls form orthogonally-connected groups that touch an edge of the grid. Draw a 1-cell wide loop that moves orthogonally, entering every cave cell (and no wall cells). Each digit on the loop in row N differs from its neighbours on the loop by at least N. Gold is found in wall cells with digits larger than their row number. All possible gold has been given. Digits separated by a white dot have consecutive values.

title: When Sudoku Segments Sum To 10...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After the trauma of the Young Sheldon finale, Simon pulls himself together enough to attempt Black_Doom's outstanding puzzle, Tenfold. This sits at a 99% approval rating (and average difficulty) and it features some absolutely lovely logic.

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/2yiw0yc01y

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop can't touch itself, not even diagonally. Additionally, the loop consists of non-overlapping segments, each of which sums to 10. Digits may repeat on the loop and even within an individual segment, if allowed by the other rules. The digit in a caged cell shows how many (of the up to 8) surrounding cells are on the loop. The caged cells cannot be on the loop. The number in the top-left corner of a caged cell shows the sum of digits in the loop cells around it.

title: The Puzzle that puts the Chocolate into Solving
description:
Here's where you can try Kropki Chocona by PixelPlucker: https://sudokupad.app/JRNmQMgrQ9 
Shade some cells such that all the following conditions are met: Each bold-outlined region contains at least one shaded cell; each orthogonally connected area of shaded cells is a rectangle; a black dot between two adjacent regions indicates that their numbers of shaded cells are in a 2:1 ratio; a white dot between two adjacent regions indicates that their numbers of shaded cells are consecutive (a region with one shaded cell next to a region with two shaded cells may therefore be marked with either a black or white dot); and all possible dots are given. That is, if there is no dot between two adjacent regions, neither of the above properties holds.
(For answer-check, place the region's number in its upper-left cell, use 0 for 10 etc). The puzzle probably won't work very well on mobiles today - sorry!

We tackled a fantastic sudoku by Kennet's Dad on the channel a couple of weeks ago. Today we try another - this one is easier but still provides an enormous ratio of joy/minute! It's called Restricted Access and we recommend everyone tries it!

Digits in cells joined by an X sum to 10; NOT all X clues are given. Digits in cells joined by a V sum to 5; ALL V clues are given and visible from the outset of the puzzle. If two digits are joined by a black dot then one of those digits is double the other. Not all black dots are given.

description:
Did you know that "a real pea-souper" once meant a thick fog? Here's where you can sample Pea Soup by Oddlyeven: https://sudokupad.app/xqgzhq4bqn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Digits on a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. 
Split-Pea Lines: The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 4-347-1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3 + 4 + 7 = 14, which is 1 concatenated with 4. Digits may repeat on a line if allowed by the other rules. Lines do not cross, branch or share cells with other lines, but they may share circles.

title: "What A Beautiful, Beautiful Puzzle."
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Delray Beach Sunrise by MaizeGator has earned itself a 100% rating.  It's been recommended to us, especially for our Saturday non-sudoku slot and we can confirm the rating is absolutely justified. This is a very special puzzle dedicated to a special place (that's been through an awful lot of late).

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/ypf71xbp99

Rules:
Divide the grid into polyominoes and fill each cell with a number equal to the size of its polyomino. Polyominoes of the same size may not share an edge. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or unshaded. All odd polyominoes are shaded, while all even polyominoes are unshaded. Numbers on cells with an arrow indicate the number of polyominoes of the SAME shading/parity seen in the direction of the arrow. Arrows do not count their own cell, but may count their polyomino if a cell within its polyomino is visible in the direction of the arrow.

title: The Last 2 Minutes Of This Sudoku Solve Will Astonish You
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears' puzzle Milestones is a sudoku which is fabulous to solve and features all of Marty's usual wit and originality.  However it also hides a secret... we won't say more but, rest assured, it's has VERY good finale!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/d4qzz9umkk

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into grey and orange regions. A region is a group of orthogonally connected cells of the same colour. No 2x2 area may be all one colour. Two regions of the same colour may not touch diagonally. A digit on an arrow cell indicates how many cells you have to travel in the indicated direction until you reach a cell of the opposite colour. Eg: if an orange arrow cell contains a 1 then the neighbouring cell in the direction of the arrow would be grey. Two orthogonally adjacent orange cells must have a difference of at least 4. A small clue indicates the number of cells in the region. In a cage, the sum of orange digits must equal the sum of grey digits. Digits MAY repeat in a cage if allowed by sudoku.

description:
Here's where you can have a go at Find the Haters by Sumanta (ANU): https://sudokupad.app/8mBD3pMgPj
Normal sudoku rules apply, except: for each type of clue, three clues are correct (generous), one clue is wrong (haters). Solvers have to find the wrong clues (haters:)), e.g: 347 is a wrong Renban or 238691 is a wrong thermo.
A correct purple line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. In a correct killer cage, there are no repeat digits and the sum of the cage is shown. For a correct thermo, digits must strictly increase from the bulb to the tip. X connects digits summing to 10 and V connects digits summing to 5 if they are correct clues. A correct orange circle indicates an odd digit.

title: A Great Puzzle Pair
description:
Here's where you can try Foes Eternal by Panthera & TheAsylm (links below)
You will start in Puzzle A. You will need to complete both puzzles simultaneously to succeed. Important note: the conflict checker will NOT work completely correctly. You may wish to turn it off to not be confused. The grid is covered by fog of war. Placing correct digits will remove the fog in the surrounding cells. In the grids, you will find labeled cages. The digits in these cages are to be transferred to the matching cage in the other puzzle to reveal more fog.
Puzzle A: https://sudokupad.app/ie3en5rp4i?setting-nogrid=1 The outside clues are red squares covered by fog of war. They indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded red. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given. For best results, remove all unshaded marking done once complete. Cells connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.
Puzzle B https://sudokupad.app/leekldq92z?setting-nogrid=1 : The color of the squares in this puzzle are yellow (Y), pink (P), green (g), gray (G), dark blue (B) and light blue (b). The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given. For best results, remove all unshaded marking done once complete.

title: He Came From Reddit To Blow Our Sudoku Minds
description:
*** NEW STREAM TONIGHT ***
10pm UK time at this link:
https://youtube.com/live/lHO0H-NcFgo?feature=share

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A few months ago we had recommendations to try a sudoku that was published on Reddit by Shintaro Fushida-Hardy.  The same constructor has appeared on the channel since too and his style is to make extremely beautiful puzzles that really sing to the solver.  This one is called Thermohaline Circulation - it was made for a competition and we suspect it probably won!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:

https://sudokupad.app/z7oxi1ve8x

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells to form a 1-cell-wide orthogonally connected loop. The loop may not touch itself orthogonally, but can touch itself diagonally. Non-loop cells form several orthogonally connected groups. Such a group of size N contains exactly the digits from 1 to N. Each cell with an arrow (called an 'arrow cell') lies on the loop. The digit in an arrow cell is the number of visible loop cells in the indicated direction, where non-loop cells obstruct vision. (The arrow cell is not included in this count). Additionally, digits increase along loop cells seen by an arrow, starting with the digit in the arrow cell.
