title: What Is Your Favourite Paradox?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love fog-of-war sudoku puzzles and this evening's has the distinction of being remarkably interesting and challenging.  The rules are straightforward but finding the logical way of clearing all that fog definitely requires some thought!  A magnificent sudoku by Chad called Renban Snakes - give it a try!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/1lh6uyp9fz

(If this link doesn't work, try the one below...)
https://sudokupad.app/kb9l12ce0e

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is mostly covered in fog. Placing correct digits will lift the fog around the placed digit revealing more clues. A cell containing an arrow is the start of a snake travelling in the indicated direction. The length of the snake is equal to the digit in the arrow's cell (snakes may be 1 cell long ie only occupy their arrow cell). A snake is a one-cell wide path of orthogonally connected cells that doesn't branch. Snakes may not overlap themselves or other snakes. Each snake acts as a “renban line” ie the digits on it form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. Cells joined by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.

title: A New Sudoku Rule: "Balance"
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Scojo comes up trumps today with a new rule created as part of the CTC Fan Discord server monthly competition.  The puzzle is called Balance and it's just brilliant.  So much clever stuff going on and yet another sudoku that can make even someone leery of math(s) learn to love numbers!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3ma2z9n9lr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Identify 9 Balance Cells in the grid such that there is one Balance Cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. Each Balance Cell must contain a different digit. The value of a Balance Cell is the arithmetic mean of the up to 4 digits orthogonally adjacent to itself, regardless of the digit in the Balance Cell. The sum of the values of every cell in the grid is 405. The values of cells in a cage must sum to the total in the top left corner. Digits may not repeat within a cage, but values may.

title: A New Sudoku Masterpiece (100%, 5/5 Difficulty)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday's sudoku was easy and brilliant; today's sudoku is rock hard and a masterpiece.  We live in the halcyon days for this passion of ours and Bodysnatchers by AnalyticalNinja and Kafkapharnaum is absolutely worth its place in the pantheon of truly great puzzles.  Some of the deductions you can make in this one will have you literally shouting with joy.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/e0l316poog

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. There is exactly one Doubler cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. These cells contain a full set of the digits 1-9 and do not overlap with the Body Snatcher cells. A Doubler cell's value is twice the value of the digit in that cell. There is exactly one Body Snatcher cell in every row, column, and 3x3 box. These cells contain a full set of the digits 1-9 and do not overlap with the Doubler cells. Body snatcher cells count as exactly one higher, or one lower than the value of one of the cells they are orthogonally adjacent to and that cell must be in the same box as the Body Snatcher it's parasited by. Each purple line contains a set of consecutive, non-repeating values, which can appear in any order. Digits can repeat on a purple line as long as no value ends up repeated on the line.

title: The Perfect Sudoku?
description:
Here's where you can try Nobody's Perfect by Lithium-Ion: https://sudokupad.app/3ppzefe55t 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells do not contain consecutive digits. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to a perfect number. A perfect number is a number that equals the sum of its proper divisors (i.e. each divisor excluding the number itself). For example, 20 is not a perfect number since the sum of the proper divisors is 1+2+4+5+10=22, which is not 20. [Hint: There are only two perfect numbers that are less than 45]

The digits on an arrow with the same shading as the arrow's circle sum to the digit in the arrow's circle. If both shaded and unshaded cells are found within a cage, each shading type must be connected in a single region. Digits in one of these regions sum to the number shown. description:

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/mqx8o45al4

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Pea lines: The sum of the digits on a line strictly between two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For instance, 3_346_1 could be a valid split pea line, as 3+4+6=13, which is 1 concatenated with 3. Zipper lines: Cells on a lavender line at an equal distance to the centre, which is marked with a dot, sum to the digit at the centre. (Note: The circles of pea lines are NOT part of the zipper lines. Ie the pea lines are green and lavender but the zipper lines are only the lavender parts.)

description:

A type of Miracle Sudoku today from James Kopp called That's 3 In The Corner.  That 3 is in fact the only given digit (or thing!) in the grid at all!!  Read the instructions, don't laugh, and then solve one of the most delightful puzzles you'll ever see!

title: Join us for some fun in the Sudoku Ballpit ...
description:
It's Wypman's birthday! Here's where you can try his XV Ballpit: https://sudokupad.app/hb3fq3jqP2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits do not repeat and sum to the number shown.
There are 5 types of balls in the grid: 
A: 1 set of digits around it must sum to 10 
B: 2 sets of digits around it must sum to 10 
C: 1 set of digits around it must sum to 5
D: 2 sets of digits around it must sum to 5 
E: 1 set of digits must sum to 5, 1 set of 2 digits must sum to 10 
A ‘set of digits’ always contains 2 orthogonally connected digits. No digit is part of 2 sets on the same circle, but it may be part of sets on different circles. There are no negative constraints, so other pairs may add to 5 or 10 around circles or elsewhere.

title: Three Puzzles In One 9x9 Grid
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A welcome return to the channel tonight for PjotrV with a three-in-one puzzle (called "3 in 1"!) combining fillomino, LITS and the perennial favourite Star Battle.  The skill with which these three types combine is prodigious and it's quite approachable too!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/ox3v11xvil

Rules:
Part 1: Normal Fillomino rules apply (see below). 
Part 2: Normal LITS rules apply (with the created regions from the Fillomino). 
Part 3: Normal Star Battle rules apply (with the created unshaded regions from the LITS (NOT the Fillomino regions)). Each Part may (if solved independently) have more than one solution but only one grid fill will satisfy all three Parts together. 
Fillomino rules: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Each cell should contain a number equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells in its region). The size of any region must not be the same of an orthogonally adjacent region. 
LITS rules: Place one tetromino into each region. No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely covered in tetrominoes. 
Star Battle rules: Place 1 star in each row/column/region such that no two stars touch each other, even diagonally.

For the solution check function to operate, place a 1 in every cell of the final grid that contains a star (and leave other cells empty). 


*** OUR RECENT "THANK GOODNESS YOU'RE HERE" STREAM ***
We had a blast playing this very original and Monty Python-esque game.  You can watch here:

title: Galaxies Collide:  2 Sudoku Geniuses Combine Forces
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears and maths professor Dorlir combine their mighty minds today to bring us Galaxies Collide - an absolutely fantastic minimalist sudoku, (lauded by Phistomefel among others).  

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/2susajautc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into two galaxies. Every cell in the grid belongs to one of the two galaxies. Each galaxy must consist of a region of orthogonally connected cells, and must have 180 degree rotational symmetry. (The central point around which a galaxy is symmetrical doesn't need to actually belong to that galaxy.) No 2x2 area may belong entirely to one galaxy. One of the two galaxies behaves like a German whisper; orthogonally adjacent cells in this galaxy must have a difference of at least 5. An arrow cell counts how many cells in its own galaxy are being pointed at altogether by its arrow(s), and this combined total is displayed on the arrow cell (the arrow cell itself is not included in the count.) Vision is not obscured by the other galaxy's cells.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What do you do if someone sits on your sudoku?  ThePedallingPianist has sat on this one with the result that he's rendered it fascinating. title: Two Sudokus Are Sometimes Better Than One
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We need to give this some more thought but this just might be one of the most impressive constructions we've ever seen on the channel.  The puzzle(s) is Gemini and it's by Christounet.  It's part of the zodiac project, created by VikingPrime some time ago and we've had so many recommendations to look at it.  It's basically got a perfect rating and you'll see why!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/6xlki7zd3x

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply in both grids. In each grid, the circles contain a complete set of the digits 1-9. For each pair of circles in the same position in both grids, the digit is the same. In one of the grids, the value of the cell is double the value of the digit. In the other grid, the value is unchanged. The doublers are not necessarily all in the same grid. It is up to the solver to determine in which grid each digit is doubled. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. The values of the cells in a cage must sum to the small clue, if given. Even if the cage total is not given, two cages in the same position in the two grids must contain values summing to the same total.

title: The King: A Fog Sudoku That May Leave You Emotional
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have had so many recommendations to try Justin Vitanza's sudoku "The King", which is an intriguing looking fog-of-war puzzle.  (And just wait until you read the rules.) All we can say is that this is one of the most memorable sudokus we're likely to solve all year.  Let us know what you think!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/7wu3gxtfgz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
The King's Law states that for a digit X, exactly X instances of the digit X are a king's move away from another instance of the digit X. However, two of the digits 1-9 (to be deduced) are rebellious and do not abide by this law. In fact, a rebellious digit is never a king's move away from another instance of itself.
The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell.

*** OUR RECENT "THANK GOODNESS YOU'RE HERE" STREAM ***

title: The Magic You Can Do With The Factors Of 12
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's Saturday so we're continuing with our series of non-sudoku puzzles.  Lizzy01 has made a variant of the Meidjuluk genre called Meidjuizy!  (We haven't a clue what these words mean!).  There are some brilliant ideas in this construction and the whole things solves like a charm.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/t790muspun

Rules:
Divide the grid into 12 regions, one of each size 1 to 12. Black cells are not in regions. A region may not contain repeated numbers, and it may only contain factors of its size (e.g. a region of size 6 may contain any combination of 1,2,3, and 6, including none of them).
In this puzzle, enter a number into each cell with an arrow (other cells remain empty). That number must equal the number of cells belonging to its own region seen in a straight line in the corresponding direction (not counting itself) before the first cell outside the region (or the edge of the grid).
(For the solution check function to work, in addition to entering the numbers on arrows, enter a 0 in the region of size 1.)

title: The Miracle Sudoku 3
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Ever since the first Miracle Sudoku all those years ago, constructors have come up with ingenious ways of creating puzzles with blank or almost blank grids.  Almost all of these puzzles, unsurprisingly, need complicated rules to create the necessary constraints to make the sudoku a) unique and b) humanly-solvable.  Michael Lefkowitz has come up with something astonishing.  It's called Little Wonder and, despite having nothing in the overlapping grids at all, there are only two short sentences of rules. title: Can You Find The Paths Through The Sudoku Fog?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A really cool fog-of-war sudoku today from Chilly titled Paths Through The Mist.  Unusually for a chaos construction (ie the 9-cell sudoku regions can be any shape) this isn't unapproachable but there are several "wow" moments during the solve!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/i0jnn0206n

Rules:
The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog, possibly revealing more clues. No guessing is required. Each row, column, and region contains the digits 1–9 exactly once each. A region is an orthogonally connected collection of cells, and regions are to be determined. The digit in a cell containing an arrow indicates the number of region borders in that direction. (If there is more than one arrow, the number of borders is the same in each direction eg a 4 in the cell with two arrows pointing East and North would indicate that there were 4 borders to the East AND 4 borders to the North). The outer edges of the grid do not count as borders. A digit in a circle equals the total number of cells seen horizontally and vertically that are in the same region as the digit, including itself. Borders obstruct vision.

[In case there are any plumbing gurus out there, Simon has a new sump pump that he needs to connect to a rigid old metal drain pipe.  However the piece of tubing he's always used for this job in the past doesn't attach to the new sump pump outflow.  (It's the same make of Sump Pump but the company has changed the connection... grrrr.)  The old metal drain pipe is a very non-standard size (the piece of tubing has an inner diameter of 27mm) but the sump pump outflow size is either 25mm or 32mm. Please bear in mind in any response that Simon is a COMPLETE BUFFOON at DIY and no knowledge AT ALL should be assumed!!)]

title: Sleepy Time Sudoku
description:
You can either let Mark's voice lull you to sleep or try Sleeper Cells by Bearded Fool here: https://sudokupad.app/06pymw27cj 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots separate cells with digits in a 2:1 ratio. White dots separate cells with consecutive digits. Adjacent cells on a green line have a difference of at least five. Digits along a red lines alternate between even and odd. Digits on a purple line form a non-repeating, consecutive set, arranged in any order. Box borders divide a blue line into segments with the same sum. Different blue lines can have different sums.
Every row, column, 3x3 box, and line has exactly one sleeper cell. Sleeper cells, though always appearing on the lines, are skipped when it comes to line logic. For example, a purple line that reads 18342 is valid if the 8 is a sleeper cell, as the digits that are not 8 form a valid purple line. Additionally, all sleeper cells contain digits equal to their 3x3 box number. Zzzzz

title: The Goldilocks Zone. Like The Twilight Zone but with more sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It wouldn't be a week on Cracking The Cryptic recently without a puzzle by Marty Sears.  (Last week's The Hare and The Tortoise doesn't count!) Today we tackle Marty's "own" puzzle from the recent imposter series.  It would be difficult to find adjectives to do this justice.  Just know it's sensational.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/a6zbf6jui2

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into 3 zones. Each zone consists of a single group of orthogonally connected cells. No 2x2 area may be entirely within one zone. The first zone is 'too hot'. Any cell in the hot zone has a value one greater than its digit. The second zone is 'too cold'. Any cell in the cold zone has a value one less than its digit. The third zone is 'just right'; this is the Goldilocks Zone. In this zone, a cell's value equals its digit, like normal. The 9 objects (bowls, chairs and beds) all contain different digits, but each object of the same type has the same value. Zone borders (NOT box borders) divide blue lines into segments, each of which has the same total (ie; the total being the sum of that segment’s VALUES.) The two ends of a blue line always lie in different zones.

Today's musical introduction is Here Comes The Sun by The Beatles and is dedicated to Boo Boo.

title: I've Never Seen That In ANY Sudoku!
description:
*** THANK GOODNESS YOU'RE HERE STREAM TONIGHT ***
We're going to play this game live on Sunday night at 10pm UK time!  Please be aware that this game does involve a swear word (we're told) so please don't watch if it may offend you. You can watch the stream at this link:

https://youtube.com/live/zgaMQV1iLDo

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ThePedallingPianist wowed us a few days ago with an imitation of Marty Sears called The Hare And The Tortoise.  But's that's not all he's been up to... a perfectly ridiculous idea today featuring the rarely seen "infinity" Little Killer clue...!!!  

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/eb90s76a4e

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and 2x3 rectangle). 
Shade every cell one of two colours such that each colour forms a single orthogonally connected area and no 2x2 area is entirely one colour. 
Clues outside the grid show the sum of the digits in the first continuous run of same-coloured cells along marked diagonals. 
The grid is toroidal; i.e. each edge of the grid is considered to be adjacent/orthogonal to its opposite edge. For example, the 2nd cell pointed at by the 22 diagonal clue is r2c1 (and, for the avoidance of doubt, this cell is orthogonally adjacent to r2c6).

title: Turkish Genius: Saturday Puzzle Series No.5
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're big fans of gmpuzzles and their devotion to handmade puzzles.  Today we feature a Snake Egg puzzle created by them especially for us by the Turkish genius Serkan Yurekli.  This is exactly the reason we thought this Saturday slot should exist - it's a beautiful and clever idea, executed with such aplomb!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/fDrRP46trL

Rules:
Draw a snake (a 1 cell-wide path) in the grid whose head and tail are given by circled cells. The snake can touch itself diagonally, but cannot touch itself orthogonally or revisit any square. Besides the snake, the remaining cells must form exactly nine white areas, one of each size from 1 to 9. Numbers in the grid must be part of white areas of the indicated size.
(For the solution check function to work, place a digit into each white cell equal to the size of its region.)

You can find gmpuzzles here:

description:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Occasionally we like to offer viewers bumper length episodes!  Here's a movie edition in which Simon does battle with Nordy's exceptional Medieval Upheaval 4.  It's a "chaos construction" with some unusual chess restrictions - the whole thing is quite fascinating but perhaps not totally straightforward :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/0of52e2mjx

Rules:
Divide the grid into regions, each consisting of nine orthogonally-connected cells. Every row, column, and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. Digits along a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, but may be written in any order. A cell with a number in its top-left corner is a “Chess Sums” cell. The number in the top-left corner indicates the amount of Chess Sums satisfied by the digit in that cell. A digit in a Chess Sums cell gives one or more of the following:
• The sum of all digits that share its region and are a king’s move away
• The sum of all digits that share its region and are a knight’s move away
• The sum of all digits that share its region and are a bishop’s move away

title: The Hare And The Tortoise:  Among Us Meets Sudoku!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Huge props to the constructor Scojo who came up with the idea of inviting other well-known sudoku constructors to imitate the styles of their peers.  In a sudoku version of Among Us, solvers can solve the puzzle and then attempt to guess whether the stated author is real or an impostor!  Today's puzzle, The Hare And The Tortoise is by "Marty Sears".  At the end of the video, you'll see whether Marty made this one or not.  In a sense it doesn't matter, this is one of the best puzzles we've EVER seen whoever the author is.  Even the rules are absolutely phenomenal.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
With poetic instructions (which Simon uses in the video):
https://sudokupad.app/qes8ggvsi4

With plain instructions:
https://sudokupad.app/6gdihuldki

Rules:
Let me tell you the tale of a Hare I know,
Who mocked an old Tortoise for being so slow.
“You think that you’re faster?” the Tortoise replied,
“Then race me and prove it, or swallow your pride!”

The Hare found the thought of a race quite amusing:
He’d win even if he spent half the time snoozing!
“Of course,” said the Hare, suppressing his laughter,
“I’ll run the race thrice; you'll still finish after!”

They set up their racing grid, neath the blue sky,
Where normal sudoku rules always apply.
And waiting to meet them by their starting blocks,
The judge of the race: the neighbourhood Fox.

Their racing lines travel in any direction,
But never share cells or cause an intersection
Except where they both end: the chequered flag’s cell.
Both lines must avoid all the blue ponds as well.

On Tortoise’s line, a ‘Slow Thermo’ by name,
The digits can increase or just stay the same.
Hare’s line is a ‘Fast Thermo’: digits still climb,
But these go up by at least 3 at a time...

...That is until box borders, where the Hare naps,
And his Thermo can restart - at low digits, perhaps.
And finally, Hare smugly shows off a line
That ENTERS each box ONCE, including box nine.

“I’ll announce the winner,” Fox shouts through the grass,
“By displaying a digit through which he does NOT pass.”
And Duck, who’s excited to watch this race live,
Says, “The digits in my pond must sum up to 5.”

So, can you help settle this age-old debate?
Who wins the race, and who is too late?
Is it best to be swift, or steady and slow?
Now let's all get cracking! Ready... and GO!

Plain instructions:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The Hare and the Tortoise must race in orthogonal or diagonal steps, and must not enter ponds, or cross or overlap each other or themselves, apart from at the finish line, where both their paths end. The Hare must enter every 3x3 box exactly once each (including box 9 - starting in box 9 does NOT count as entering it). The Hare's racing line will be a valid “Fast Thermo” - ie. digits along it increase by at least 3 at a time, but the Hare has a nap at every box border and the Thermo may begin again on any digit in the next cell. The Tortoise's racing line will be a valid Slow Thermo - ie. digits along it may not decrease. The Fox declares the winner by displaying a digit that does NOT appear on the winner's racing line. Digits separated by the Duck sum to 5.

title: Can You Join These Twelve Dots?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
For the last months we've featured an almost weekly Marty Sears puzzle!  There is absolutely no reason to stop now!!  Here's one of his new sudokus, which many of you have recommended/requested.  It's called Twelve Spots and, as you might guess, it's absolutely brilliant AGAIN!

Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1-6, once each, into every row, column and box.) Draw 6 lines, each with a different turquoise spot at both ends. Each line is a 'same difference' line ie Every pair of adjacent cells along a line has the same difference - this is its 'difference value.' Every line has a different 'difference value'. Digits in a cage sum to the total given in the cage’s top left corner.

title: Who Knows if it's a Lizard or a Baby?
description:

title: Simon's Favourite Phistomefel?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon doesn't need too much persuading to attempt a Phistomefel puzzle and many of you have requested he try this (supposed) 3* rated concoction called HöhlenSTIL.  It's difficult to know what to say about it without giving too much away but the ideas in this one are wonderful. It's easy to get carried away in the moment but it's certainly one of Simon's favourite puzzles of the year.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/l0ffcltlz4

Rules:
Shade some cells in the grid such that all unshaded cells (the inside of the ‘cave’) are orthogonally connected to each other and all shaded cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid. Clue cells are unshaded and indicate the number of unshaded cells seen in the four orthogonal directions from that cell, including itself. Shaded cells obstruct vision. 
The cave and each wall section is a separate region for the purposes of a ‘LITS puzzle’. In a LITS puzzle, solvers must place one tetromino into each region. No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely covered in tetrominoes. 
For the solution check function to work, having completed the puzzle, solvers should enter a 3 into every cell filled with a tetromino; a 2 into every non-tetromino shaded cell; and a 1 into every non-tetromino unshaded cell.

title: Inner Peas
description:
Here's where you can reach Inner Peas by SamuPiano: https://sudokupad.app/qwd7jxoeym 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 region can be completely shaded or unshaded. Each cell in one region has a value of its digit plus 1. Each cell in the other region has a value of its digit minus 1.
The sum of the values of cells on lines connecting two circles is equal to a concatenation of the two values in the circles, in some order. For example, 3_346_1 is valid, as 3+4+6=13. Leading zeros are allowed. Every line between two circles is summed separately.

description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT RELEASED YESTERDAY ***
We've launched a brand new competition - a sudoku hunt (by us) featuring lots of sudokus with connections to Hollywood sandwiches!  Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

An original and absolutely brilliant sudoku today called Bookends by mnasti2.  (Hence the Simon & Garfunkel intro today.) This is a seriously clever piece of puzzle setting as you'll discover the moment you try it!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/e0yukfm7p9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply (ie place the digits 1 to 6, once each, into each row, column and rectangular box). One cell in each row, column, and box is a ‘doubler’, and each digit is doubled once. Digits do not repeat in cages. Each cage sums to a different total (with doubled digits counting as twice their value) and the totals are ranked in order from lowest (1) to highest (6). The number in the top left of the cage, if given, indicates this rank.

description:

title: The Final Rat Puzzle?  Finkz In The Fog!
description:
*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT RELEASED TODAY ***
We've launched a brand new competition - a sudoku hunt (by us) featuring lots of sudokus with connections to Hollywood sandwiches!  Check it out for as little as $2/month here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The most popular sudoku series of all time continues/concludes tonight with Simon tackling Marty Sear's Rat Run 10: Sensored.  Nobody familiar with the adventures of Finkz (or the puzzles of Marty) will find it surprising that this is another humdinger of a puzzle. Simon feels it would be quite easy to make (unjustified) logical leaps while solving it but did his best to avoid doing so - forgive him for the length of the video!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/fjayk4klcz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. 
The maze has been filled with fog. When correct digits are entered, the nearby fog will clear. No guessing is required. 
Digits connected by a blackcurrant are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. 
The digit on a pink motion sensor indicates how many of the (up to 9) cells immediately surrounding the sensor are visited by Finkz - ie; any cells neighbouring the sensor cell (diagonally or orthogonally), as well as the sensor cell itself, are counted, if they lie on the path. 
Digits don't repeat in a cage. Every cage has an electricity symbol, which indicates its 'shock value'. Any cage with a shock value of 5 or higher should not be entered by Finkz. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are safe to enter. In this experiment, the first cage that Finkz enters could have any total. After that, each subsequent cage she enters must have a total exactly one greater than the previous cage she entered. Cages not entered by Finkz can have any total.

title: Everythign is Wrogn Here!
description:
Here is where you can attempt the extraordinary Lief, the Univeres, and Everythign by SSG: https://sudokupad.app/3nkifpknc6, 
SSG is turning 42? That can't be rihgt. 
Normal sudoku rules apply; but, every clue is wrogn. Any clue that fully obeys one of the following rules is not wrogn.
Ambiguous Thermos: Digits along a gray line must strictly increase from one end to the other.
Ascending Starters: A clue outside the grid applies to the sum of the first run of ascending digits from the position of the clue (i.e. the sum from the first digit encountered until digits are no longer ascending). This may be only a single digit.
Entropic Lines: Along a peach line, every group of three consecutive cells must contain one low {1,2,3}, one medium {4,5,6}, and one high {7,8,9} digit.
Killer: Digits in a cage may not repeat and must sum to the given total.
Modular Lines: Along a teal line, every run of three digits must all have different remainders under division by 3.
Nabner: No two cells on a yellow line may contain either the same digit or consecutive digits.
Parity Lines: Along a red line, adjacent digits may not have the same parity.
Renban: Digits along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set.
Quadruples: Every digit in a circle must appear at least once in the surrounding four cells.

title: Don't Make 4 In A Row:  Saturday Puzzle Series No.3
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
In the third of our new series where we spend our Saturday evenings in the company of logic puzzles rather than sudoku, Simon attempts Kurotto (Aqre) by the brilliant KNT!  It combines two puzzle types he only has vague familiarity with but, provided you remember not to make 4 in a row, you can go far!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/en96i1su3o?setting-conflictchecker=0

Rules:
Shade some cells such that all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and there may not exist a run of four or more consecutive shaded or unshaded cells horizontally or vertically anywhere in the grid. Furthermore, each cell containing a number must not be shaded, and the number in the cell represents the total count of shaded cells in orthogonally connected groups sharing an edge with that number. A '?' indicates a single digit number. A '??' indicates a double digit number. (The solution check function will work if you enter an 'A' into every unshaded cell and a 'B' into every shaded cell once you've finished the puzzle.)

title: Phistomefel Breaks Our Brains
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon has returned from his brief vacation in Portugal to find a new puzzle by Phistomefel!  It's called Copycat Confusion and, as you might expect, it is a work of genius. Some of the discoveries you have to make to solve it are really mind-bending.  This is a sudoku for connoisseurs! 

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/hrsnhhdbno

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Divide the four lines in the grid into two pairs. The lines in a pair are copycats of each other, i.e. they have the same composition of digits. E.g. if one line has two 3s, five 4s and a 9, then the other one also has two 3s, five 4s and a 9. The order of the digits is not necessarily the same on the two lines. The two lines in the grid with a circle on one end are an average arrow and a thermometer. The two lines without a circle are a region sum line and a german whispers line. The solver has to deduce which line obeys which rule. 
Average Arrow: The digit in the circle is the average (exact, not rounded) of the digits on the line. 
Thermometer: The digits have to increase along the thermometer, starting from its bulb. 
Region Sum Line: The line is cut into multiple segments by the box borders, each summing to the same number. 
German Whisper: Two neighboring digits have a difference of 5 or more.

title: A 10/10 Fog Sudoku:  Fifteen Cages by James Sinclair
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon has returned from his brief vacation in Portugal and is rather delighted to find a James Sinclair' Fog-of-War sudoku for him to attempt as a welcome-home present.  This is apparently the only puzzle James has rated 10/10 for difficulty in his weekly puzzle letter Artisanal Sudoku (link below).  What we can say is that, from start to finish, this is AMAZING.  Do give it a try if you can.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/fifteen-cages

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Correctly placed digits clear the fog around them. The grid contains exactly fifteen cages that do not overlap and each cage occupies two or more cells. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Not all cage sums are given but sums that are given are located in the left-most cell in the highest row reached by the cage. Two cages of the same size cannot have the same sum (regardless of whether either cage's sum is given). Digits in cells with a shaded circle must be odd. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.

Find more puzzles like this at artisanalsudoku.com

title: The Ghost Cages
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***

title: Don't Electrocute The Rat!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This series of Rat Run sudokus by Marty Sears is one of the best things going on in the world of puzzles at the moment.  We move on to the ninth episode: Shock Value in which Finkz the rat now has to deal with the threat of electrocution!! We have it on good authority that the final puzzle in this series of scientific experiments is a fog-of-war puzzle - so please don't be alarmed if that appears on the channel soon.  Simon is unlikely to be able to wait very long before trying it!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/vaeya6u829

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
TELEPORTS: Entering a yellow teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the other teleport. From there she can continue her journey. The teleports contain the same digit.
BLACKCURRANTS: Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given.
CAGES: Digits don't repeat in a cage. Every cage has the same total, which is to be deduced. The digit on a cage's electricity symbol is its 'shock value'. Any cage with a shock value of 5 or more is switched on, and Finkz should not enter these for safety reasons. Cages with a shock value lower than 5 are switched off and therefore safe to enter.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the correct path will be a valid Chinese Whisper line, ie; adjacent digits along the path must differ by at most 2.

title: The Magic of an Empty Grid
description:
Here's where you can try Mathemagics by Lithium-Ion: https://sudokupad.app/7BghrPt24L 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a one-cell wide loop that moves orthogonally through the center of cells and does not branch, intersect with itself or touch itself (neither orthogonally nor diagonally). The loop has to visit each box at least once. For each box, the maximum number of cells belonging to the loop is k, where k is the box number. Within each box, the box number has to be part of the loop. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Two orthogonally adjacent cells are only allowed to contain digits that sum to 7 or 10 if both cells are not part of the loop. The 24 cells that are enclosed by the loop have to contain two magic squares. A magic square is a 3x3 region containing the digits from 1 to 9 once each, where each row, column and diagonal must sum to the same value.

There are some constructors that can be absolutely relied upon for innovation and wit... ThePedallingPianist is one such creature! The digit in the circle shows how many times it appears in that circle. The eight cells with teeth attached all contain different digits. title: The Rat has Friends ...
description:
Here's where you can try With friends like this... by Ratfinkz: https://sudokupad.app/vgpr0pfsqm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat and sum to the total shown. Consecutive digits cannot border each other in the same cage.
There is 1 negator in every row, column and box, forming a set of the digits 1-9. If negators appear in a cage they subtract their value from the sum of the other digits. 
Each diamond is a friendly square. Friendly cells are cells which match either their row number or their column number. Digits may never repeat in friendly cells, but not all digits need appear as a friendly cell. The circular white dot joins consecutive digits.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's rare nowadays for Simon to get to try a 1* rated sudoku but, perhaps unsurprisingly, it's a Michael Lefkowitz puzzle (called "Trace Amounts") that fits the bill! The idea here is that there are "ghost cages" and the solver has to deduce how the killer cages should look.  It's so original and utterly enchanting to solve.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/j8w1vml1mn

title: The Train And The Fly: One Of The Most Interesting Puzzles We've Ever Featured
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of our testers had a look at this puzzle when it was first released and has been sending Simon a daily email since asking whether he has tried to solve it!  Well now he has.  It's called The Train And The Fly and it's (yet) another creation from the seemingly-limitless imagination of Marty Sears.  It's also one of the most interesting and elegant puzzles we've ever featured.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/wjiiera37d

Rules:
Fill each cell with a single digit and draw a “train” that covers every cell in the grid. The train consists of 4 carriages of equal length and each carriage is formed of an orthogonal path of cells. A carriage doesn't touch itself, not even diagonally. Adjacent digits along a carriage are consecutive. An X connects the end cells of two carriages, which sum to 10. The black fly connects two digits with a 1:2 ratio. Identical digits may not touch each other orthogonally. A digit on the train indicates how many times that digit appears on the train.

title: The Fairy Tale Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Simon is appalled that he didn't mention The Frog Chorus (We All Stand Together) by Paul McCartney in the introduction to this evening's sudoku!  It's called Aquanuradoku and it's by Mennoo_ who has a birthday this coming week.  And it comes with a fairy story about frogs... what more could you ask for?!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3gdgz1a4il

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a main diagonal (marked in blue) digits may not repeat. Purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits. A white dot separates cells containing consecutive digits. Not all dots are given. The golden ball in the centre of the pond and the frog king with the crown (in the bottom-left corner, i.e. r9c1) each contain an odd digit. The frogs in the corners are “frog-fountains” which behave as thermometers, with the number on a frog indicating how far the fountain reaches towards the middle of the grid along the indicated diagonals (i.e. diagonal thermometers of length N+1 with N the digit on the frog). Along a frog-fountain, digits increase away from the frog.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're thinking of introducing a new series on the channel where we designate one day of the week to puzzles of any type that AREN'T sudoku!  Is this a good idea?  Well we thought we'd give it a try tonight by trying Poseidon by Shintaro Fushida-Hardy (of Mystery Prime Sudoku fame).  It's absolutely remarkable that such a sparsely-filled grid can solve this beautifully but it does!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/roa3ic53te

Rules:
Yin-Yang: shade some cells so that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 region is entirely shaded or unshaded. In addition, place a digit (from 1 to 9) in every cell with an arrow. This digit is the total number of shaded cells in the indicated direction (including the cell itself, if it is shaded). No two shaded cells can contain the same digit, and no two unshaded cells can contain the same digit. (However, the same digit may occur once shaded and once unshaded.) Cells without arrows do not contain digits.

title: Rat Run Sudoku: Marty Sears Is Surely Trolling!!
description:
[My apologies that tonight's video was released 30minutes late.  I had an internet outage this evening. If you wouldn't mind dropping a "Like" on the video to try and remind the algorithm that the video might still be interesting even if released outside our normal schedule, I would certainly appreciate it. Simon]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
About once a week we have had the absolute pleasure of solving the latest puzzle in Marty Sears' Rat Run sudoku series.  This one is called Discontinuous and it's so clever it's actually funny.  The routes Finkz takes to get to the cupcake are never the most straightforward :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/etuf5ak2y4

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
MODIFIER: There are 9 doubler cells to be located in the maze, one in each row, column and box, and each containing a different digit. The real value of a doubler cell is calculated by doubling the digit that appears in it.
BLACKCURRANTS: The values of cells connected by a blackcurrant are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given.
FORBIDDEN DOORS: The values of cells connected by a red X sum to 10. Finkz may never pass through a red X. Not all possible Xs have been given.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, dotted box borders divide the correct path into segments, each of which must be a valid 'nabner line'; no two cells anywhere on a path segment can have consecutive or equal values. title: The "Fog Of War" Sudoku Paradox
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Darth Paradox has made an absolutely remarkable fog of war sudoku and tonight we try it out.  It isn't easy but it's gorgeous and extremely clever from start to finish.  Prepare to be amazed!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/2s9gi1de7p

Rules:
Place the digits 0 to 9 once into each row, column, and 3x3 box. One cell in each row, column, and box is an S-cell containing two digits. The value of an S-cell is the sum of its digits; no two S-cells contain the same pair of digits. Fog covers some cells, and will be cleared when a correct single digit is placed in a cell; S-cells do not clear fog. “Renban loops” contain a set of consecutive values in any order. Each loop is a different colour of thick line, and does not cross or intersect itself. The value in a circle is equal to the sum of the values along the attached arrow. Each arrow is a different colour of thin line, and does not branch. The values in cells surrounding an X sum to 10, and the values in cells surrounding a V sum to 5. A cell with a grey square contains an even value.

You can watch @usagymnastics ' video about the puzzle exploits of gymnast Stephen Nedoroscik here:

An old friend of the channel returns today with a very unusual new ruleset and a sublime puzzle with twelve (12!!!!) given digits!!  It's called Euclidean Windmill and it's by Botaku. description:

title: The Sudoku Rat: She's BACK!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After the utter genius of yesterday's sudoku, we needed a puzzle that could fill big boots and who better to rely on for such things than Marty Sears... especially as Marty's RatRun series is one of the greatest things in sudoku, period!

So here's the next one: Multiple Choice - which, as you might expect, will have you shaking your head at its cleverness.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/yp87tkg99m

Rules:
RAT RUN 7: Multiple Choice
by Marty Sears
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell.
TELEPORTS: Entering a teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the matching coloured teleport. From there she can continue her journey. Matching teleports always have identical digits, but teleports that don't match always have different digits.
ONE-WAY DOORS: Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, for any two adjacent digits along the correct path, one can be divided by the other to give an exact integer (ie; one is a multiple of the other.)

title: Are You Sure You Know The Rules Of Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's sudoku would have some claim to be the most innovative puzzle of all time.  We won't tell you why - just solve it and you'll see.  It's by "Karl The Fog", which we understand to be a pseudonym for ThePedallingPianist and Michael Lefkowitz. 3 stars out of 5 for difficulty and a 100% approval rating...  

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/e3dz5lytps

Rules:
Oh! You're solving my puzzle, aren't you?  That's so exciting! Oh, right, the rules... what were they... Okay, yes, here we go: Normal 6x6 Sudoku rules apply (obviously); Red lines are "Modular" lines - every 3-cell sequence on a red line contains a digit from {1,4}, {2,5} and {3,6}; Blue lines are "Region Sum" lines - box borders divide them into multiple segments with the same sum; Lines only move orthogonally; Lines can't share cells with other lines; Red lines are "Modular" lines -- wait, did I do that one already? I can't remember; Cages are uh.... hmm... oh yeah, "Killer Cages!" - Digits in them can't repeat, and their sum is always always always given in the Upper Left corner (the leftmost cell of the topmost row of the cage) - And they don't overlap; I'm covering most of the grid, but if you place a *correct* digit, I'll clear from that cell and the cells around it.
Whew! I'm sure those were all the rules. Oh, I'm so hopeful that you can solve it!
-- Karl the Fog

title: Nothing Negative to Say about this Puzzle!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Negator XS by Thoughtbyte: https://tinyurl.com/negatorxs
Normal sudoku rules apply. Nine cells (one in each row/column/box) are negators, and have values equal to the negative of their digits. Each digit appears in exactly one negator. A clue outside the grid is the sum of the first X cells in the corresponding row/column, where X is the value in the cell nearest to the clue. If the value of X is negative, count the first X cells going in the opposite direction. For example, if R2C1 is a negative X-sum digit -4, the X-sum is the total of R2C1, R2C9, R2C8, and R2C7. Question mark clues are any single digit integers (-9 to 9). The cell with grey the square contains an even digit; the cell with the grey circle contains an odd digit. Digits cannot repeat along the indicated diagonal regardless of their sign.

title: A Beautiful Sequel: Sudoku meets Nurikabe
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There are some logic puzzles whose appearance should make you smile - nurikabe is one such and Niverio has managed to combine it with sudoku today in a beautiful hybrid.  The puzzle is called Galapagos and is the sequel to The Caribbean, which we featured back in September 2023.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6r1czEP1NQw

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/DhFTHL63t7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected (without creating a 2x2 area) which divides the unshaded cells into blocks of unshaded cells (islands). Each island contains exactly one clue (the small numbers in the grid), and that clue gives the sum of the digits on the island. All clues (except the given 4, whose shading is unknown) are part of the islands. Digits do not repeat on an island. No island is contained within a single 3x3 box, and an island’s cells must have the same sum within each box that island enters. Different visits to a box DO NOT count separately. (Example: A 36 clue island may have cells in 4 boxes that all sum to 9; or 3 boxes with all summing to 12; or 2 boxes with each box's digits summing to 18.)

title: One of the Most Fantastic Colouring Exercises Ever
description:
Here's where you can play Factor Map by Ul-Rhymm: https://sudokupad.app/c325ibxs31 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Within cages, digits cannot repeat. Each cage has a value equal to the sum of all the digits it contains. Color each cage 1 of 4 colors. Cages of the same color cannot share sides, though they may touch corner-to-corner. All cages with the same color have sums whose prime factorizations contain the same set of prime factors. [E.g. If a red cage is 20 = 2x2x5, then all other red cages must have a prime factorization of 2^X*5^Y. For example, 10, 20, 40, 50, 80, 100, etc could all be valid. 25 would not be valid (no 2's). 30 would not be valid (2x3x5 has a 3). Any other colored cage could not have a 2 nor 5 in its prime factorizations.]

A few weeks ago, we featured a gdc puzzle that contained the most amazing sudoku cell we'd ever seen.  Well, gdc is back and this one gives that earlier puzzle a run for its money.  Which cell is it?  You'll know it when you see it!!

title: These Shapes Look Completely Impossible
description:
Here's where you can play Non-repeating Palindromes by Amin Khalek: https://sudokupad.app/100ywt1d63 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are nine doubler and nine halver cells in the grid. Place one doubler and one halver in every row, column and box such that doublers and halvers cannot share a cell, and each digit from 1-9 appears once in a doubler cell and once in a halver cell. A doubler cell's value counts as double its digit while a halver cell's value counts as half its digit. Values on a grey palindrome line read the same forwards and backwards. Box borders divide each blue line into segments whose values have the same sum. Each inequality symbol ‘points’ to the smaller value of the two joined cells.

A REALLY clever 6x6 sudoku today from Teal.  It's called 45 - and we have no idea why!  It doesn't seem to have anything to do with the secret of sudoku.  Oh and did we mention that you're not told which six digits you have to use to fill this puzzle??!

title: The Purple Man:  This is sudoku GENIUS.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
All we can say about this one is WOW.  It's called Zebediah Killgrave and it's the work of starwarigami.  It uses zipper lines in a new and clever way and, although it's a 5* rated puzzle, it's just SO good.  And, no, Simon didn't know who Zebediah was...

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/nnf5fqru6z

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may not repeat in a cage. The totals of cages an equal distance from the central cage along a lavender line must sum to the total of the central cage. Eg For the line beginning in r7c1 there are five cages along the line left-to-right; labelling these cages A, B, C, D & E, the central cage C (comprising r8c5&r8c6) sums to the same as the cells in cages B+D and the same as the cages A+E. The digit in the cell marked with a square is even.

title: The Sudoku Rat Seeks Equality?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we attempt the sixth puzzle, Equilibrium, in one of the most epic of sudoku series: Marty Sears' Rat Runs.  The adventures of Finkz continue - this time with blackcurrants and a teleport - as she attempts to get to the cupcake :)

These sudokus are so fun to solve - we can't remember this one highly enough!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3xa2x14bxe

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path must not visit any cell more than once, cross itself, or pass through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through a round wall-spot on the corner of a cell. Entering a yellow teleport will cause Finkz to be instantly transported to the other teleport. From there she can continue her journey. The teleports contain the same digit. Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. Cells connected by a blackcurrant are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. In this experiment, the sum of the digits on the path before teleporting must equal the sum of the digits on the path after teleporting.

title: Find the Islands
description:
Here's where you can try Zodiac Project: Ponta Delgada by Florian Wortmann: https://sudokupad.app/2p1an6oilw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The nine cells containing a clue form an extra region, i.e. they contain the digits 1-9 without repetition. Shade some cells so that all of the following conditions are fulfilled: All shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area (water); Groups of orthogonally connected unshaded cells form islands. An island may consist of only one cell, and each island contains exactly one clue; No 2x2 may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. Each island acts as a killer cage, in which digits may not repeat and sum to the given clue (although for some of the cages the sum is unknown). Within an island, digits must either all increase or all decrease orthogonally in every direction, starting from the cell with the clue.

title: The Path Through Life
description:
Here's where you can try The Path Through Life by Tobias: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/TQdQfrd2HB 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a 1-cell wide path across life. The path does not branch and does not touch itself orthogonally. Start in one of the cages, visiting the hidden letters E and M there in that order. Continue the path into the other cage, visiting V and A (in that order) before returning to the first region visiting M again. Letters each represent a different digit, and any letter shown in the grid is not on the path. The path leaves exactly one region of each of sizes 2,3,4,5,6,7 and 8 behind. If a circle is on the path, its digit says how many path-cells it "sees" (counting itself – non-path cells block the view), and if a circle is off the path it says how big its non-path region is. Along the path, a blue square indicates a pair of digits summing to 10 whereas in the areas not on the path it indicates a pair of digits summing to 5. No blue square is only partially on the path.

title: The Cleverest Rat Run Sudoku Yet
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we attempt the fifth puzzle, Disparity, in one of the most epic of sudoku series: Marty Sears' Rat Runs.  The adventures of Finkz continue - this time with blackcurrants and a parity line - as she attempts to get to the cupcake :)

In our opinion this might just be the cleverest sudoku in this series yet - which is saying quite something!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/wv01avmfs9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path will be a snaking line that passes through the centres of cells, without visiting any cell more than once, crossing itself or passing through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass through a rounded corner / end of a wall. Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two values it sits between. Cells connected by a blackcurrant are in a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. In this experiment, the correct path will be a valid alternating parity line - ie: any pair of adjacent cells along the path must contain one even digit and one odd digit.

title: A Brilliant Combination of Rules
description:
Here's where you can try Little Killer Sandwiches by jreg: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/eennxzmcfl
Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot appear in cells separated by a (chess) king’s move (ie. in cells touching diagonally). The clues outside the grid all have two meanings: they give the sum of the diagonals indicated by the arrows, AND they give the sum of digits "sandwiched" between the numbers 1 and 9 in the clue's row or column. (The latter doesn't apply to the clue in the top left corner as it doesn't see any row or column directly.)

title: This Grid is Chock a Block Full (and that's a clue)
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Chock-a-Block by Marty Sears and Justin Vitanza: https://sudokupad.app/1j53hl97cx 
Normal sudoku rules apply. ALL lines in the grid are N-Lines. Each N-line is composed of one or more non-overlapping sets of adjacent digits, each of which sum to N. Every line has a different N value. Coloured lines (not including the grey ones) each have an additional rule:
• Renban (pink): Digits on a pink line form a non-repeating consecutive set, which can be arranged in any order.
• Even Sum Lines (darker blue): All the digits on a darker blue line sum to an even number.
• Prime Lines (purple): Adjacent digits on a purple line sum to a prime number.
• Anti-Kropki Lines (red): No two digits anywhere on the same red line are consecutive, or in a 1:2 ratio (but they may repeat).
• Same Difference Lines (turquoise): Each pair of adjacent digits on a turquoise line have the same difference. This difference must be determined for each turquoise line.
Here's a colourblind-friendly version: https://sudokupad.app/dc0dbdewab

title: The Return Of Star Battle!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The return of many wonderful things on the channel today: the constructor AFrayedKnot, Star Battle and LITS!  Moreover Simon mistakenly decides it would be a good idea to "quickly" solve the example 8x8 puzzle - not realising that this is a treat in and of itself!  So there's two "Let's Get Cracking"s in the video today.

Play the example 8x8 puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/b9GJQ2h4Nm

Play the main 12x12 puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/J9L2r7gL39

Rules:
Normal LITS rules apply. Ie Shade one tetromino in each region. (A tetromino is a shape of four orthogonally-connected cells.) No two tetrominoes of the same shape may share an edge - reflections/rotations count as the same shape. All tetrominoes must form a single orthogonally connected area. No 2x2 area of the grid can be completely shaded. Additionally, each row, column and region must contain exactly one white star and one black star.  Black stars must be located on tetrominoes, and white stars must not. Regardless of colour, stars may not touch each other - not even diagonally. 

For answer check to work, use the digit 1 for unstarred white cells, the digit 2 for starred white cells, the digit 9 for unstarred black cells and the digit 8 for starred black cells.

title: 600,000: Like 300 only 2000 times better
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Dorlir, a maths professor, sets incredible puzzles and he's been kind enough to put together this one to celebrate CtC reaching 600,000 subscribers on YouTube!  And it's absolutely brilliant.  The only thing we weren't quite certain about was the rules so you can play the puzzle with two versions!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/MBJ89f8h9D

Rules:
[These are the rules Simon assumed when solving the puzzle.]

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a snake in the grid which must start and end at grey circles. The snake is a one-cell-wide path of orthogonally connected cells which may touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. If the snake passes through box N, then the digit N must be part of the snake in that box. The snake cannot pass through a white dot. Finally, the product of the digits along the snake is equal to 600,000.

[A slightly easier version would read as follows...]
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a snake in the grid which must start and end at grey circles. The snake is a one-cell-wide path of orthogonally connected cells which may touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally. Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. If the snake passes through box N, then the digit N must be part of the snake in that box. The snake cannot enter any cell touched by a white dot. Finally, the product of the digits along the snake is equal to 600,000.

title: 6 Rules, 4 Clues.  99% Sudoku Beauty!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had this sudoku recommended to us a LOT. 99%Sneaky's puzzle called Six Rules, Four Clues has exactly what you might expect but it combines them in a gorgeous way and grants the solver a stint of pure pleasure.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/wdzu2e0qne

Rules:
1) Normal sudoku rules apply. 2) Digits along the thermometer must increase from the bulb to the tips. 3) Digits along arrows sum to the digit in the attached circle. 4) The digits in the cage sum to the small number printed in the corner. Digits may not repeat in the cage. 5) Along the blue line thick box boarders divide the line into segments with equal sums. When the line re-enters a box a new segment is formed. 6) Cells separated by a knight's move in chess may not contain the same digit.

title: Spot the Song Appearing
description:
Here's where you can have a go at My Favorite Song by Theasylm: https://sudokupad.app/9wm6ctm2hv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits increase from the bulb end. The squares outside the grid indicate the order of the runs of contiguous cells that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number in the square indicates the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but that is not required for runs of different colors. All shaded runs are given.

title: A Step-By-Step Guide To Solving A Mesmerising Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely astonishing return to the channel tonight for grkles in the form of a brand new, 100% rated puzzle called Stepping Stones - which features an original ruleset and a festival of logical joy!!  As the great Qodec wrote, this is "Mesmerising".

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/cj8grmrtes

Rules:
Fill the grid such that each row, column, and orthogonally-connected 9-cell region contains each of the digits 1-9 with no repeats. Region borders must be deduced (though one is given). Clues outside the grid give the sum of the first digit seen in each successive region in that row or column. **The summed digits always appear in increasing order.**

title: When The Sudoku Moriarty Brings His Friends...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A terrifying prospect today in the form of the great zetamath teaming up with his friends to create a puzzle!!  This means the combined IQ devoted to the construction of this sudoku will be prodigious - and it also means the sheer quality in play will be staggering.  Don't watch the football - this is much more fun!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/7fapjms0yv

A colour-blind friendly version of the grid is also available at this link  but you'll need the full version of the rules included below:
https://sudokupad.app/y697kc2umn

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, in this puzzle digits cannot repeat on a line. Digits along a grey line can be broken into non-overlapping segments whose digits sum to ten. Eg 71246 is a valid fill for a length 5 line, because it can be broken into 712 and 46, each of which sum to 10. Along a green line, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Along a blue line, the 3x3 box borders divide the line into segments; each segment’s digits have the same sum. (Different lines can have different sums.) eg r5c2+r4c2 = r3c2+r3c3+r2c3 = r2c4+r2c5+r2c6. The sum of the digits along a line connecting two circles is equal to the sum of the digits in the circles. In this puzzle, digits can't repeat in any of these five cells. Any three adjacent digits along a teal line must include one digit from 147, one from 258, and one from 369. Any three adjacent digits along a peach line must include one digit from 123, one from 456, and one from 789. Along red lines, each pair of adjacent digits must have one even and one odd digit.

title: This Sudoku Is Borderline Genius
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we attempt the fourth puzzle, Borderline, in one of the most epic of sudoku series: Rat Runs by Marty Sears.  The adventures of Finkz continue - this time with blackcurrants and a region sum line - as she attempts to get to the cupcake :)

One renowned setter wrote to us and described this puzzle as "casual perfection".

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/wv8l8x67dy

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze (the path will be a snaking line that passes through the centres of cells, without visiting any cell more than once, crossing itself or passing through any thick maze walls.) Diagonal moves are not possible in this maze. Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given. Finkz may only pass directly through a purple arrow if moving in the direction the arrow is pointing. An arrow always points to the smaller of the two digits it sits between. In this experiment, the correct path will be a valid Region Sum line - ie: box borders (dotted lines) will divide the path into segments which each have the same sum.

title: The Arctic Expedition: A Most Extraordinary Sudoku Grid
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for Cale Schoon who has created one of the most extraordinary grids we've ever seen.  Our job is to find a path for Polly the Polar Bear across the entire arctic tundra, which might sound easy but, Simon claims, isn't!! 

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/28k5j6fvfe

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Create a path to bring Polly the polar bear (r2c2) back to her home in Snow City (r9c9). To explore the entire tundra efficiently, the path must visit each cell in the grid exactly once. The path can only move between orthogonally adjacent cells whose digits differ by 2 or more. Some cells are covered in Unfriendly Ice, which prevents Polly from turning. Her path can only change direction on a cell if it is 'friendly', meaning its digit matches its row, column, or box number. (Boxes are numbered in normal reading order.) Digits separated by a white snowball must be consecutive. Not all possible snowballs are necessarily given.

title: The Most Amazing Sudoku Cell We've Ever Uncovered
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love fog of war sudoku and this one, Lots Of Lavender by gdc, is an INCREDIBLE example of the form.  One cell in particular is so jaw-dropping it will leave you lost for words!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/f5vq2fborp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. No guessing is required. Digits an equal distance to the circled centre of a lavender zipper line sum to the central digit. A digit in a yellow circle counts the number of odd digits on the attached line (including itself and the central cell). A digit in a blue square counts the number of even digits on the attached line (including itself and the central cell). Zipper lines only move orthogonally and don't share cells with other zipper lines.

title: I Heard You Like Cages!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for vitaminz aka Justin Vitanza with a beautiful-looking and beautiful-solving puzzle involving look-and-say cages!  It's called I Heard You Like Cages and it's well worth your time!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/62l02qt79r

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage in the grid is either a killer cage or a “look-and-say” cage (or both), with each to be determined by the solver. Cage colours are purely for decoration. In a killer cage, digits must not repeat and must sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of the cage. In a “Look-and-Say” cage, the number in the top left corner reveals how many of a digit are in that cage. The units place indicates the digit and the tens place indicates exactly how many times that digit appears. Digits may repeat in look-and-say cages if allowed by this and other rules. Example: If a look-and-say cage has the clue "14" then there is exactly one 4 in the cage.

title: Achieving a Stage Victory
description:
Here's where you can play TDF Stage 1 by Palpot: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/d70u447pn4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Two cells connected by a Yellow line must have a difference of at least 4. Two cells connected by a Green line must have a difference of at least 5. Two cells connected by a Red line have a different odd/even parity. The Grey line must be divided into contiguous groups of cells that each sum to 10. These groups of cells cannot overlap. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by X sum to 10. 
Yellow: Earns 1 point for every 5 on its path. Green: Earns 1 point for every 4 or 6 on its path. Red: Earns 1 point for every adjacent pair of consecutive digits along its path. Grey: Earns 1 point for every 3-cell segment that sums to 10 along its path. Yellow beats Green, who beats Red, who beats Grey.

title: The MOST Devious Sudoku Trap!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
So many recommendations to try this puzzle tonight... with one eminent setter describing it as the "most fun they've had solving this year"! The sudoku is called Copycat Collaboration and it's the work of Scojo and some of his streaming friends (including, we understand, Flinty, juggler, palpot, ratfinkz and gdc.)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/j3hwgi98hr

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Place 9 “Copycat Cells” into the grid so that there is exactly one Copycat Cell in each row, column, and 3x3 box. Each Copycat Cell must contain a different digit. The value of a Copycat Cell is the digit in the cell rotationally opposite itself in the grid (180° rotation about the centre of the grid). For example, if r2c3 is a Copycat Cell containing the digit 5, and r8c7 contains the digit 9, the value of r2c3 is the digit in r8c7, which is 9. Values an equal distance from the centre of a lavender line sum to the value in the centre of the line (which is marked with a small circle). A value in a yellow circle counts the number of odd values on the attached line.

title: The Sudoku Rat Returns!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we attempt the third puzzle in one of the most epic of sudoku series, Double Dutch by Marty Sears.  The adventures of Finkz continue - this time with blackcurrants and dutch whisper lines - as she attempts to get to the cupcake :)

As usual, this is about as much joy as you can extract from a 9x9 grid!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/5b1du6ra7d

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path will be a snaking line that passes through the centres of cells, without visiting any cell more than once, crossing itself or passing through any thick maze walls.
As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.
BLACKCURRANTS: Cells connected by a blackcurrant have a 1:2 ratio (one is double the other.) Not all possible blackcurrants have been given.
TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, the correct path will be a valid Dutch Whisper line - ie: adjacent digits along the path must have a difference of at least 4.

title: The Overlapping Sudokus
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight's puzzle has been hailed as a masterpiece.  It's called Full House and it's a collaboration between Michael Lefkowitz and Lulero. There are four interlocked sudokus of different sizes to resolve and the logic involved is quite astonishing. Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
If you're playing on a computer:
https://sudokupad.app/4pqenuxwmn?setting-nogrid=1

If you're playing on a mobile:
https://sudokupad.app/pbz4ij1joh?setting-nogrid=1

Rules:
In each N-by-N grid, normal N-by-N Sudoku rules apply. Overlapping cells contain the same digit eg if r6c8 is a 4 in the 9x9 grid then it is also a 4 in r1c1 of the 6x6 grid. COUNTING CARDS: A digit in a cell with a suit symbol indicates how many times that digit appears in cells with that suit symbol. Eg if r6c5 of the 9x9 grid contains a 6 then exactly 6 diamond cells in the grid must contain a 6.

title: An Extraordinary New Sudoku Rule
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had lots of recommendations to try this sudoku from CaptZebraCakes - it's called Mislabeled Killers and we just want to say that this is a BEAUTIFUL puzzle. The logic is fresh and fascinating and, although it has a 4* rating for difficulty, it's incredibly fun to solve once you cotton on to some of the key ideas.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/ejfmnsdqaf

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage is a “killer cage” where digits cannot repeat.  The two-digit pill in each cage forms a two-digit number when read from left to right, and this two-digit number represents the sum of a different killer cage (i.e. a two-digit pill value cannot be the sum of the cage that contains that pill). title: The "Parker Square" Miracle Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
8 years ago, @numberphile released a video in which Matt Parker (@standupmaths ) talked about his attempt to create a 3x3 magic square made out of different square numbers.  His attempt was christened a "Parker Square" by Brady Haran and has come to be associated with noble failure.
In tonight's video, we attempt to solve Blashyrkh's sudoku, The Parker Miracle - a 6x6 puzzle which Blashyrkh attempted to create with absolutely nothing in the grid but, in the end, needed a single inequality sign.  It's an absolutely extraordinary attempt and features a logical path that it seemed nature intended us to find!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/BTGhbHLhJF

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and outlined box). Boxes are numbered in normal reading order. Orthogonally adjacent digits must not sum to their box number(s). For example, r2c4 and r3c4 must not sum to 2 or 4. Additionally, diagonally adjacent digits within the same box must not sum to their box number. The inequality sign points to the lower digit.

title: Discover The Squares Under The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A glorious return to the channel tonight for the American math teacher RockyRoer whose puzzle, Square Numbered Fog Totals, teaches us some really weird facts about how square numbers interact with sudoku grids!

Tell your friends about this - it's a genuinely fascinating one!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/RJtrMfLmBq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Placing correct digits will remove fog from surrounding cells to reveal more clues. Somewhere in the fog are 9 marked cells - one in every row, column and 3x3 box.  These cells must contain the digits 1-9 once each.  For each marked cell, the sum of ALL the digits in the cells up to and including that marked cell, (top to bottom, left to right, as one might read) must always sum to a square number.
For example, if R4C2 is a marked cell, then the sum of all the digits in row 1, row 2, row 3, R4C1, and R4C2 must be a square number.

description:
