Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits along an orange line must have a difference of at least 4.  Each number in the grid indicates the height of a skyscraper in its cell, a clue outside the grid indicates the number of skyscrapers visible from that direction (where taller skyscrapers block shorter ones from view). Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in that arrows circle, digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules. An inequality symbol between two digits 'points' to the smaller digit. description:
Here's where you can play Kropki Cave by Ben Needham: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/3D64nRR387 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells (walls) such that they form orthogonally connected regions that must touch an edge of the grid. Similarly, leave some cells unshaded (tunnel) to form a single orthogonally connected path, which may not touch itself diagonally and does not branch. No 2x2 area of the grid may be completely shaded or unshaded. Cells marked with a square indicate how many cells (including themselves) they see orthogonally (walls block their view, but they may themselves be walls). White dots indicate consecutive digits along the path (all white dots are shown). Black dots indicate that cells are in a 1:2 ratio within the wall (all black dots are shown). title: Can Our Sudoku Rat Solve The Maze?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This is the second of Marty Sears' series of puzzles in which Finkz the rat must negotiate a maze to find the cupcake!  This is another lovely & clever puzzle and not too tricky (2 out of 5 stars)! We can't wait for the full size version :)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/3xofp0uc0s

Rules:
Normal 8x8 sudoku rules apply; fill the grid with the digits 1-8 so that no digit repeats in a row, column, or marked 4x2 box. 

AIM OF EXPERIMENT: Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path will be a snaking line that passes through the centres of cells, without visiting any cell more than once, crossing itself or passing through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.

TEST CONSTRAINT: In this experiment, any two adjacent cells along the correct path must sum to at least ten.

title: The Viper In The Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Lots of you enjoyed yesterday's Fog Of War sudoku by Oddlyeven so we thought we'd try another one today - but this one is a little harder.  It's called Viper In The Fog and it's by Jolly Rogers.  It features a very original ruleset and some absolutely lovely logic! Enjoy.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/23fMD676d3

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required. Digits in a circle must appear within the four surrounding cells. Draw a single one-cell-wide snake of orthogonally connected cells which begins and ends in Box 4. The snake can touch itself orthogonally and diagonally but must not branch or overlap. Box 'N' must contain 'N' amount of snake cells, and within this Box ‘N’ the digit 'N' must appear on the snake. (Boxes are numbered in normal reading order.) Eg Box 5 must contain exactly 5 snake cells, and one of these snake cells must be the digit 5. Box borders divide the snake into segments which sum to either 1, 5, 10, 15 or 20. Cells which are not part of the snake must be able to orthogonally connect to the grid boundary.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel today for MaizeGator and their sudoku How Far I'll Go, which combines sudoku with the wonderful Nurikabe logic puzzle. This is a very highly rated 3* difficulty construction that is a joy to solve from start to finish.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/rj53fjf9jo

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells blue (“water”), such that all water cells are orthogonally connected, but water may not fully cover a 2x2 area. Shade the remaining cells green, which represent islands. Digits may not repeat within an island. Each island contains exactly one numbered clue, which gives the product of i) the sum of the digits on the island and ii) the size (number of cells) of the island, e.g. an island filled with 346 would have a "39" clue (13x3). A "?" may represent any single, double, or triple-digit number. A cell with an arrow(s) may be land or water, and the digit gives the total number of island cells in the indicated directions combined, not including itself. Not all arrows are given.

title: I Was Challenged To Do This Without A Calculator...!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of those rare (and daunting) sudokus today - a 100% 5* puzzle!  It's called Millstone and it's by James Sinclair.  Many of you have recommended it and claimed that it can be solved without too much maths if you can understand the ideas behind it...  Let's see!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/millstone-v3

Rules:
Fill the grid with the digits 0-9 so that digits do not repeat in a row, column, or 3x3 box, and exactly one cell in each row, column, and box contains two digits. A cell's value is equal to the sum of its digits. A cage's product is equal to the value of each of its cells multiplied together. Each cage's product is consecutive with that of exactly one other cage in the puzzle, and no two cages have the same product. Some cage products are given, others must be deduced. Digits cannot repeat within a cage (but values can). The sum of the values along an arrow is equal to the value in the connected circle. Values in cells with a shaded square must be even.

description:

Place the digits 0-9 once into each row, column, and region. Identical digits may not be separated by a knight's move. The digits 0 and 9 may not be orthogonally or diagonally adjacent to each other or themselves.

title: Predicting the Euros Result ... in Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can try 
UEFA EURO 2024 Opening Game by Arlo Lipof: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/PMbj498TFt 
Today the UEFA EURO 2024 tournament kicks off in Munich. This sudoku is a prediction of the last-minute winning goal for hosts Germany against Scotland in the opening game. In this aerial view the big circles represent five German attacking players, the missing digits being their shirt numbers. The attached arrows show the home team's passing, dribbling and shooting of the ball, from the initial corner kick to the decisive goal. The killer cage represents (the visible part of) Scotland’s goal, the black dot is the Scottish goalkeeper, and the white dots are the Scottish outfield players defending in time added on. 
Rules: Normal sudoku rules apply. In a cage, digits sum to the number shown. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in the attached circle. In this puzzle all circled digits are different. A grey line is a palindrome and reads the same in both directions. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.

title: The Rat Race by Marty Sears
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most original and witty setters in the whole world of sudoku is Marty Sears who has now invented another new type of puzzle!  It involves finding a route for our pet rat (Finkz) through the maze to the cupcake!!  This is a lovely & clever puzzle and not too tricky (2 out of 5 stars)!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/iu50qghplg

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.

AIM OF EXPERIMENT: 
Finkz the rat must reach the cupcake by finding a path through the maze. The path will be a snaking line that passes through the centres of cells, without visiting any cell more than once, crossing itself or passing through any thick maze walls. As well as moving orthogonally, Finkz may move diagonally if there's a 2x2 space in which to do so, but may never pass diagonally through the rounded end / corner of a wall.

TEST CONSTRAINT:
In this experiment, any two adjacent cells along the correct path must sum to a prime number. Also, ALL digits within a marked 3x2 sudoku box that lie anywhere on the correct path must sum to a prime number too.

title: Sometimes you have to Know when to Start Again
description:
Here's where you can try Snake Farm by Cris Moore: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/ot5h01fnjr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is divided into 9 snakes. Each snake is a path of length 9, starting at its tail in the southwest and moving orthogonally north or east — never west or south — to its head in the northeast. Three heads (red diamonds) and two tails (green squares) are shown, pointing to the next cell in that snake.
Digits in a snake cannot repeat. The snake that contains the blue dot is a thermosnake, with digits increasing from its tail to its head. Adjacent digits connected by a dot differ by 1 if the dot is white, and have a ratio of 1:2 if the dot is black.

title: Would You Wish THIS Man A Happy Birthday?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
PjotrV has made Simon a sudoku for his birthday!  And it's a really good puzzle!  Huge thanks to Peter for such a kind thought.  The puzzle is based on a clever physical calendar called A-Puzzle-A-Day so check out the pictures in the video if you want to understand the background.

Thanks also to all those of you who wrote in with birthday wishes and indeed puzzles.  It means a lot.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/czke3g17fr

Here is the original link that Simon opened (which includes useful pictures about A-Puzzle-A-Day!):
https://amgine.nl/puzzles/Happy_Birthday_Simon.pdf

Rules:
"Place the digits 1-7 exactly once in every row and column. Place 8 polyominoes (an L pentomino, an N pentomino, a P pentomino, a U pentomino, a V pentomino, a Y pentomino, a Z pentomino and a 2x3 rectangle) exactly once in such a way that only the cells with grey text in them are not covered by one of the shapes (ie the "8", the "Jun" and 6 cells with "X" in them), so the grid spells out 8 June (Simon's Birthday). The polyominoes can be reflected and rotated as required. Each cage is part of a polyomino and no polyomino can have more than one cage. This cage can be anywhere in the polyomino. The small number in the top left of the cage gives the sum of the digits of that polyomino and digits can't repeat within a polyomino. The digits along the pointed diagonal sum to 45.
There are some cells with oddballs in the puzzle, which have odd digits in it. These are put in, because Simon is a bit of an oddball, in the most positive way: an eccentric and exceptional character.

Now enjoy your puzzle and your chocolate cake with iced frosting on it and the best to you! Peter"

title: I Would Rate This Sudoku 100%
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears has done it again.  This puzzle, Counting Calories, is another masterpiece.  The logic from start to finish is breathtakingly clever and satisfying... please have a go at this one, it comes with Simon's rating of 100%!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/meq4crszcg

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into yellow regions and brown regions. Each region must consist of orthogonally connected cells, and two regions of the same colour may not share an orthogonal edge. Brown regions (chocolate bars) must be rectangular or square. Yellows regions (bananas) must NOT be square / rectangular. Digits may repeat within regions. A digit in a banana cell indicates exactly how many banana cells contain that digit. A digit in a brown diamond belongs to a chocolate bar and indicates the size of that chocolate bar. Every chocolate bar has a different size. A digit on an arrow cell indicates the total sum of the closest (neighbouring) cells in each of the indicated directions.

description:
*** BRAID STREAM AT 10PM TONIGHT UK TIME ***
You can watch us streaming this evening at this link:

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Many of our viewers request that we do the occasional non-sudoku puzzle - something we're only to happy to try every now and again (let us know what you think!) So tonight we try a recent puzzle by KNT called Pentomino Yajilin, which is incredibly highly thought of.  The denouement of this one is ridiculous... can you discover it?

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/QMQdFfF9Fg

Rules:
Draw a loop that moves orthogonally between cells and does not visit any cell more than once. Cells containing clues must not be visited by the loop. Every other unvisited cell (i.e. those that do not contain clues) must belong to a pentomino - areas of five orthogonally connected cells. No pentomino shape may repeat and they must not touch each other, not even diagonally.  (A rotation or reflection of a pentomino should be treated as a repeat of that pentomino and therefore not allowed.) Not all of the 12 possible pentomino shapes are necessarily used. A clue specifies the number of cells belonging to pentominoes in the indicated direction.

To make the "answer check" function work, enter the digit 8 in every cell that contains a pentomino.

title: A Total Eclipse of the Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can try Eclipsed Whispers by Space_man: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/2lfn0sf0o6 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a loop of orthogonally connected cells (the sun loop) and a loop of diagonally connected cells (the moon loop). Each loop is one-cell-wide and may not intersect itself or touch itself orthogonally (but may touch itself diagonally). Both loops act as German Whispers lines: adjacent digits on the loop must differ by at least 5.
Every location where the two loops intersect is marked with a sun or moon. A sun indicates that the digit on the moon loop is eclipsed (hidden) by the digit on the sun loop, and a moon indicates that the sun digit is eclipsed by the moon digit. An eclipsed digit must be from 1-9 and strictly lower than the visible digit. Digits separated by the white dot are consecutive.

title: The Arkenstone: The Sudoku Quest
description:
*** THE LORD OF THE RINGS SUDOKU HUNT TODAY ***
At 4pm UK time this afternoon we launched the sudoku event of the summer.  Blobz' puzzles and Ted Nasmith artistry combined in one of the most beautiful, approachable and fun hunts we've ever published.  Get hyped!!! Teaser puzzle here:

https://sudokupad.app/blobz/a-long-expected-party

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
To celebrate the release of our new June reward on Patreon, The Lord Of The Rings sudoku hunt by Blobz, tonight we're attempting Blobz' sudoku, The Arkenstone - based on the previous Tolkien book, The Hobbit!

We know the ruleset for this one is a bit tricky but stick with it and read the rules carefully - the puzzle is excellent. 

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/blobz/the-arkenstone

Rules:
Bilbo Bobbins is on a quest to, uh, "procure" the Arkenstone (R5C5) that sits in Dragon Snyder's Lair (a 2x2 region in box 5) under Logic Mountain. 

R9C1 marks the entrance to the Whispering Tunnels: an orthogonally connected region leading to the lair. Adjacent digits along the tunnels (and deadends) differ by at least 5. The path from start to lair (ignoring deadends) is 26 cells. 

With Arkenstone acquired, Bilbo must escape through the Modular Passage, that begins on the opposite side of the lair and leads to a secret door exiting the mountain (R5C9). Every set of three digits along this passage (which does not branch) must contain one each from the sets {1,4,7}, {2,5,8}, and {3,6,9}. The total sum of digits along this "Secret" passage is 45. 

Normal sudoku rules apply. 

Shade some cells ("walls") and leave others unshaded ("tunnels", "lair", "passage") such that no 2x2 region (except the lair) is fully shaded or unshaded. Also, there are no "checkerboard" patterns of shaded/unshaded cells, i.e. the unshaded region does not touch itself diagonally. All wall cells must be in orthogonally connected groups with at least one cell at the grid's edge. All caged cells are either tunnel or passage. 

The digit in the cage, plus its modifier, indicates how many unshaded cells (including itself) can be seen orthogonally from that position (walls block sight). E.g., if a cage contains a 7 and has a "-2" modifier, then that cell can "see" 5 unshaded cells total (including itself).

title: Where Does it All End Anyway?
description:
Here is the link (and ALL the rules) to: Where Does it All End? by apetersen: https://sudokupad.app/lc3vr050ng 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Correctly entered digits remove fog in surrounding cells. Cells with a grey square contain an even digit. Each line has a distinct color. Lines do not branch or cross and only move orthogonally. All lines have a length of 3 or more. The box location of each line's ends determine its type(s):
1: Ten Line
2: Renban
3: German Whisper
4: Same Difference
5: Between
6: Modular
7: Nabner
8: Region Sum
9: Entropic
e.g. yellow has one end at r3c5 and the other at r7c5. It is both Renban (box 2) and Region Sum (box 8).
Ten Line: The line can be broken into segments such that each sums to 10.
Renban: The line contains a set of non-repeating consecutive digits, in any order.
German Whisper: Adjacent digits along this line must differ by at least 5.
Same Difference: Adjacent digits along this line have the same difference for all pairs.
Between: All other digits along the line have values that fall strictly between those of the ends.
Modular: Every group of 3 consecutive cells along the line contains a full set of remainders modulo 3: one from (1,4,7), one from (2,5,8), and one from (3,6,9).
Nabner: None of the digits on the line repeat, nor are consecutive with any other digit along the line.
Region Sum: Box borders break the line into segments with the same sum.
Entropic: Every group of 3 consecutive cells along the line must contain a low (1,2,3), mid (4,5,6), and high (7,8,9) digit.

title: Zippery When Wet by Marty Sears: A Sudoku Masterpiece
description:
*** THE LORD OF THE RINGS SUDOKU HUNT TOMORROW ***
At 4pm UK time tomorrow we launch the sudoku event of the summer.  Blobz' puzzles and Ted Nasmith artistry combined in one of the most beautiful, approachable and fun hunts we've ever published.  Get hyped!!! Teaser puzzle here:

https://sudokupad.app/blobz/a-long-expected-party

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Happy 40th Birthday Marty Sears!  We've had so many folk write in to wish you many happy returns and request we do THIS puzzle to celebrate your big day... So we have!!

This has one of the longest rulesets we've ever featured but, just occasionally, a lengthy ruleset is justified by the sheer quality of the resultant sudoku and this is one of those occasions.  A masterpiece.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/7kov2n4lrz

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cell is either land or water. All cells of the same type must be orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be entirely land or entirely water. 

Line Types:
 - Renban (pink) - Digits on a pink line don't repeat, and form a consecutive sequence, but these can be arranged in any order along the line.
 - Nabner (yellow) - A digit on a yellow line cannot be consecutive with (or the same as) any other digit anywhere on the line.
 - German Whisper (green) - Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of at least 5.
 - Region Sum (blue) - Digits along a blue line must have the same total within each 3x3 box.
 - Parity (red) - Digits along a red line must alternate between odd and even.
 - Entropic (orange) - Any group of 3 adjacent digits on an orange line must contain a low digit (1, 2 or 3), a medium digit (4, 5 or 6), and a high digit (7, 8 or 9).
 - Palindrome (grey) - A grey line must read the same in either direction.
 - Same Difference (turquoise) - Each pair of adjacent digits along a turquoise line must have the same difference.

ZIPPERY WHEN WET:
• Any line that is completely wet (only enters water cells) loses the property of its presenting colour, and instead becomes a zipper line. Along a zipper line, each pair of digits that are the same distance from the line's central cell, sum to the digit in that centre cell.
• Any line that is completely dry (only enters land cells) behaves normally, as described in the list above. It does not behave like a zipper line.
• If a line is partly dry and partly wet, it retains its presenting property, but it is ALSO a zipper line as well.

title: This Fog Sudoku Is Genius.
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
IcyFruit returns to the channel today with a fog-of-war sudoku of quite astonishing brilliance.  It's hard to imagine how the fog mechanic could be used better than this - the only we don't understand about the puzzle now is the name!?

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/qvjh329nc0

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Placing a correct digit will clear the fog from the neighbouring cells.  Guessing is not required. Lines travel orthogonally or diagonally through the centres of cells. They do not branch and do not cross themselves or each other. All given lines are a different colour. A grey dot may hide part of a line. Lines are “region-subset lines” ie The 3x3 box borders divide lines into segments. If a digit appears in a segment of length N, it must appear in all segments of length N or greater on that line. All lines have at least two segments. In addition, a digit on a line indicates the number of times that digit appears on that line.

The puzzle Simon mentions during the intro that viewers might like to think about in terms of the "3rd secret of Yin Yang" is here:

title: The Newest Form Of Chess
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had this older gdc puzzle recommended and, it turns out, with good reason.  This is a brilliant hybrid of chess and sudoku where you have to imagine the chess pieces dancing over your number pads!  Bravo to gdc for including a line for every chess piece too!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/b193jegg4x

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a line must form a valid chess move by the indicated piece on a 3x3 numpad. For example, a 1 on a knight line may only have the numbers 6 and 8 next to it so 6-1-8-1 would be valid. Pawns can only move exactly one cell up or one cell down, so 2-5-8-5 would be a valid pawn line.

description:
Here's where you can try ±1 by Math Pesto: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/6guvv1za0z 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Values along a purple line comprise a set of non-repeating, consecutive numbers (in any order). A black dot joins two values in a 1:2 ratio. 
There is exactly one 'knapp daneben' cell in each row, column, and box. A digit in a knapp daneben cell has its value either increased or decreased by exactly 1 (e.g. a 3 becomes either 2 or 4). Each digit appears in a knapp daneben cell exactly once. (However, it is permissible for two digits to become modified to the same value, such as both 5 and 7 becoming 6.)

title: The Colour Wheel
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for The Book Wyrm and their puzzle Colour Wheel, which was apparently constructed in just 90 minutes.  This will seem utterly extraordinary when you see the logic required in this one - it is original and brilliant (and not that easy!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/bBR8Rj8Ng7

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not repeat. Sum all the digits in a cage and then colour each cage according to the last digit of its sum (i.e. cages that sum to values with the same last digit are the same colour, and cages that sum to values with a different last digit are different colours). Numbers in the top left corner of a cage (“Cage X”) give the sum of all orthogonally-adjacent cages of different colours to Cage X. Every digit, except the digit in the central cell (r5c5), has a 'partner digit' that is always placed 180° rotationally symmetrical to it, seen from the centre of the grid. Which digits are paired up must be deduced by the solver. (Example: If the digits 1 and 2 turned out to be a rotational pair, and r2c4 is a 1, r8c6 must be a 2.)

title: Mercy Snakes Alive!
description:
Here's where you can attempt Diagonal Snakes by Monkey Apprentice: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/QFgMQf2NpF 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Create two non-overlapping, non-crossing snakes connecting the colored cells (i.e. one snake connecting the purple cells and one snake connecting the green cells). The snakes move horizontally or vertically, and may not touch themselves, even diagonally, but they may touch each other. One snake contains either all high digits (6,7,8,9) or all low digits (1,2,3,4), and the other all odd digits or all even digits. No snake may enter a cell with a gray circle. A digit in a gray circle is odd. Digits separated by an “X” sum to 10; digits separated by a “V” sum to 5. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive; digits separated by a black dot have a 2:1 ratio. Digits cannot repeat along the negative diagonal.

title: Fakes In The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Two of the most enjoyable things in the world of sudoku: fog of war AND Marty Sears!  These two things combine tonight in a puzzle full of the cleverness and panache that we've come to expect from one of the most original setters out there.  The title of this video could have been 'An Hour Of Being Made To Feel Stupid And Yet Loving Every Second Of It!"

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/x56ymej4lq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Enter correct digits to clear fog. No guessing is necessary. In every row, column and box, there is exactly one 'pseudo cell'. The digits 1-9 each appear once in a pseudo cell. The real value of a pseudo cell is calculated by adding its row number to its column number. Eg: if there is a pseudo cell in r8c5, it has the value of 13, regardless of which digit is in that cell. On a lavender 'zipper' line, the values of any pair of cells that are an equal distance from the central spot  always sum to the value on that central spot. On a turquoise 'same difference' line, the values of adjacent cells always have the same difference (but this difference may be different for different turquoise lines.) Values joined by a V sum to 5.

title: Mathematicians Will Not be Able to Cope with This!
description:
Watch out for 1 being considered 'prime' here! This is where you can play P is for Prime by Chaos is Inevitable: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/H66NhnG9mm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on the red line differ by at least 5. The amount of times a number is shown on the red line must be a prime number. Digits cannot repeat in a cage. A cage either contains only prime numbers and sums to a non-prime, or contains no prime numbers, but sums to a prime number, eg. 2 and 5 in a 2-cell cage is not possible since the numbers are prime AND it sums to a prime. IN THIS PUZZLE, 1 counts as prime, so the ‘prime’ set is 1/2/3/5/7.

title: The Art Of Puzzles
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
gmpuzzles.com is about to start a new season of puzzles and they've sent us this Snake Egg/Star Battle hybrid by JinHoo Ahn to have a go at!  This is a PHENOMENAL miracle of a grid - just three dots is all you get.  The logic feels like magic when you find it.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/Tqfg9qNd2L

Rules:
Draw a snake (a 1-cell-wide path) in the grid. The snake can touch itself diagonally, but cannot touch itself orthogonally or revisit any square. The grid already  provides some of these diagonal touching points (as grey circles).  The remaining cells (not occupied by the snake) must then form a 'Star Battle puzzle' ie there must be two stars in every row, column, and region divided by the snake's body. Stars cannot be  placed in adjacent cells that share an edge OR a corner. (For answer check to work, use a 1 in a cell with a star.)

You can find out more about gmpuzzles.com here:
https://www.gmpuzzles.com/blog/2024/05/season-3-free-preview-week/

title: These Sudoku Rules... They're Mad!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
KNT is a constructor of such extreme intellect that any sensible solver approaches their puzzles with a sense of awe and fear!  So when one is "only" rated of average difficulty it represents a chance for us mere mortals to visit, if only briefly, the brain of a mastermind.  Oh and this one has mad rules... did we mention that?! 

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/jgdFdqhmn2

Rules:
Place the digits from 1 to 6 exactly once in every row, column, and region. The regions are orthogonally OR diagonally connected and must be located by the solver. A number in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits in the orthogonally connected section of the region that cell belongs to. A cell with a red X in the bottom right corner indicates the size (ie the number of cells) of the orthogonally connected section of the region that cell belongs to. All possible size clues (red Xs) are given.

title: A Miracle Sudoku For A Little Miracle
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have featured many puzzles by the maths professor Dorlir and today it is his daughter's 7th birthday!  He has made a special miracle sudoku to celebrate so we thought it would be a nice puzzle to have a go at in today's video. This is an astonishing piece of work (how did he have the idea??!) and, although not easy, showcases some stunning logic. Bravo Dorlir and a very happy birthday to your daughter!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/zos75s0s5z

Rules:
Fill the grid with eight non-overlapping 2x4 regions oriented horizontally (i.e. 2 rows and 4 columns), such that each region contains the digits from 1 to 8 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions don't contain digits. Draw a single one-cell-wide loop in the grid that travels orthogonally, doesn't branch, and isn't allowed to touch itself, not even diagonally, and doesn't pass through any of the empty cells. Any two adjacent cells along this loop must include one extreme digit [1,2,7,8] and one medium digit [3,4,5,6]. For each region N, the digit N must be on the loop within this region. (Regions are numbered in reading order, based on the position of their top left cell, i.e. a region with its top left cell further down in the grid than another region will have the higher region number. If two regions have their top left cell in the same row, the region on the right will have the higher region number.) Digits along marked diagonals sum to the number indicated outside the grid.

The BBC radio programme Simon mentions in the introduction is called Just One Thing and the episode in question is available here:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/m001z6pb

Simon reads Kubla Khan by Samuel Taylor Coleridge at the end of tonight's video.

title: No GUESSING Is Necessary In The Sudoku Fog
description:
*** STREAMING TONIGHT ***
Just a reminder, we're streaming more Dungeons & Diagrams tonight at 10pm UK time.  You can watch at the following link:

https://youtube.com/live/v-HZKdVvnoQ

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love Fog-Of-War sudokus and today we get to try Oddlyeven's Foggy Nonsense, a lovely example of the form in which we need to use the digits 0-8!  Don't forget, the constructor will have designed the puzzle such that guessing is not required or intended so try to solve it by logic alone!
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/lvxh3flv0i

Rules:
Place the digits 0 to 8 once each in every row, column and 3x3 box. One cell in every row, column and box is a “doubler”. This cell counts as double its value for the rules below. Each of the digits 0 to 8 appears exactly once in a doubler cell. Values on an X sum to 10. Values on a V sum to 5. Digits in a cage may not repeat. Values in a cage sum to the total in the top-left most corner of the cage. The grid is partially covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells. Guessing is not necessary.

title: Some Super Smashing Symmetry!
description:
Here's where you can try Tenet by Jazzora: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/8d4q3NdNLR 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are no repeated digits on a marked diagonal or within a coloured region. Two cells joined by a V or an X sum to 5 (V) or 10 (X). Two cells joined by a white dot have a difference of 1. Two cells joined by a purple dot have a ratio of the number written in the purple dot. A cell with a circle contains an odd digit, and a cell with a square an even digit. 

 It takes between 15 and 20 minutes to complete Kathrin Bohnet's master's thesis survey. The survey is anonymous and no data can be traced back. The data collected is used exclusively for scientific research purposes:

title: Team Phistomefel vs Team Simon
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Phistomefel's latest sudoku features a completely original ruleset and is, as we've come to expect, now THE quintessential puzzle to showcase these new bizarre rules! The whole thing is fascinating - you have to split the nine sudoku digits into teams and then make the clues work :) 
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/21xzz0q3gd

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the digits from 1 to 9 into two teams such that every digit from 1 to 9 is in exactly one of the two teams. Thereby, the finished grid has areas (of orthogonally connected cells) which contain only digits from one team and are bounded by digits of the other team and/or the border of the grid. A number clue gives the sum of all the digits in such an area. Digits may repeat in such an area and the sum clues are in an arbitrary position within the area. Each area has at most one clue, but may also have none at all.

Jane Street's Bug Bytes puzzle is available here:
https://www.janestreet.com/bug-byte/

description:

title: How Easy Is It To Add Numbers To 10?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Today we return to the world of zetamath whose puzzle, Zag, we somehow haven't featured yet.  This is a VERY nice sudoku combining arrows and ten-lines in innovative ways.  Two of the arrows in this puzzle would stand a chance of being on the podium in the Arrow Olympics!
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/LJqq7g8d8d

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the orange line must be broken into one or more contiguous groups of cells that each sum to ten. Such groups cannot overlap. Digits may repeat within such sums if allowed by other rules. For example, 513173 is a valid fill for a length 6 line, because it can be broken into 5131 and 73, each of which sum to 10. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.

title: The Genius Equation
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
ThePedallingPianist is quite quite mad.  But also a genius.  This 100%-rated 6x6 puzzle is both fascinating and incredible.  A complete one-off from one of the most original minds in sudoku.
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/eep49o4qx6

Rules:
Normal 6x6 sudoku rules apply. (Place the digits 1 to 6, once each, in every row, column and region). 
Yin Yang: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area, as do all unshaded cells, and no 2x2 area is entirely shaded or unshaded.
Counting Yin Yang: A digit in a shaded cell shows how many times that digit appears in shaded cells.
Quadruples: A digit in a circle must appear in the surrounding 4 cells. If a digit appears twice in a circle, it must appear twice in the surrounding 4 cells.

title: Use Cluedoku Skills to Find the Killer!
description:
Here's where you can try Pseudo Cluedo by Marty Sears: https://sudokupad.app/el9sus7p0o 
A murder has been committed in Grid Mansion! Dr Awkward has been found dead, and there are six suspects. Can you work out who did it? Normal sudoku rules apply: place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 3x3 room.
FIND YOUR PATH:
• Draw a line passing through the centres of some cells to represent your journey from room to room, as you interrogate suspects and look for clues.
• Your path must start at one of the lettered cells (these are initials labelling the six suspects and the victim.) The path must finish at another lettered cell, and visit all the other lettered cells along the way. 
• Your path may move orthogonally or diagonally between cells, but may not cross itself.
• You may not pass through a thick black wall; you can only get from room to room by travelling through the CENTRE of a doorway. For some doorways this may mean you have to go through diagonally.
• The value of digits along your path must constantly increase or stay the same (like a slow thermometer). You must never move from a higher value to a lower value.
PSEUDO CELLS:
• Every row, column and room has exactly one 'pseudo cell'. These 9 pseudo cells contain the digits 1-9 once each.• For the purposes of your path, and for the weapon, victim and suspect rules below, the value of a pseudo cell equals its room number (regardless of which digit appears in the cell.) Rooms are numbered from 1-9 in reading order. Eg: room 1 is in the top left, room 7 is in the bottom left.
WEAPONS:
• Some weapons have been found, at locations marked by an X. The values of the two cells separated by a weapon sum to 10.
THE VICTIM:
• Dr Awkward's body was found lying awkwardly in the doorway between rooms 4 and 7. This has been marked by a white outline. All that's known about the victim is that the values of his cells form a palindrome, reading the same from either end.
THE SUSPECTS:
• Digits do not repeat in a killer cage (although their values might.) Each suspect has a particular trait:
• Miss Parity (red) - values of orthogonally adjacent cell have a different parity (one is odd, the other is even).
• Mrs Summer (blue) - a doorway divides her cells into two distinct groups, whose values both have the same sum.
• Miss Tenclumpz - (white) - her cells can be divided into smaller distinct groups of orthogonally connected cells, each of which sum to 10.
• Colonel Nabner (yellow) - none of his cell's values are consecutive with (or the same as) each other.
• Professor Zipworthy (purple) - cells an equal distance from his central spot sum to the digit on his central spot.
• The Whispering Reverend (green) - adjacent cells must have values with a difference of at least 5.
One particular digit (not value) appears in all of the suspects' cages, except for the real killer. Who is it?

title: A Sudoku Catastrophe
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have been alerted of a potential sudoku catastrophe.  We've never featured a puzzle from by the constructor Meggen033 and it's something that some of you know we need to put right!  So tonight we're trying their One-Fog-Nine sudoku - a 159 puzzle mixed with a little dose of fog!  And it's a really nice debut (and fairly approachable we'd say!).
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/wyqe8cjb01

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each digit in column 1 indexes the 1 in its row (eg if R3C1=4 then 1 must appear in the fourth column of that row ie R3C4=1).  The same rule applies to column 5 digits indexing 5 in its row, and column 9 digits indexing 9 in its row. The digits in a cage must sum to the small clue in the cage’s top left corner. Digits may not repeat within a cage. A black dot between cells indicates cell values with a 2:1 ratio (ie one digit is double the other). ALL BLACK DOTS ARE SHOWN. The grid is partially covered with fog. Correctly placed digits will clear the fog around that cell. No guessing is required.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The wonderful James Sinclair returns tonight with his latest puzzle, Quadrilateral.  Unsurprisingly it's a magnificent sudoku and serendipitously seems to result in Eva Green making an appearance during the solve!
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/quadrilateral

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Purple “renban” lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order. Gold “nabner” lines contain a non-repeating set of digits, and no two digits on the same line can be consecutive (regardless of their position on the line). Along orange “entropic” lines, every set of three adjacent cells must contain one low digit (1-3), one middle digit (4-6), and one high digit (7-9). Digits in cells separated by an X sum to 10. Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even.

Jane Street's Bug Bytes puzzle is available here:

title: Amazing New Rules = Amazing New Puzzle
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new constructor, Jolly Rogers, has created a really remarkable ruleset based around introducing more squares to the sudoku grid (there clearly aren't enough already!) The upshot is a sudoku that has several distinct parts to the solve - all of which are really interesting!
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/7FngrT9ftq

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Divide the grid into non-overlapping square-shaped regions. The sum of a square's four corner cells must be divisible by the number of cells that square contains. E.g the sum of the corners for a 3x3 square must be divisible by 9. Every cell must belong to a square and a 1x1 square region is not valid. The cell containing a red circle cannot be a corner of any square region. Orthogonally adjacent cells separated by a square region border must have the same parity (odd or even). Square region borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Each line must be divided at least once.

title: The Hardest Version Of TETRIS (Phistomefel)
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Phistomefel is setting sudokus again and Simon tackles his newest puzzle: Stostone Cold, a crazy variation of Tetris!  What can we say except this is everything we've come to love from one of THE most brilliant minds. Oh yeah, it's not absolutely straightforward to solve...  we should probably add that.
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/a21fmb469t

Rules:
Fill the cells with the digits 1 to 8 such that each digit appears exactly once in every row, column and region. A region is a collection of eight orthogonally connected cells. Determining the shape of the regions is part of the puzzle. Each region has exactly one clue which is a small number in the upper left corner of some cell in that region (not necessarily the top left cell). Shade some cells such that: a) no orthogonally neighboring cells are shaded across a region boundary; b) all shaded cells within a region are orthogonally connected; an c) the digits in all shaded cells within a region sum to the region's clue. If all of the shaded groups were to fall straight down without changing shape, they must completely fill the bottom half of the grid.

title: What Is "Snake Egg Sudoku"?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
To celebrate our new competition on Patreon, we're tackling a Snake Egg sudoku here by none other than Glum Hippo - the master constructor of this form! 

[The version Simon plays in the video has slightly differently worded rules to the version below.  We tried to clarify them to make them as clear as possible.]
 
Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/pqttdq9MbQ

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake (a one-cell wide path) into the grid which does not touch itself orthogonally. Areas not covered by the snake form 8 separate regions, one of each size 1-8 ('eggs') which, in turn, may touch one another diagonally but not orthogonally. Adjacent cells on a green line must contain one snake cell and one egg cell AND these cells’ digits must differ in value by at least 5. If a circle is in an egg, it gives the count of cells in the egg. If a circle is on the snake, it gives the number of snake cells “seen” by that circle, including itself (ie the number of contiguous snake cells extending horizontally and vertically from that cell, including itself).

*** NEW SUDOKU HUNT ON PATREON ***
We're delighted to share with you a brand new sudoku hunt themed around snake egg puzzles by Glum Hippo.  If you've never tried snake egg logic puzzles before, prepare for serious fun - these sudokus are outstanding!  Finish by May 20 to enter the competition!

description:
Here's where you can play La PrimeAvera by Kothornos: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/kgozp9smu9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along the indicated diagonal, digits do not repeat. Black dots indicate that cells are in a 2:1 ratio. Numbers outside the grid indicate the sum of the cells in the direction of the arrow. In cages, the number in the top left denotes the sum of the cells in that cage. Digits cannot repeat in cages. A given cage can only contain prime numbers, or it can only contain non-prime numbers. For instance, a single cage can contain 2,3,7, since they are all prime, but it cannot contain 1,2,3,7 since 1 is not prime but 2,3,7 are prime.

title: "One Of The Best Puzzles I Ever Solved": WARNING: VERY Hard!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We had a really lovely email from Jakhob telling us about his friend (with whom he constructs puzzles) wooferzfg's birthday and requesting we take a look at Loop Nurikabe, a puzzle they are so proud of they made a fridge magnet of it!

This puzzle has a 100% rating but very few people have managed to solve it in nearly a year.  (One of our testers spent HOURS on it and couldn't finish.) Simon decided to give it a go and started early this morning...  it was a good job he didn't start later!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/ay00mqlwli

Rules:
Every cell is either water or land. All water cells must be orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area may be entirely water. Groups of orthogonally-connected land cells form islands, which do not touch orthogonally, but may touch diagonally. Draw a non-intersecting loop through the centres of some cells which passes through each island exactly once. The loop may only visit one cell in each island. If a clue is on a land cell, it indicates the size of its island. Every island must contain exactly one clue. If a clue is on a water cell then the loop must pass through that cell and the clue indicates how many water cells are visited by the loop between the previous island and the next island. Every water section of the loop must pass through exactly one clue. A '?' can represent any non-zero value.

Note that, to check whether you have the correct solution, either compare your solution to Simon's in the video (which is correct) or play the puzzle in Penpa at the link below (which has an inbuilt answer check function for loops!):

https://tinyurl.com/2yzxfbkl

title: Is This A Genuine Miracle?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
What an extraordinary sudoku we have for you today. It's called Miracle Once Again and it's by Sumanta Mukherjee.  Sumanta has actually discovered a puzzle (which starts with a completely blank grid) where just a paragraph of rules can lead to a unique solution.  It's a really beautiful experience to solve this one.  Enjoy!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/NbqQ2HhP4P

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. (ie place the digits 1-9, once each, in every row, column & 3x3 box). A digit in a circle indicates how many circles contain that digit. Place some circles in the grid such that a box “m” contains exactly “m” number of circles. (Boxes are numbered in normal reading order so the top left box of the grid is box 1, the bottom right box is box 9, etc).  ie Box 1 should have 1 circle; box 3 should have 3 circles; etc. If a cell, eg R1C1, contains a circle then all the cells beneath it in the grid (8 cells in this case) must contain circles. No two 9s in the grid can be separated by a single Chess King’s or single Chess Knight’s move; but every 9 must share a diagonal with at least one other 9.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Prime digits (2,3,5,7) must NOT be orthogonally adjacent to each other. title: The Return Of A Sudoku Legend
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The sudoku world has missed one of its giants but we're delighted to see a new puzzle from the great Jay Dyer.  It's called Cave Of Killers and it's just wonderful.  

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/aem1ckhlvc

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shade some cells so that the unshaded cells form a single orthogonally connected area, and each connected shaded region touches the grid boundary. A circle is always unshaded, and the digit in the circle equals the number of unshaded cells visible in a straight line from that cell, including the cell itself. Shaded cells obstruct the view. Each shaded region contains a corner clue which equals the sum of the digits in that region. Digits may not repeat in a shaded region, and the digit in the clued cell equals the size of the region.

title: "Octopus Rules Apply"!!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
[Simon recorded this video on his laptop and we're aware that the video quality drops in the last 15 minutes.  Apologies.  It would have been awful to have to junk it given the quality of the puzzle.  Things should be back to normal tomorrow.]

Happy Birthday ThePedallingPianist - who returns to the channel with an absolutely extraordinary sudoku tonight called Killer Octopus.  It is absolutely remarkable that this has a unique solution and the logic is extremely original.  He shouldn't really be giving us presents on his birthday but it seems he has!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/d7siz7tehr

Or with added Octopus graphics:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/seisxtsh0f

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage must sum to the given total. Octopus rules apply. I.e. draw 4 lines that must each: i) not cross or overlap anywhere except r5c5, where they all intersect; ii) have 180-degree rotational symmetry around r5c5; iii) visit exactly 2 cells on the edge of the grid, which are the beginning and end of the line; and iv) all be the same length (in number of cells passed through). The 4 lines are "Same Difference" lines. I.e pairs of adjacent digits on a line must all have the same difference, though this difference may be different for different lines.

*** NEW SANDRA & NALA FOG PACK ***

title: The Miracle Snake
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A collaboration today featuring two absolutely top-tier setters: Nordy and yttrio (who set at Nordyttrio!).  It's called Earth Wurm and it really is astonishing that just four squares and two circles is enough to specify a unique solution.  It's a blast to solve too so do give this one a go if you can!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/lbvymeu3as

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Construct a one-cell-wide snake of orthogonally-connected cells whose two endpoints are given as circles. The snake cannot branch and cannot touch itself orthogonally, but may touch itself diagonally. Additionally: All squares are on the snake; a digit in a square gives the number of snake cells seen in all horizontal/vertical directions combined, including the cell with the square - non-snake cells block the vision; the snake acts as a “German Whisper” line ie adjacent digits on the snake must have a difference of at least 5.

title: How will Anybody Know we were Here?
description:
Here's where you can pit your wits against Now the People Will Know We Were Here by ViKingPrime: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/7m8l0f0m4a 
Normal sudoku rules apply. White dots separate two cells containing consecutive values; Black dots separate two cells where one value is double the other [1:2]. Values along a purple Renban line form a set of consecutive, non-repeating values in any order. Values along a yellow Nabner line form a set of non-consecutive, non-repeating values in any order (e.g. if a cell of value 3 appears on a Nabner line, then values of 2 and 4 cannot appear).
There are 9 Hot cells contained within the grid comprising a set of the digits from 1 to 9. Each row, column and box contains exactly one Hot cell. There are nine 9 Cold cells contained within the grid following the same rules as the Hot cells. A cell may have only one of these roles. Hot cells increase the value of the contained digit by 1. Cold cells decrease the value of the contained digit by 1.

title: Fully Booked And Yet Magnificent
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've had loads of recommendations to have a crack at this logic puzzle (not sudoku!) - it's called Fully Booked and it's by MicroStudy.  It's a quite lovely mash-up of Fillomino and Numbered Rooms that is interesting from start to finish.  

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/10mumnjiuu

Rules:
The entire grid is comprised of an inner 9x9 grid and the areas (of non-black cells) where outside clues are to be placed by the solver. Divide the entire grid into regions of orthogonally-connected cells such that no two regions of the same size share an edge. Enter a number into each cell equal to the size of its region (ie the number of cells it contains). Regions can contain cells from both the inner 9x9 grid and the outside area. Numbers outside the 9x9 grid are valid “Numbered Rooms” clues. Ie A clue indicates the number that appears in the Nth cell of the clue's direction (inside the 9x9 grid) where N is the digit next to the clue in that direction. 

Eg if the cell to the left of the given 2 contained a 6 then 6 must be placed in the cell to the right of that 2 (because this is the 2nd cell in the 9x9 grid from that direction).

If you are unsure about the rules there is an example grid at this link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000GPF

title: A Miracle Puzzle that's Solved by Magic!
description:
Here's where you can and should try The Miracle of the Magic Squares by BobZeBuilder: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/mds9euoo1c 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In the grid there are 5 IDENTICAL Magic Squares (a magic square is a 3x3 area in which the rows and columns and the two diagonals all have the same sum). In addition, there is a 6th 3x3 Magic Square; the SPECIAL SQUARE. The Special Square contains the same layout of digits as the other 5 magic squares, but rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise, and it is composed of the centre digits of the nine 3x3 sudoku boxes, in the same layout. Along the negative diagonal (from R1C1 to R9C9), a digit's value cannot be within 1 of its row/column number, ie. R4C4 is not allowed to be 3, 4, 5. However, there is one naughty cell on this diagonal which is breaking this rule; the location of the naughty digit is to be determined.

title: Each Clue does THREE Jobs!
description:
This is where you can try In The Orchard by Philipp Blume, aka Glum_hippo: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/bTddT728fG 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in circles are simultaneously skyscraper sums, full rank clues, and arrow bulbs.
SKYSCRAPER SUMS: imagine each cell as a building of height N, where N is the digit in the cell. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of heights of buildings that can be seen in that row or column, whereby larger buildings obscure the view of smaller ones, eg the row 415798362 has a skyscraper sum of 4+5+7+9=25 from the left and 2+6+8+9=25 from the right.
FULL RANK: imagine each row and column, read in either direction, as a 9-digit number. If all 36 such numbers were listed in ascending order, then the clue indicates the rank which the corresponding row/column would take in that list. 
ARROW BULBS give the sum of the digits along the attached arrow. Digits may repeat on arrows if permitted by other sudoku rules. Arrow shafts in R4C6 cross each other; they do not bend.

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Michael Lefkowitz is one of the most original constructors in the puzzle world and, yet again, he's come up with something that WILL confound your expectation.  Things are not as they first appear!!!!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/yiaonocy5d

title: How To Crack The Sudoku Code
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Marty Sears is a sudoku-making machine.  He's making puzzle after brilliant puzzle and many of you have stated (with good reason) that this is your favourite sudoku of 2024 so far.  It's called Quad Code and it WILL make you smile.  Don't miss this one.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/7613uxdt7g

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. In this puzzle, each digit from 1-9 is represented by a letter from A-I. You must determine which letter represents which digit. When discovered, these can be entered into the orange boxes at the bottom. The 2x2 area surrounding a quad circle must contain all the digits represented by the letters in that circle. The digits along a grey line can be divided into one or more non-overlapping groups of adjacent cells, each of which sums to 10. The digits in a blue or yellow cage must sum to the total in the top left corner. Enter correct digits near the grey fog cells to clear the fog. No guessing is necessary.

title: The Puzzle With The Most Unexpected Endgame
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Christounet returns to Cracking The Cryptic today with a 100%-rated monster: Yin Yang Killer Deconstruction (to give it its full title) is brilliant and baffling!  It's only got 4* for difficulty on Logic Masters but it certainly puts up some resistance and several of the steps on the way to the solution are FANTASTIC.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/bL36N3P9tH

Rules:
Fill the grid with 9 non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions do not contain digits. The whole 11x11 grid must form a valid “yin yang” grid: ie shade some cells such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected, all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected, and no 2x2 area is fully shaded or fully unshaded. Digits in a cage must not repeat. The number in the top left corner indicates either the sum of the digits of the shaded cells or the sum of the digits of the unshaded cells contained within that cage.

An absolutely GREAT tribute to the constructor Aad van de Wetering today from PotatoHead21's sudoku "Quad van de Wetering"!  One of the shortest rulesets we've seen in recent times but, don't worry, there's a whole host of interesting and original logic in this one!

title: Does the Hardest Geezer do Sudoku?
description:
Heres' where you can play Project Africa by ThePedallingPianist: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/2hw7t4w2lm 
(Colour-blind friendly version: https://sudokupad.app/slzvdt2kqg )
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on the red line must differ by at least 5. On land, "hotter" cells contain higher digits; i.e. orange cells contain larger digits than orthogonally adjacent yellow cells, which contain larger digits than orthogonally adjacent green cells. The four cages must be filled with four important numbers from Russ Cook's journey, read left to right. The solver must decide which number goes in which cage:
352 (days on mission);
19 (million steps, at least);
16 (countries/cells passed through);
? (total no. of "1s and 2s" on the red line)
Russ Cook today completes his mission to become the first person to run the entire length of Africa, and has made over £500k for charity so far. Please consider sharing or even contributing to Russ' fundraising efforts. https://sudokupad.app/slzvdt2kqg

title: Why Are We Doing A Puzzle With a 2% Approval Rating?!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Well the answer to the question in the title is because a boatload of people have recommended it to us!  James Sinclair's suspiciously-titled Polar Foil not only has the lowest rating but also the longest ruleset we've ever seen!!  To discover why it's so brilliant, you'll need to have a go at it (or watch the video!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/polar-foil

Rules:
11x11 deconstruction rules apply: fill the grid with nine non-overlapping 3x3 square regions, such that each region contains the digits 1-9 once each and no digit repeats in any row or column. Cells outside regions do not contain digits.

All cells that contain digits form a single orthogonally-connected region. All cells that do not contain digits form a loop that is one cell wide and does not branch or touch itself, even diagonally.

The following standard clues appear in the puzzle:
Thermometers: digits on thermometers increase from the bulb.
Region sum lines: box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum.
Renban lines: purple lines contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits in any order.
Nabner lines: gold lines contain a non-repeating set of digits, and no two digits on the same line can be consecutive (regardless of their position on the line).
Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even.
Digits in cells with a shaded circle must be odd.
However, all clues are wrogn! For the purposes of this puzzle:
A thermometer is not “wrogn” if any cell on the thermometer contains a digit that is equal to or less than a digit in a cell that is further from the bulb.
A region sum line is not “wrogn” if any two segments (as divided by box borders) on the same line contain a set of digits that sum to the same number.
A renban line is not “wrogn” if, for any digit N that appears on the line, another digit on the line is equal to N, N–1, or N+1.
A nabner line is not “wrogn” unless all of the following conditions are true:
- the smallest digit on the line is consecutive with exactly one other digit on the same line,
- the largest digit on the line is consecutive with exactly one other digit on the same line, and
- all other digits on the line are consecutive with exactly two other digits on the same line.
A cell with a shaded square is not “wrogn” if it contains an even digit.
A cell with a shaded circle is not “wrogn” if it contains an odd digit.
For each of the clues above, cells that do not contain digits are ignored.

In addition, exactly one of the following chess-based constraints applies:
Anti-bishop: cells separated by a bishop’s move cannot contain the same digit.
Anti-king: cells separated by a king’s move cannot contain the same digit.
Anti-knight: cells separated by a knight’s move cannot contain the same digit.
Anti-rook: cells separated by a rook’s move cannot contain the same digit.

*** NEW JAMES BOND SUDOKU HUNT OUT ON 1 APRIL ***

title: One Of The Very Best Fog Sudokus
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love Fog Of War sudokus and today's puzzle - by Astral Sky called Caged Snakey - is one of the best we've ever seen.  Truly original from start to finish and full of fascinating logic.  And quite mad!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/LbhRLHDjJH

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits may repeat within a cage and sum to the total in the cage’s top left corner, if given. All cages must be of different sizes. Two cages that neighbour one another (ie share an edge) must not share a common digit. All the cages in the puzzle combined form a 1-cell-wide snake. The snake doesn’t branch and doesn’t touch itself orthogonally, but may touch itself diagonally. The start and end of the snake must be found by the solver. The grid is partly covered with fog. title: The "Easiest" Phistomefel Sudoku!?
description:
*** NEW JAMES BOND SUDOKU HUNT OUT YESTERDAY ***
Do you know your Drax from your Goldfinger? Make sure you've got your licence to kill renewed to enter our latest competition: a brand new James Bond-themed sudoku hunt!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of the most fantastic pieces of recent news from the world of sudoku is the emergence of more puzzles from the great setter Phistomefel. Today we try his latest creation, Copycat, which some of you have claimed is his "easiest"...  

We're not so sure but we do agree it's another piece of brilliance from the legend himself.

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/myxmj3f1g9

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey line is a palindrome - the digits on a palindrome line read the same in both directions. The lavender line is a Zipper line - digits an equal distance from the centre of a zipper line must sum to the digit in the middle of that line. The two lines have the same composition of digits. E.g. if one line has two 3s, five 4s and a 9, then so does the other. The order of the digits is not necessarily the same on the two lines. Cells separated by a white dot contain digits whose values differ by 1. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 2:1 ratio ie one digit is double the other. Not necessarily all dots are drawn in.

title: Two 5 Year Olds Set A "Soduko"
description:
*** NEW JAMES BOND SUDOKU HUNT OUT TODAY ***
Do you know your Drax from your Goldfinger? Make sure you've got your licence to kill renewed to enter our latest competition: a brand new James Bond-themed sudoku hunt!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Well it's April Fools Day and we're thrilled to share with you a puzzle apparently by two 5 year olds, Marty & Nordy, called My First Soduko!  It's a wrogn puzzle in which five of the clues are lying - which ones you'll need to work out; bearing in mind that the wrong clues could be those given by Mark, Simmon & Bobbins The Cat (!!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/iutvqv1ht8

Rules:
Normal soduko rules apply. We have drawed a lot of clues, to mak it a really good puzzle. We have even put some red clues outside the grid. All clues are telling the truth accept for 5 of them, which are lying.  (if a clue doesnt completly work like it should, then it is lying.) Can you find the 5 lying clues?

All the clues are standdard rules:

A pink line is a rembam, this means that all the digits on there are in a seqeunce, maybe like 4567, but they dont repeat and the seqeunce can be in a diffrent order like 5746.

Green means a German Shhhhh line. All of ajaxent digits on green lines must be at least 5 diffrent from eachother. Like 6 and 1 is ok but 4 and 2 is not ok.

Red CLues outside the grid pointing inwards diloganly give the sum of the digits on that dialagonal.

If there is a dashed line cage then this is a KILLER! cage. anythign you rite in there cant repeat, and must sum to what the small number in the corner says.

Digits along the light grey thermomometer must increase as you move away from the end with the blub.

Ditgits on a light blue arrow sum to whats in the circle.

Dark grey lines are Ten Lines which is an idea we stole from zetamaths. A ten line is made of groups of adjaxent digits which do'nt overlap and each group sums to 10. EG: 28532 can be split into two groops which sum to 10.

Digits with white dot means they are consticutive like 3 and 4 are.

A little purple arrow sits between two digits and points at the smaller one. Eg: 2 is smaller than 8.

Digits with an X sum to 10. Eg: 3 and 7.

Finaly! There is some caracters we drawed outside the grid. What they are saying (in red) counts as clues too, so remember thjey might be lying! lol

description:
Here's where you can try Warming Sets by Teal: https://sudokupad.app/k9p714r5cw 
Place a subset of the digits 1-9 in each row, column and box (you can use different sets for different regions). Digits cannot repeat in rows, columns, or boxes. The sum of Row 6 is less than the sum of Row 5, which is less than the sum of Row 4, and so on (indicated by the thermometer). Box borders separate the blue Region Sum line (as in r1c3-6) into segments which sum to the same amount. A red entropy line (as in r1c1-3) must contain an equal number of low (1,2,3) middle (4,5,6) and high (7,8,9) digits. Adjacent digits on a green German Whisper line (as in r5c3-5) must differ by at least 5. Digits on an arrow sum to the attached circle. A black kropki dot separates digits with a 1:2 ratio.

title: 4 Different Logic Puzzles In One Grid!?
description:
Please note that in the UK the clocks spring forward 1 hour tonight so, if your clocks don't change this evening, tomorrow's videos will appear one hour earlier than you might expect!

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
One of these jaw-dropping creations today from Testarossa, who has somehow combined shikaku, starbattle, masyu and killer sudoku in the SAME grid.  An absolute treat for those of us who love the logic puzzles of Nikoli, the Japanese publishing giant.  None of the individual elements is too tricky so do have a go (and we know that the rules of masyu can seem daunting if you've never seen them before but we promise they aren't too bad!!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/n4qHMLbtTd

Rules:
Stage1 - Shikaku: Divide the grid into rectangular or square pieces. Each piece must contain exactly one digit, that shows its area.
Stage 2 - Star battle: Place stars into the grid, so that each shikaku rectangle/square has one, and each row/column/3x3 box contains two of them. Stars can't be adjacent, even diagonally.
Stage 3 - Masyu: Stars from star battle act as masyu circles - if it has a digit in the same cell, it is black; if not - it's white. Draw the single non-branching non-intersecting loop. The loop should pass through all circles in such a way that: White circles must be passed through in a straight line, but the loop must turn in the previous and/or the next cell; Black circles must be turned upon and the loop must travel straight through the next and the previous cell.
Stage 4 - Killer sudoku: Normal sudoku rules apply. Groups of cells not visited by the masyu loop act as killer cages. Those groups and killer cages already drawn in the grid must all sum to the same total.

description:

The world of sudoku has hit another purple (lavender?!) patch.  Today we tackle another beauty from Marty Sears called My Zipper Is Broken.  The logic here will make you smile!!

https://sudokupad.app/zfvmhmn8ev

Connect the $ symbols with a single meandering Redline. The Redline moves along cell edges and never touches itself. It cannot cross a dot or the train tracks. title: Can You Become A Professor Of Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Maths Professor Dorlir has come up with an a blisteringly brilliant puzzle today - it's part sudoku and part fillomino... one difficulty the solver faces is that we aren't told which digits are which!!  The whole thing is fascinating but take care - it is very easy to make a mistake!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/tpi8hjfum7

Rules:
Each digit from 1 to 8 must appear eight times in the grid. Some digits from 1 to 8 are sudoku digits and the others are omino digits. All instances of a particular digit are of the same type. For each digit, its type must be determined. A sudoku digit must appear exactly once in every row, column and box. An omino digit indicates the size of its omino (an omino is a group of orthogonally connected cells containing identical omino digits.) Two ominos of the same size may not touch each other - not even diagonally. For a digit in a circle, it indicates exactly how many circles contain that digit. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive digits.

title: Phistomefel Told Us To Do This!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We had an email from none other than Phistomefel recommending we have a go at IcyFruit's Solver, There's A Fly On My Sudoku! Predictably enough, this is a fantastic puzzle and it features a VERY dynamic fly...  See what you think!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/1weh2nwtje

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 1:2. A fly has flown across the page, in orthogonal lines. It always went north from a cell containing a 2, east from a 4, south from a 6, and west from an 8. On odd digits, it kept going in a straight line. The fly entered the grid heading west at the arrow, and exited heading east at the bottom right of the grid. It did not leave and re-enter the grid at any point. The fly may have crossed its own path, but it never flew directly across a dot.

title: An ASTONISHING Sudoku Variant
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Tonight we try yttrio's latest, Sashigane Whispers, which combines sudoku with the Japanese pencil puzzle Sashigane.  It's all about making L-shaped pieces in the grid but the way it works here is quite staggering.  If you are lucky enough to have time to try this one you won't regret it!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/tl5phvto7f

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. 
Sashigane: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells.  Each region must be an L shape with a width of one cell. Digits cannot repeat within a region. Arrows must lie at one end of an L and point toward the bend.  The digit on an arrow must contain the number of cells along that leg of that region, including the bend and arrow cells. Circles must lie at the bend of an L.  Digits in a circle must contain the total number of cells in the region, including the circled cell. 
Any Sashigane region that contains either a circle or arrow clue must act as a German Whispers line (i.e., adjacent digits within such a region must have a difference of at least 5).  A Sashigane region without a circle or arrow clue has no such restriction.

title: Aren't Sudokus Meant To Only Have 81 Squares?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A lovely debut puzzle for Giesmania tonight and their sudoku Dark Magic.  It's an 11x11 grid where you have to work out where to position the nine 3x3 boxes!  And any 3x3 box not in a corner needs to be a magic square :)

Only 3 stars for difficulty and it might even be easier if you know one or two secrets!

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/bhxcnaf8gg

Rules:
Draw 9 non-overlapping 3x3 boxes and fill them with the digits 1-9 such that no digit repeats in a row, column, or box. Cells outside these 9 boxes should be left empty. Any 3x3 box that is not in the corner of the grid must also be a magic square: ie Each 3-cell row, column, and main diagonal of that box must sum to the same total. Black dots separate digits whose ratio is written on the dot. White dots separate consecutive digits. A clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. Digits along a thermometer increase from the bulb end. Digits cannot repeat on the blue diagonal. All clues inside the grid must fully fit inside the 3x3 boxes (except the blue line).

title: The Most Powerful Kingdom In Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
 Marty Sears is one of the most inventive setters in the puzzle world and he shows that again today with Counting Castles, his latest creation.  We love the idea about dividing the grid into kingdoms with different power!  It's not a simple sudoku though (or at least Simon doesn't think so!)

Play the puzzle at the link below:
https://sudokupad.app/5060viuw2v

Rules:
Divide the grid into 9 kingdoms of orthogonally connected cells. Fill the grid with the digits 1-9 so that each digit appears once in each row, column and kingdom. A digit on a castle indicates exactly how many castles contain that digit. Every kingdom has a score, representing how powerful it is. This is calculated by adding the number of castles the kingdom contains to the number of neighbouring kingdoms it borders. (Two kingdoms are considered neighbours if they share at least one orthogonal edge.) A digit in a blue square indicates its kingdom's score. No two kingdoms have the same score. A bridge connects two digits in different kingdoms, and they will either sum to 5, sum to 10, or be in a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other).

description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Juggler is one of the most inventive puzzlemakers in the World and he's come up with a great innovation to killer sudoku using tangrams.  This is a simply lovely construction (and not too difficult).  

https://sudokupad.app/zmgcavpoxu

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage sum to the number in its corner. Cells that half-appear in a cage only contribute half their value to its sum. Digits appear at most once in the same cage (but half-appearing twice counts as appearing once!).

NB For the sake of clarity: In this particular puzzle the last line of the rules means that there could theoretically be a repeated digit in r6c2 and r7c3, for example.  (Because, each time that digit appeared in the 12 cage, it is only counting for half its value).

title: One Galaxy to Rule them All
description:
Dorlir has come up with a coimpletely original ambiguity puzzle! Try it here: Segue Ursa by Dorlir: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/twacfrsxbk 
Normal sudoku rules apply. It must be determined whether each white dot is a kropki dot or the centre of a galaxy.
The two digits joined by a white kropki dot have a difference indicated by the number on the kropki dot.
A galaxy is a group of orthogonally connected cells, that has the white dot at its centre and is rotationally symmetrical through 180 degrees. The number on the central dot of a galaxy indicates the number of cells (N) in the galaxy. This galaxy must contain all the digits from 1 to N. Galaxies also function like region sum lines; digits within each 3x3 box sum to the same amount if they are within the same galaxy. This region sum may be different for different galaxies. Galaxies cannot share cells with any other galaxies or cells joined by a kropki dot.

title: The Sudoku Proof That P=NP
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After the re-emergence of Phistomefel yesterday, what a thrill to see damasosos92 reappear today with P=NP, a provocative title if we understand the reference!  This is a quite gorgeous sudoku with some really unusual and interesting logic.  Well worth your time!!

https://sudokupad.app/in3a5cg87s

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage in the grid is either a P pentomino or an N pentomino. Every pentomino is completely filled by either a renban line or a thermometer, hidden behind the pentomino. Cells along a renban line contain a set of consecutive, non-repeating digits in any order. Digits on a thermometer must strictly increase as they move away from the bulb. The position of the bulb has to be deduced by the solver. Thermometers only make vertical or horizontal turns inside the pentominoes and don't branch. All the cages of the same shape hide the same constraint: the solver has to deduce which constraint is hidden behind each shape.
