title: He's Back! The Return Of Phistomefel
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It has been no less than nine months since the last puzzle by the extraordinary constructor known as Phistomefel.  No one knew where he had gone or what he was doing but, a few days ago, he suddenly re-emerged from his cocoon with a brand new puzzle!!  Modular Region Sum Lines, as one comment said, solves like a Phistomefel sudoku - the "best compliment a puzzle can receive"!

https://sudokupad.app/4ev7ufnh17

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw in lines that move orthogonally from cell to cell. Two circles of the same colour are start and end of a line. Lines may not intersect themselves or other lines. The lines drawn in the grid act both as a Region Sum Line (RSL) and a Modular Line (ML). Additionally, digits CANNOT repeat on a line. Region Sum Line: Along a RSL line, box borders divide the line into segments with the same sum. Every set of three sequential digits along a ML must contain a complete set of residues modulo 3, i.e. one digit from {1,4,7}, one from {2,5,8}, and one from {3,6,9}.

description:
Here's where you can try Pentominoku for Layla by ibn Muhyiddin: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/5nyl31krz4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Tile the grid (except for the shaded central cell) in pentominoes. Each pentomino shape is associated with a number from 1 to 9 (its pentominoku number): F: 6, L: 2, N: 3, P: 4, T: 5, U: 8, V: 7, W: 8, X: 9, Y: 1, Z: 9. The pentominoku number must occur exactly twice in each pentomino; starred cells show where some of these occurrences are. It is possible for other numbers to occur twice within a pentomino. You do not need to use all pentomino shapes, and pentominoes of the same shape can be orthogonally adjacent.

title: The Cure For Brain Fog
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Scojo returns to the channel tonight with a quite brilliant fog-of-war puzzle. It's also a cipher sudoku, which is a genre/ruleset we've rarely covered - we know all the letters represent different digits but we don't know which ones!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
Version 1 (including a notepad to keep track of the letters - RECOMMENDED):
https://sudokupad.app/8vzgxh2w8i

Version 2 (no notepad - more memory required!):
https://sudokupad.app/8zrctglexn

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Most of the grid is obscured by fog. Placing a correct digit will remove the fog surrounding that cell. Each letter from A-J uniquely represents one of the digits 0-9. A two-letter clue represents a two-digit number which does not begin with 0. A clue outside the grid represents the sum of the digits in the first X cells seen from that clue, where X is the first cell seen. (Eg if r1c5 is a 5 then the IF clue is summing the first 5 cells in its column.) Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the cage total, which is given in the leftmost cell of the highest row of the cage.

title: Not your Average Puzzle at all
description:
Here's where you can try Not Your Average Thermo Puzzle  by Scojo: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/6D6Lrqt7p7
[Remember to select “Draw Arrows above Lines: On” in Settings!]
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along a thermometer, digits increase from bulb to tip. Digits along an orange arrow average exactly to the digit in that arrow's circle. Multiple arrows extending from the same circle are treated as different arrows each averaging to the circled digit. For example, a circled 3 could have 15 on one of its arrows, and 24 on the other, because both arrows would average to 3. For clarity, 'average' in this puzzle refers to the arithmetic mean.

description:
Here's where you can have a go at Difference Fences by RockyRoer: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/17rhp0owyb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in the quad circles must appear in the surrounding four cells. Digits in some quads must be deduced. The white segments represent 'Difference Fences'. Each segment has a value equal to the difference between the cells they separate. On a fence, no two segments can have the same value. Each fence has a total value equal to the sum of all the segments on the fence and this total value is given in the attached quad (it may be a 2-digit number). Some total values will need to be deduced.

title: The Treacherous Sudoku
description:
*** ISLANDS OF INSIGHT STREAM TONIGHT ***
We're going to risk streaming this game, which sounds so perfect for the channel.  Tonight at 10pm UK time - we'd love to have your company! You can watch it here:

https://youtube.com/live/nGgZYUt1zpg

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We have had a whole host of recommendations to try this puzzle by blackjackfitz called Duplicates.  It's got a fascinating (and brain-breaking) ruleset but it's a LOT of fun to solve. Just remember, sudoku isn't always your friend!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/jdcz0c4rtb

Rules:
Fill each cell with a digit from 1 to 9.  For every row 'n' and column 'n' there are exactly 'n' unique digits present. The remaining cells are filled with duplicates. e.g. Row 3 could be filled (1,2,7,1,2,7,7,7,7) containing 3 unique digits. Digits in a cage do not repeat and sum to the number in the top left hand corner of the cage, if given. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a blue diamond are duplicates (i.e. the same). Not all dots or diamonds are given.

title: The Mathematics Of Fog
description:
** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
 It's been half a year since we last saw a puzzle from Jeet Sampat - after a short hiatus from setting, he returns today with Genus 3 - an absolutely stunning sudoku, full of brutal and brilliant logic. It's a fog-of-war puzzle - which we love - merged with little killer sudoku and a bit of maths!  Oh yes, and it's 11x11 and we aren't told where the 3x3 regions are...

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/f0zxtm2lrs

Rules:
The grid is covered in fog that hides cells underneath it. Placing correct digits will reveal surrounding cells. Construct nine non-overlapping 3x3 regions in the grid containing digits 1-9 once each. The rest of the grid must be left empty. Digits must not repeat along any row or column. Digits on a grey thermometer must strictly increase from the bulb-end. The sum of digits along a diagonal indicated by a clue outside the grid must satisfy either the given inequality or the corresponding relationship with other such clues.

title: Battleships AND Sudoku!
description:
** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Oripy has created a whole series of hyrbid puzzles marrying up some of the best Japanese logic problems with sudoku.  Many of them have been recommended to us over the last few weeks so we thought we'd have a crack at this one: Kaiserliche Marine.  This is a SERIOUSLY excellent puzzle which combines elements of both puzzle types beautifully. 

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/anfigouctj?setting-nogrid=1

Rules:
Normal 9x9 Sudoku rules apply. 

Battleships: Place the given fleet of ships into the grid so that no two ships are touching, not even diagonally. Rotating ships is permitted. A clue outside the grid indicates the number of cells in the corresponding row or column that are occupied by ship segments.

German fleet: All ships are German Whisper lines. Adjacent digits along the line must have a difference of at least 5.

Kropki Dots: Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one is exactly double the other. Not all dots are necessarily given.

There is a smaller example puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/r2j26yf2s3

title: You Won't Believe The Ending Of This Sudoku!
description:
*** HEXCELLS STREAM TONIGHT ***
Our latest Hexcells stream will be tonight at 10pm UK time.  Do join us if you can at the following link:

https://youtube.com/live/ZQTJXTtIu60

** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We've been almost inundated with recommendations to tackle this Marty Sears' sudoku called Pseudoscience - which introduces a the concept of a "pseudo cell".  It is epic from start to finish but the finish is really really extraordinary.  We went say more but do try the puzzle and discover why! 

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/0ham0u0jtt

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply.
In each row, column and box there is exactly one 'pseudo cell.'
The digits 1-9 each appear once in a pseudo cell.
The real value of a pseudo cell (for the purposes of the coloured lines) is determined by multiplying its row number by its column number. Eg; if there is a pseudo cell in r6c3, it has the value of 18, regardless of which digit appears in that cell.

GERMAN WHISPER: The values of adjacent cells on a green line have a difference of at least 5.
RENBAN: The values of the cells along a purple line form a non-repeating consecutive set, which can be arranged in any order.
NABNER: The value of a cell on a yellow line may not be consecutive with (or the same as) any other values on that line.
REGION SUM: The value of cells within each 3x3 box along a darker blue line sum to the same amount.
SAME DIFFERENCE: The values of adjacent digits on a turquoise line always have the same difference.
DIFFERENT DIFFERENCE: The difference between the values of adjacent cells on a peach line must be different for every pair of adjacent cells on that line. Eg: if there are two cells with values of 7 and 9 next to each other on the line, then cells with values of 4 and 6 may not appear next to each other on the same line (as both pairs would have a difference of 2.)


The puzzle Simon mentioned in the introduction is called Region Geometry and it's by Emre Kolotoğlu.  If you have some minutes free, you can try it at the link below.  We will make this 3hr 36min video available on Patreon in the coming days.

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0009WX

title: Enter the Dragon!
description:
Here's where you can try Year of the Dragon by Marushia Dark: https://sudokupad.app/bDLDDJTNLG 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains a number of colored line segments that together form the Chinese character for "Dragon." Adjacent digits on a colored line must differ by at least the amount written in the cell of the same color, eg. the 2 in R9C3 indicates that adjacent digits on a blue line must differ by at least 2. The grey and purple lines must each form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits in any order. For clarity, there is one purple line and the grey cell must be deduced. Additionally, there are two dancing dragons wandering the grid. Each dragon starts and ends at a red dot and forms a non-repeating set of consecutive digits IN ORDER. Dragons may move orthogonally or diagonally and may touch themselves or each other. Dragons may not branch, cross themselves or each other, nor enter cells marked by an X.

title: The Miracle Sudoku: Rubik's Cube
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There have been a whole host of miracle sudokus since Mitchell Lee's original puzzle all those years ago.  Most achieve their sparsely-filled grids with extremely complicated, long rulesets.  Michael Lefkowitz bucks that trend!  Here is an almost entirely blank grid and a SHORT ruleset - the whole thing, which is called Rubik's Cube, is quite mad!!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/P4h9q6HtRH

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The white dot separates digits with consecutive values. Cells in the same position in two 3x3 boxes may not contain the same digit. (So eg, r1c1 and r4c4 cannot contain the same digit as these are both in the top left corner of their 3x3 boxes.) 'XYZ' means 'Row X Col Y is digit Z.' If XYZ is true, YZX is also true.

title: One of These Things is Not Like the Others!
description:
Here's where you can try One of these things ... by Jrosas: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/TRFJDDjmjt 
Normal sudoku rules apply. All cells in the grid can be divided into two orthogonally connected regions with no 2x2 square entirely in either region. Each cage contains one cell that is not like the others, ie. one digit in each cage is in a different region than are all the others in that cage. The sum clue in a cage is the sum of the “others” in that cage, eg. if the cage sum is 3 and there are three cells in the cage, there is an unknown digit that is in the opposite region from the other two, which are a 1 and a 2. Digits do not repeat within cages. A black dot joins digits that are in a 1:2 ratio. A white dot joins consecutive digits.

title: When A Digit Can Be In One Of Six Places And It Matters...!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday we mentioned that it was blackjackfitz' birthday and today we try his puzzle: Rellik Loop - which is flying high at a 99% approval rating.  It has a medium difficulty rating and is just wonderful throughout - a stunning debut, including one really amazing idea mid-solve.

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/ka3olc7kq1

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a given killer cage must sum to the total in the top left hand corner. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1 to 2 ratio. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Draw a single, closed, 1-cell-wide loop that moves orthogonally through the centres of cells, and does not branch, overlap, or touch itself (not even diagonally). All of the purple diamond 'relliks' are on the loop. The loop creates a set of “rellik cages” where every discrete set of orthogonally connected loop cells within a single box is considered a rellik cage. In a rellik cage, any combination of one or more digits CANNOT sum to the rellik cage value. A rellik cage value is equal to the number of cells in the rellik cage. If the loop passes through a box multiple times, each individual segment is its own rellik cage. e.g. A 6 cell rellik cage may not contain (1,2,3), (1,5), (2,4) or a 6.


The puzzle Simon mentioned in the introduction is called Region Geometry and it's by Emre Kolotoğlu.  If you have some minutes free, you can try it at the link below.  We will make this 3hr 36min video available on Patreon in the coming days.

title: Can you Beat this Dog at Sudoku?
description:
Tomorrow is Chuy's birthday, and Nala has sent her friend a puzzle and some instructions. You can try it here: Chuy the “Frisbee Detective” by Sandra & Nala: https://sudokupad.app/sandra-and-nala/chuy-the-frisbee-detective 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is partially covered in fog. Entering correct digits will clear the fog from surrounding cells, possibly revealing more clues. If an arrow is present in a cell, the digit in the cell the arrow comes from appears in the grid in the direction of the arrow at a distance of N cells, where N is the digit in the arrow's cell. Example: If R3C4 had an arrow pointing to the left and R3C4 was a 2, then the digit below that arrow (R4C4) would appear in R3C2 again. Each line in the grid is a palindrome. The sequence of digits along a palindrome read the same from both ends. Each palindrome is a single line in a unique color. Digits in cells that are connected by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells that are connected by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
IcyFruit's sudoku puzzles are just magical.  This is their latest offering and it's brim full of gorgeous, innovative logic.  It's a puzzle that seems impossible to start until you realise a couple of things and then you can't let it go until you've finished it!!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/748nmm3bpM

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue lines are ‘region sum lines’ ie 3x3 box borders divide each blue line into segments with the same sum. Brown lines are ‘product sum lines’ ie the digits on each end of the line must multiply together to give the sum of ALL digits on the line. Draw a 1-cell-wide snake which moves orthogonally and does not touch itself (even diagonally). The snake must enter every 3x3 box exactly once and may not include any cell which is on a line (but may include circled cells). The snake acts as both a region sum line and a product sum line. A digit in a circle indicates the number of times that digit appears on the snake.

*** CIRCLE SUMS by JESPER ***

title: Things Are REALLY Wrogn In The Sudoku Fogn!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Surely the most daunting and mad ruleset in sudoku history as ViKingPrime decides to merge fog, liar clues AND Schrödinger cells in one puzzle!!  This is not for the faint hearted but some of the logic is really incredible.  Remember you don't need to guess...!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/Gr6P42rgHH

Rules:
Place the digits 0 through 9 once each in every row, column and box; to enable this, each row, column and box contains exactly one Schrödinger Cell ie a cell that contains two digits. The grid is partially covered in fog; placing correct digits in non-Schrödinger cells will clear the fog from the surrounding area (no guessing is required).  Each of the standard clue types below occurs exactly three times in the grid; for each, exactly two of the appearances of that clue are correct and the other is incorrect. The clue types are: 
 - Counting Circles (ie each circled digit counts exactly how many circles contain that digit. All other clue types consider the sum total of a cell as that cell’s value.); 
 - Dutch Whisper - adjacent cells along an orange line must differ in value by at least 4;
 - German Whisper – adjacent cells along a green line must differ in value by at least 5; 
 - Killer cages - values in a killer cage must sum to small clue in the top left corner of the cage & digits cannot repeat in a cage; 
 - Kropki dots ie cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive values & cells separated by a black dot must contain values in a 1:2 ratio (ie one value is double the other); and 
 - X/V rules ie cells separated by an X must contain values summing to 10 and cells separated by a V must contain values summing to 5. 

Disconnected lines within the same cell indicate two separate lines.

*** CIRCLE SUMS by JESPER ***

title: The Colours Of Logic
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
With a deadline looming, Simon attempts a gorgeous new sudoku from yttrio called Mad Mod Quad Loop.  There is not one thing about this puzzle that is not extremely enjoyable (and Simon will probably get the video up by 8.30pm - maintaining a record since the start of the first lockdown!!)

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/nuf4q68voj

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a 2:1 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). Not all possible dots are necessarily given. Digits in a circle must appear in at least one of the four surrounding cells. Draw a one-cell-wide loop of orthogonally connected cells. The loop may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The loop must enter exactly one of the four cells surrounding each given quad clue. The loop acts as a modular line. Each set of three adjacent digits along the loop must be one each from the sets [147], [258], and [369].

title: Seeking out that Orange Snake!
description:
Here's where you can play Dutch Baby by Glum Hippo: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/hm580ts3a9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. There is an orange snake in the grid, which moves from one cell center to the next horizontally or vertically (i.e., never diagonally). It may not touch itself orthogonally. The snake divides the non-snake cells into 8 different regions, one of each size from 1-8 cells. Each of these regions is orthogonally contiguous and acts like a killer cage. Each cage encloses exactly one sum clue, which indicates the sum of the digits in that cage, and digits may not repeat in any cage. (The sum clue need not be in the top left corner of the cage). The snake itself is a so-called 'Dutch Whisper' line, i.e. neighboring digits on the snake must differ by 4 or more. The white dot joins consecutive digits.

title: How can Cages, Regions and Boxes all be Different?
description:
Here's where you can try Numbers in Cages in Regions in a 6x6 by PeterJoe: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/GhG9BQQfG2 
Place 1-6 in each row, column and marked 3x2 box. Digits in cages sum to the clue in the top-left corner, if given. N represents a number that must be deduced. Build regions such that all regions from sizes 1 to N are present exactly once. Cage totals also indicate the size of the region in which the cage resides. Every cell is in a region. Orthogonally adjacent regions must have sizes of opposite parity. Orthogonally adjacent cells in different regions must be of opposite parity.

title: This Puzzle Will Literally Create Thousands Of Hours Of Joy
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An absolutely brilliant twist on the Zipper Line ruleset from gdc today with a sudoku that is wonderful from start to finish.  It is a lovely thing to contemplate how many hours of joy gdc will have contributed to the world by creating this puzzle... we can safely say it's thousands and thousands.  ie Net worldwide joy has increased as a result of its existence...!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/4hq3qvqmnk

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Values an equal distance to the circled centre of a lavender “zipper” line sum to the value of the central digit. Nine cells (one in each row, column and 3x3 box) contain a “Mirrored Digit”. A Mirrored Digit takes the value opposite to its digit on the 1-9 scale. (In other words, 1 takes the value of 9, 2 the value of 8... 9 the value of 1.) Each digit 1-9 is mirrored once. Unmirrored digits use their digits as values.

title: How To Become A Puzzle Grandmaster
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A logic puzzle today from the brilliant Turkish constructor Serkan Yürekli.  Serkan, along with Thomas Snyder (3x World Sudoku Champion) is one of the brains behind gmpuzzles.com - a great place to find handcrafted puzzles: https://www.gmpuzzles.com/blog/

Serkan has made this cool Fillomino variant especially for us on Valentine's Day!  

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/JtPQ3d3R4D

Rules:
Divide the grid along the grid lines into regions called polyominoes. Place a number inside each cell equal to the total area (in number of cells) of the polyomino it belongs to.  No two polyominoes with the same area, or with areas that differ by one, can share an edge. The number at the top left of each cage gives the sum of all numbers that appear inside of it. Numbers may be repeated in cages. [Answer check will work if cells are filled with just the units digit of their numbers.]

GM Puzzles produces puzzles under a CC licence (https://tinyurl.com/3pj3byec). No changes have been made to this puzzle.

title: The Minimum Number Of Given Digits For A Sudoku Is Now 14
description:
*** HEXCELLS STREAM ***
Our latest Hexcells stream is tonight at 10pm UK time at the following link:

https://youtube.com/live/7fsRf0Q28s8

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A lot of people are aware that the minimum number of given digits necessary to create a classic sudoku with a unique sudoku is 17.  The constructor Lepton has discovered that, in a 10x10 grid, WHERE THE SOLVER MUST FIND THE LOCATIONS OF THE NINE 3x3 BOXES, it is possible to REDUCE the number of given digits to just 14. description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
It's been a few years now since Simon opened a puzzle live on camera that turned out to be Mitchell Lee's original Miracle Sudoku. https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/159-miracle

(NB The rules below are slightly lengthened and might be helpful if you're new to the 159 constraint.)

Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit in column 1 indicates the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row.  (Eg If r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). A digit in column 5 indicates the column in which the digit 5 appears in that row.  A digits in column 9 indicates the column in which the digit 9 appears in that row.  Digits in cells with a shaded square must be even. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.

title: This Sudoku Is 100% Rated AND Isn't THAT Hard!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
This sudoku, Parity Snakes by Malrog, has achieved a rare distinction: a 100% rating on Logic Masters but only 3 stars for difficulty.  There are actually only a handful of such puzzles in existence!  Many of you have recommended this one - and you were quite right to do so - it's absolutely brilliant (and not too hard!)

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/y23lun2exp

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a white dot must be consecutive (not all dots are given). A digit in a grey square must be even. Each cell containing a circle is the head of a parity snake, whose length is the digit in the circle. A parity snake is a non-branching one-cell-wide path of orthogonally connected cells of the same parity, which may not orthogonally touch itself or other cells of matching parity. A snake may not have two heads, and may be a single cell.

description:

Normal irregular 7x7 Sudoku rules apply, i.e. each row, column and region must contain the digits from 1 to 7 once each. All cages are “Rellik Cages”. title: This Fog-Of-War Sudoku Is Absolutely Stellar!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We love fog-of-war puzzles and Nurator's Cosmic Balance is a fascinating sudoku which mixes the fog with spiral galaxies.  This makes for some lovely original logic - remember you don't need to guess to solve fog puzzles!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/emienzh9f1

Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits reveals clues in the surrounding 3x3 area. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other). Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive. Not all dots are given. Digits in big white circles (quads) must appear in the surrounding 4 cells. Digits in a grey circle must be odd. Divide the grid into “galaxies” ie orthogonally-connected groups of cells that have 180 degree rotational symmetry about their centres, and do not overlap with other galaxies. All cells must be part of a galaxy. The digits in each galaxy do not repeat and sum up to 27. All circular clues (dots, quads, grey circles) are centres of galaxies. All centres of galaxies contain a circular clue.

*** HEXCELLS STREAM ***
We're planning on streaming more Hexcells on Wednesday night at 10pm at the following link:
https://youtube.com/live/G3hseZBCxIE

title: The Doppler Effect:  Another sudoku of crazy brilliance
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Knickolas specialises in sudokus that are memorable and world-class.  This latest, Doppler Effect, joins a stable of puzzles that have few peers. This one forces Simon to think in new ways - we'll be interested to hear whether there are any mathematical theorems out there that would help!

Have a go at the puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/F9fHgrQqQF

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains two “galaxies”.  A galaxy is a collection of orthogonally-connected cells which exhibit 180 degree rotational symmetry around the central cell of the grid. Eg If r2c4 is in a galaxy then r8c6 must also be in that galaxy. All cells must be part of a galaxy and the two galaxies may only ever overlap in one cell - the central cell of the grid. No 2x2 area may be fully part of one galaxy. One of the galaxies is “redshifted” and cells in it have a value of one greater than their digit. The other galaxy is “blueshifted” and cells in it have a value of one less than their digit. Values along an arrow sum to the value in that arrow’s circle. Values in a cage sum to the given total. Digits may not repeat in a cage, but values may.

title: When Sudoku Becomes Poetry...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Exceptional stuff today from Marty Sears and Dorlir who somehow trump what they can each produce individually!!  It's called Catch The Zippersnake and makes Simon feel all poetic... (yes, Captain Beaky is POETRY!).

Have a go at this wonderful puzzle here:
https://sudokupad.app/9onywsf67u

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a snake that starts and ends at a purple spot and has a purple spot exactly at its centre. The snake can only move orthogonally from cell to cell, and may not touch itself, not even diagonally. The snake functions as a “zipper line” ie any pair of digits that are an equal distance from the central spot sum to the digit on that central spot. Any pair of cells connected by a clue (dot, diamond, X or V) must either both be on the snake, or both be off the snake. Cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells connected by black dot contain digits in a 1:2 ratio (ie one is double the other.) Cells connected by a green dot must contain digits with a difference of at least 5. Cells connected by a red diamond contain digits with the same parity (ie both are odd or both are even.) Cells connected by an X contain digits summing to 10. Cells connected by a V contain digits summing to 5.

title: This is a PERFECT sudoku puzzle.
description:
*** JUST RELEASED!!! ***
A brand new sudoku hunt from Riffclown for our February competition!  Get it here for just $2:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We expected this sudoku to be good but it's actually exceptional. It's called 45-45-90 and it's from a debut constructor arctan. It was recommended to us by the brilliant constructor James Sinclair and we would like to thank him - give this a try, it's a blast!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://beta.sudokupad.app/fbhfM7M84N

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits in yellow circles indicate how many yellow circles contain that digit. Additionally, digits in yellow circles must be grouped into pairs.  Each pair form opposite corners of a square, one other corner of which must be the sum of the pair. (Eg if r4c7 and r7c4 were a pair, the sum could go in r4c4 or r7c7.) Different pairs cannot use the same square for their sum. (Eg if r3c4 and r4c3 were also a pair, then r4c4 could be used for the sum of this pair OR the sum of the previous pair, but NOT both.) It is possible that the sum for one pair of circles may itself be in a cell which is already circled. Which circles are paired and where their sums go must be determined by the solver.

description:
We had to re-upload this video tonight due to an audio glitch in the first version.  We'd be grateful to anyone who feels able to give this video a "thumbs-up" or a nice comment just so the algorithm doesn't treat it too unkindly.

*** OUT THIS AFTERNOON ***

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We feel a bit guilty because, although today is Senator Gronk's 53rd birthday, the Senator has given US a present in the form of Pseudo Coup, an absolutely BRILLIANT sudoku puzzle.

[Simon's intro today is Karma Police by Radiohead.]

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/GthdP3BQt6

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  The cells on each pink line contain a set of consecutive values in any order. Adjacent cells on green lines have values that differ by at least 5. Cell values on a grey thermometer increase from the bulb end. Cells separated by a black dot have values in a 1:2 ratio (ie one value will be double the other). Each row, column and box has exactly one "pseudo" cell. The pseudo cells consist of a set of the digits 1-9. For all clue types, a pseudo cell's value is that of its 3x3 box number. description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A new setter bfranj17 has come up with this extraordinary puzzle involving the Phistomefel Ring and factorials!  This is a really remarkable sudoku with some fascinating logic hidden inside it.  We have no real idea how difficult it is - it felt quite challenging... but awesome.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/QBmD43GFg3

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. title: I created this sudoku puzzle. Why did this other guy sign it?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Perhaps the best ruleset in sudoku history today from Michael Lefkowitz ("juggler)!  If you've ever wanted to make your own sudoku then today's the chance but make sure you give the setter what he wants...  

There is a detailed version of the rules below in case some of the terms (German Whispers/Zipper/etc) are unfamiliar.  

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/2g4pswdpxz

The version below has the extended rules:
https://sudokupad.app/rJR9BGfbtD

Rules: 
I need a break from setting sudokus. Could you set one for me please?

I'd like for my sudoku to have five straight lines (and nothing else):
- A horizontal Arrow pointing east (with a one-cell circle)
- A horizontal Thermometer
- A horizontal German Whispers line
- A vertical German Whispers line
- A vertical Zipper line

Each should be as long as it is possible to make orthogonal straight lines of that variety in a sudoku. Put them wherever, just not in the cells with my signature please. 

I'd also like some sort of anti-chess constraint: anti-knight, anti-king, or anti-bishop (up to you, whichever works). Oh, and make sure the solution has a 3 in the corner, won't you? 

Glossary: Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.
Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. 
Adjacent digits on a German Whispers line must differ in value by at least 5. 
Digits which are an equal distance from the centre of a 'zipper' line have the same sum. For odd length lines, that sum is also the central digit.
An anti-knight constraint would mean cells a single chess knight’s move apart may not contain the same digit.
An anti-king constraint would mean cells a single chess king’s move apart may not contain the same digit.
An anti-bishop constraint would mean that a digit could not repeat anywhere along the diagonals radiating from that digit’s cell.

title: A Crazy Sudoku Labyrinth
description:
Here's where you can try Negative Gifts by Patrick Junke: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/T4FNnnm2RQ 
Place 1-9 in each row, column and marked region. All instance of five of the nine digits, to be determined, constitute an area of orthogonal cells, a ‘labyrinth’. The other four digits are considered to be ‘wall’ cells. An arrow appears in a ‘dead end’ of the labyrinth pointing to the only way out, ie. the only labyrinth cell to which it is connected. a 2x2 square containing only labyrinth has a blank square in the middle; a 2x2 square containing only wall cells has a black square in the middle. An X joins two cells that sum to 10, a white dot two consecutive digits, but only if those two cells include one in the labyrinth and one in the wall. All arrows, Xs, white dots and squares are given.

title: The Sudoku Secret Is Made Public
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A quite remarkable miracle-esque sudoku tonight and a debut for shadow-nexus called Public Secrecy.  Bucking the trend of recent short rulesets, this is well worth the extra effort - it's absolutely gorgeous that this solves so (relatively) smoothly and cleverly.  And don't assume you know the digits that are left off the loop - you don't need to know the public secret to solve this puzzle!

(Simon has a golf match today and recorded this video on Thursday evening. This is why the end of the video features tipsy Simon.)
 
Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/Nf89TQFtH2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The green cell is part of a single closed loop whose path must be determined by the solver. The loop travels orthogonally from one cell to the next and visits each 3x3 box at least once, eventually returning to the given green cell clue. The loop may touch itself (even orthogonally) but does not cross itself. Consecutive digits on the loop differ by at least 5. Two “publicly secret” digits never appear on the loop. In each 3x3 box, the corresponding box number must orthogonally neighbour at least one of the secret digits, or be a secret digit itself, or both. In boxes without any of the three given clues, the box number also indicates exactly how many of that number's surrounding cells (including its own cell) are NOT part of the loop. E.g, R5C7 is part of box 6, so if its digit is also 6 then: i) at least one of R4C7, R5C6, R5C7, R5C8, R6C7 should contain a secret digit; and ii) out of R4C6,R4C7,R4C8, R5C6,R5C7,R5C8, R6C6,R6C7,R6C8, 3 cells are visited and the other 6 are NOT visited by the loop. Note: Boxes 1/2/3 contain given clues, in those boxes the box number still neighbours at least one secret digit, but the number does not constrain the line.

title: A Miracle Thermometer Sudoku
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Some recommendations are so fulsome that we obey them instantly!  Marty Sears told us this sudoku by Michael Lefkowitz ("juggler") was a stone cold classic and so we had a go.  You'd be correct in thinking that the grid seems rather empty and the rules somewhat open-ended but there is a unique solution and it is humanly-findable!!

(During editing we noticed a small logical error very late in the video (58mins) right as Simon says "That's the droid we're looking for" (it turned out it wasn't the droid after all!!).  The puzzle is virtually solved at this point but, in case anyone is interested, the easy way to continue without the error is to notice that r1c7 could not be a 5 at this point as it could not attach to a 6.  No droids were harmed as a result of this error but Simon apologises nevertheless.)
  
Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/bnq909vwgm

Rules: 
Fill the grid with the numbers 1-7 such that no number repeats in a row or column. The grid is completely covered by thermometer lines. You cannot see them because they are invisible. Nevertheless, numbers increase along thermometers starting from their bulb end. Thermometer lines move orthogonally and diagonally, and do not cross themselves or other thermometers, except at the white diamonds, where they must cross themselves or another thermometer. Thermometers do not pass through Xs. Thermometer bulbs do not touch each other, even diagonally. All thermometers have the same length.

You can find Delia's recipe for Chocolate Guinness Cake here (but remember: no walnuts and double the icing):
https://www.deliaonline.com/recipes/occasions/easter/easter-holidays-chocolate-recipes/chocolate-beer-cake

title: Great Snakes Alive!
description:
Here's where you can try Pentominophibian by Lil Gunga Jr: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/t4vu4ndtl3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw three snakes in the grid by connecting the yellow, green, and blue dots to their respective partner. Each snake is an orthogonally connected set of cells that doesn't branch, doesn't touch itself (even diagonally), and doesn't share cells with any other snake.
Digits in a gray square are even, and digits in a gray circle are odd. Cells containing a square or circle may not lie on any snake. Digits in a square or circle indicate how many of the surrounding (up to 8) cells belong to a snake. Digits separated by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio. Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive.
Divide each snake into contiguous groups of 5 cells, i.e., pentominoes, such that every cell along each snake belongs to exactly one pentomino. No two pentominoes in the entire grid may be of identical shape. Two pentominoes are considered identical shape if they can be mapped into each other by pure rotation (for example L and ꓶ). Pentominoes are considered different shapes if they require a reflection in order to be mapped into each other (for example L and ⅃), or cannot be mapped into each other at all (for example L and I).
One of the snake paths creates a Dutch whisper line, where adjacent digits along the line must differ by at least 4. One of the snake paths creates a palindrome, where digits read the same in both directions. One of the snake paths creates a renban line, where digits along the line create a set of consecutive digits without repeats, in any order. The solver must determine which snake is the Dutch whisper, palindrome, and renban line.

title: The Thermometer Sudoku Quest
description:
[Quick update: Simon's solve of TotallyNormalCat's Broken Secrets was released on the main channel this morning!]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A Chaos Construction is a sudoku in which the 3x3 areas are replaced by 9-cell regions which the solver must determine the shape of.  This example from Scojo is fabulous with a variety of different logic needed to tease out the geometry.  We've had over a dozen recommendations to try this one so do give a go!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/f2ajiy0h66

Rules: 
Place the digits 1-9 once each in every row, column, and 9 cell orthogonally connected region. The location of each region must be determined. Along a thermometer, digits must increase from bulb to tip. The digit in the bulb of a thermometer indicates how many thermometer bulbs contain that digit. Additionally, the digit in the bulb of a thermometer indicates how many times that thermometer crosses a border between regions. A digit in a square indicates how many cells in its region are on a thermometer. A V shape between two digits points to the lower digit.

You can watch us in the latest @numberphile  video here:

title: This Cat Is NOT "Totally Normal"!!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
We're continuing our series of incredibly long and difficult sudokus that have generated a lot of requests from viewers.  In this one, Simon tackles an old puzzle by TotallyNormalCat called Broken Secrets.  Although the video is slightly "shorter", it is worth emphasising that this is an incredibly clever puzzle.  Simon's method of tackling it is definitely a good way to solve this one.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/jMg44R2tpb

Rules:
When Simon was young, he used to hide his secrets in 9 cell cages. On his 45th birthday he decided to revisit his childhood toys and found out the cages broke! Help him put them together to reveal the secrets of the universe! Any resemblance to actual persons, living or dead, or actual events is purely intentional. 

Normal sudoku rules apply. There are 18 cages in the grid. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Each cage has exactly one partner such that, when combined together, they would form a valid 9-cell cage (ie containing no repeated digits). Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end. Cells with grey squares must contain even digits.

title: A Wonderful Portion of Ramen
description:
Here's where you can try Ramen by Nebuzaradan (yet again normal sudoku rules DO NOT apply!): https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/k4y2ak2rim 
Fill SOME cells of the grid with digits such that digits do not repeat within a row, column, or region, and each row, column, or region contains all digits 1 through N, where N is to be determined for each row, column, or region. On each purple line, the digits are consecutive (in any order) and do not repeat. On each blue line, digits on the line sum to the same value within each region the line passes through. The line is considered to pass through the region even if all the cells in the region are empty. Each clue line must pass through at least one digit. title: The Sudoku Tricks Of A Magic Square

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
After some really challenging sudokus this week, we can confirm that this lovely puzzle by Will Power is approachable and very fun! It's called Face Off At Center Ice and it's uses a magic square in the central 3x3 box (reminding us of Aad van de Wetering's tour de force from a few years ago (which remains to this day our most viewed video ever!))

Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10. Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5.

title: Stairway To  ̶H̶e̶a̶v̶e̶n̶  Eleven!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
The usual brilliance today from James Sinclair whose puzzle, Not Just Once, features an intriguing and beautiful stairway of eleven cages up the grid.  This is a genuinely surprising puzzle with lots of "Aha" moments. Well worth a few minutes of your precious sudoku time :)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/james-sinclair/not-just-once

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the indicated diagonal. Cages show their sums. Digits in cells separated by a white dot are consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (ie one digit is double the other).

You can watch us in the latest @numberphile  video here:

title: The Most Beautiful Sudoku In The World
description:
[Quick reminder that we are streaming Hexcells tonight at 10pm UK time!]

*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Wisteria Falls blows our minds tonight with a "sudoku" (can we call it that?) which disobeys some of the fundamental laws!!  In this puzzle you CAN repeat digits and you don't know which digits are used...  All of which adds up to a very long video (for which Simon obviously apologises) but boy is this a brilliant construction.

Play the puzzle at the following link:
https://sudokupad.app/w1n9shvh3t

(Please note that the rules below should be used as they are slightly clearer than those stated in the link.)

Rules: 
Solvers must determine a set of nine digits from 1 to 9 (inclusive), WHICH MAY INCLUDE REPEATS. Place one of these digits into each uncoloured cell such that every row and column with less than nine cells contains a subset of these nine digits and each marked region and 9-cell row/column contains all of these nine digits. Digits on an arrow sum to the digit in the connected circle. Squares contain even digits; and white dots separate consecutive digits. For clarity, the coloured cells are decorative and contain NO digits.

You can watch us in the latest @numberphile  video here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pezlnN4X52g

Simon's solve of TotallyNormalCat's Broken Secrets will appear on the main channel either tomorrow morning or Saturday morning.

title: A Great Introduction to Japanese Sums
description:
Here's where you can try Power Up! By TheAsylm: https://sudokupad.app/hMpJGmdHJ6 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Colors used in this puzzle are Black and Red. For best results, remove all unshaded marking you've done once complete. Japanese Sums rules: the squares outside the grid indicate the order of the contiguous runs of cells found in that row or column that must be shaded the color of the clue. The number inside the clue gives the sum of the cells in the run. There must be at least one unshaded cell between runs of the same color, but there is no need between runs of differing colors. All runs are given.
Power Up! (color-blind version): http://tinyurl.com/d8crx36n

title: Which Is The Best Cell In This Sudoku?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A really nice debut on the channel today for Nurator in the form of Odd Nebula, an approachable Fog Of War sudoku!  You'll need to think a bit about parity to sort this one out and see if you agree with Simon's nomination for "Cell Of The Day"!!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/86fQt7nfBQ

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In the grid is a “galaxy” ie an orthogonally-connected group of cells centred on the middle cell of the grid and rotationally symmetric by 180° around that cell.  Eg if r3c3 was in the galaxy then r7c7 must also be in the galaxy. The galaxy contains ALL of the cells containing odd digits but none of the cells containing even digits. Digits do not repeat in a cage and sum to the total given in the top left corner of the cage. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. The grid is covered in fog. Placing correct digits will clear the fog from the surrounding cells. No guessing is necessary.

You can watch us in the latest @numberphile  video here:

title: Maths Professor Loves Puzzle With No Maths!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
A debut on the channel tonight for Mennoo_ and their puzzle Low Cloud In A German City!  This was strongly recommended by Dorlir, the maths professor, and our testers loved it (with good reason!).

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/u2pnuvnrcy

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5. Each digit in the grid represents the height of a skyscraper located in that cell. Clues outside the grid indicate the number of visible skyscrapers from that direction, with taller skyscrapers blocking the view on smaller skyscrapers behind them. However, due to low hanging clouds in the city today, skyscrapers from 5 or lower are never visible for clues outside the grid. Therefore those clues can only see skyscrapers from 6 or higher.

title: Never Canter through an Orchard
description:
Here's where you can have a go at Orchard by Blobz: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/blobz/orchard 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains nine "Doubler Fruit", one in each row, column, and box. Each tree has exactly one doubler fruit, which is on one branch tip. Five other fruit are scattered around the orchard. Cells containing a doubler fruit count as double their digit value. Each digit from 1 through 9 is doubled exactly once. Along the grey "Thermo Tree" values must increase from the bulb end. Along the pink "Renban Tree" values form a non-repeating consecutive sequence. Along a blue "Region Sum Tree" values have an equal sum N within each box it passes through. Where the line passes through the same box more than once, each individual segment sums to N separately. Different lines may have different values for N. Values in cages sum to the given clue.

title: Imagine Having A Brain Like This...
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
There are some puzzles that just make us jealous of the brains of some of these sudoku constructors.  Exclusivity by zetamath is one such example.  If it was any more elegant this would be in a fashion show!

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/2sly4fnrqh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, no digit may appear more than once on a particular clue type. Type 1: Digits on a purple line form a set of non-repeating, consecutive digits in any order. Type 2: Along green lines, adjacent digits must differ by at least 5. Type 3: Digits separated by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio, meaning one is exactly double the other. Type 4: Digits along a grey thermometer must increase from the bulb end. Type 5: Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.

title: The Best Fog Of War Sudoku Puzzle Of Them All?
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
When Simon warned constructors not to even consider using negative numbers on Zipper Lines, gdc recognised a challenge!  This fusion of Zipper logic, Fog Of War sudoku, Yin Yang and negative numbers adds up to one of the very best Fog Of War sudokus ever.  The inventiveness and sheer beauty of this one are epic.

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/iql7m9a36u

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered in fog. Placing a correct digit will clear the fog from the surrounding cells. Values of the pair of cells with an equal distance to the circled centre of a lavender line sum to the value in that central cell. Shade some cells orange such that all shaded cells are orthogonally connected and all unshaded cells are orthogonally connected. No 2x2 area may be fully shaded or fully unshaded. The value of a shaded cell is its digit. The value of an unshaded cell is zero minus its digit (a negative number).

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pezlnN4X52g

title: Journey through the City of Sudoku Skyscrapers
description:
Here's where you can try City of Skyscrapers by Kitty Trouble: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/DdfLMG9fGf 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in killer cages cannot repeat. Each killer cage represents a skyscraper with a height equal to its sum. Digits outside cages do not have any skyscrapers. Clues outside the grid indicate how many skyscrapers it can see from that direction. For example, if there are 5 killer cages in a row or column, and their sums are 4, 10, 10, 13, and 5, leading away from a skyscraper clue, the skyscraper clue's value would be 3.

title: There Are Fractions In My Sudoku Cage Totals???!
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
An older sudoku today but one that definitely needs to be seen.  It was published back in September 2023 by sujoyku and still retains a 100% approval rating.  It's called Fraction Party and, yes, those cage totals do include some actual fractions!!  Don't let that put you off - it doesn't involve heavy maths but it is VERY fun to solve :)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/oepolnj5ur

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. All given cages are “divisor killer cages”. Digits in a divisor killer cage do not repeat. Each cage contains one divisor digit (which has to be determined by the solver). The clue in the top left indicates the value of the sum of all other digits in that cage divided by the divisor digit. Example: A 3-cell divisor killer cage containing the digits 1, 2 and 3 may have a valid clue of either 5=(2+3)/1, 2=(1+3)/2 or 1=(1+2)/3.

title: The Phistomefel Ring Sums To 109
description:
*** TODAY'S PUZZLE ***
Yesterday we showcased a "lost " puzzle by the incredible constructor Phistomefel. Today we feature a sudoku which invokes the name of the mighty Phisto in its ruleset!! It's by PotatoHead21 and is called Smoggy Knights and we LOVE it.  (It's also Fog Of War!!)

Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://sudokupad.app/HmmDgD66rH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is covered with fog. Placing a correct digit will clear the fog from the surrounding cells. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Cells separated by an X contain digits summing to 10. In cages digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. A cell with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. A cell with a grey square must contain an even digit.  Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in an 1:2 ratio (ie one digit will be double the other). The ring of 16 cells on the outside of the central 3x3 box (ie touching it either orthogonally or diagonally) – sometimes called the “Phistomefel Ring” – contains digits summing to 109.
